chapters.title: Unit 1: Prophet Muhammad the Model of Tolerance

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary

  • Q: Define 'compassion'.
    Ans: A strong feeling of sympathy for people who are suffering and a desire to help them.
  • Q: Define 'debt'.
    Ans: A sum of money that somebody owes.
  • Q: Define 'epitome'.
    Ans: A perfect example of something.
  • Q: Define 'dreadful'.
    Ans: Very bad or unpleasant.
  • Q: Define 'restraining'.
    Ans: To stop somebody or something from doing something.
  • Q: Define 'amnesty'.
    Ans: A period of time during which people can admit to a crime or give up weapons without being punished.
  • Q: Define 'counselling'.
    Ans: Professional advice about a problem.
  • Q: Define 'perseverance'.
    Ans: The quality of continuing to try to achieve a particular aim despite difficulties.
  • Q: Define 'debate'.
    Ans: A formal discussion on an issue at a public meeting. In a debate two or more speakers express opposing views.
  • Q: Define 'precedence'.
    Ans: The condition of being more important than somebody else and therefore coming or being dealt with first.
  • Q: Define 'adversity'.
    Ans: A difficult or unpleasant situation.
  • Q: Define 'renounced'.
    Ans: To state publicly that you no longer have a particular belief or that you will no longer behave in a particular way.
  • Q: Define 'testified'.
    Ans: To say that you believe something is true because you have evidence of it.
  • Q: Define 'Rabbi'.
    Ans: A Jewish religious scholar.
  • Q: Define 'ostracised'.
    Ans: To refuse to let somebody be a member of a social group; to refuse to meet or talk to somebody.
  • Q: Define 'opponent'.
    Ans: A person that you are playing or fighting against in a game, competition, argument, etc.
  • Q: Define 'scarcity'.
    Ans: If there is a scarcity of something, there is not enough of it and it is difficult to obtain it.
  • Q: Define 'gracious'.
    Ans: Kind, polite and generous, especially to somebody of a lower social position.
  • Q: Define 'revenge'.
    Ans: Something that you do in order to make somebody suffer because they have made you suffer.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What does the Quran say about tolerance?
    Ans: The Holy Quran teaches believers to seek help through patience and prayer, and it assures them that Allah is with the patient (Al-Baqarah 2:153). It also describes Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) as Rahmatul-lil-Alameen, a mercy unto the whole mankind and the universe. The Quran further promises that those who are patient will be given their reward without measure.
  • Q: Q2. The Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) was a man of extraordinary endurance. Explain.
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) showed extraordinary endurance throughout his life. When the Quraish ostracised him and his family, Banu Hashim, in the valley of Shab-Abi-Talib, he endured three years of scarcity of food and water with no means of income, yet he remained calm and tolerant and never thought of revenge. He also bore harsh treatment, such as that of Rabbi Zaid, with patience and repaid it with kindness.
  • Q: Q3. How did Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) treat the people of Makkah after victory?
    Ans: After the conquest of Makkah, the Muslim army entered the city humbly and peacefully. No house was robbed and no man or woman was insulted. Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) granted a general amnesty to the entire population of Makkah and forgave even his worst enemies, including Abu Sufyan and his wife, instead of taking revenge.
  • Q: Q4. Why was the Rabbi asking for the repayment days before the loan was due?
    Ans: The Rabbi, Zaid ibn Sanah, was asking for the repayment days before the loan was due because he wanted to test the tolerance of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him). He deliberately behaved harshly to see whether tolerance and perseverance would take precedence over anger in the Prophet's conduct.
  • Q: Q5. What does the tolerance of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) teach us?
    Ans: His tolerance teaches us to remain calm and patient in the face of adversity and to answer harsh treatment with kindness instead of anger or revenge. It teaches us to forgive even our enemies and to treat all people with compassion. It also shows that tolerance can win hearts, as it won the heart of Rabbi Zaid.
  • Q: Q6. What was the effect of the kindness of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) on the Rabbi?
    Ans: The Rabbi Zaid found that tolerance and perseverance took precedence over anger and that his harsh treatment was repaid with kindness, as he was given his loan back with twenty Sa'a of dates extra. He was so moved that he immediately renounced his religion and testified before Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) that there is none worthy of worship but Allah alone and that Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) is His Messenger.
  • Q: Q7. What is the main idea of the lesson?
    Ans: The main idea of the lesson is that Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the perfect model of tolerance, forgiveness, patience and compassion for all mankind. Through examples such as the boycott at Shab-Abi-Talib, the general amnesty at the conquest of Makkah and the incident of Rabbi Zaid, the lesson shows that he never took revenge and always answered harshness with kindness.

Comprehension B — Choose the correct answer

  • Q: Q1. Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) said to Hazrat Umar, 'Go and repay him his loan, and give him twenty Sa'a extra.' In this sentence 'him' refers to ______.
    Options: Rabbi Zaid / Abu Sufyan / Hazrat Umar / Hazrat Usman
    Ans: Rabbi Zaid
  • Q: Q2. The tolerance of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) knew no bounds. In this sentence the phrase 'knew no bounds' means ______.
    Options: his tolerance was immeasurable for Muslims / his tolerance was not confined to Muslims only / his tolerance was restricted to Muslims only / his tolerance was confined to Muslims
    Ans: his tolerance was not confined to Muslims only
  • Q: Q3. Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'A Muslim is he from whose hand and tongue the Muslims are safe'. This hadith means ______.
    Options: a true Muslim does not hurt Muslims physically and emotionally / a true Muslim does not bad mouth or curse anybody / a true Muslim does not beat or injure anybody with his hands / a true Muslim does not trouble anybody mentally
    Ans: a true Muslim does not hurt Muslims physically and emotionally
  • Q: Q4. Truly, he is an epitome of tolerance, forgiveness, patience and compassion. The word 'epitome' in this sentence means ______.
    Options: essence / embodiment / contrary / example
    Ans: example
  • Q: Q5. Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) granted a general amnesty to the entire population of Makkah. The word 'amnesty' in this sentence means ______.
    Options: patience / forgiveness / tolerance / acceptance
    Ans: forgiveness

mcqs.q: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) said to Hazrat Umar, 'Go and repay him his loan, and give him twenty Sa'a extra.' In this sentence 'him' refers to ______.
options: Abu Sufyan
Hazrat Umar
Rabbi Zaid
Hazrat Usman
mcqs.why: The loan belonged to Rabbi Zaid, who had demanded repayment early, so the Prophet ordered Hazrat Umar to repay Zaid and give him extra dates.

mcqs.q: The tolerance of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) knew no bounds. In this sentence the phrase 'knew no bounds' means ______.
options: his tolerance was not confined to Muslims only
his tolerance was restricted to Muslims only
his tolerance was confined to Muslims
his tolerance was immeasurable for Muslims
mcqs.why: The lesson stresses that his tolerance extended beyond Muslims to all people, including Rabbi Zaid and the people of Makkah, so it was not confined to Muslims only.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'A Muslim is he from whose hand and tongue the Muslims are safe'. This hadith means ______.
options: a true Muslim does not bad mouth or curse anybody
a true Muslim does not beat or injure anybody with his hands
a true Muslim does not hurt Muslims physically and emotionally
a true Muslim does not trouble anybody mentally
mcqs.why: Hand stands for physical harm and tongue for emotional harm through words, so together the hadith means a true Muslim hurts others neither physically nor emotionally.

mcqs.q: Truly, he is an epitome of tolerance, forgiveness, patience and compassion. The word 'epitome' in this sentence means ______.
options: essence
contrary
embodiment
example
mcqs.why: The glossary defines epitome as a perfect example of something, and the lesson presents the Prophet as the perfect example of tolerance and compassion.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) granted a general amnesty to the entire population of Makkah. The word 'amnesty' in this sentence means ______.
options: patience
tolerance
forgiveness
acceptance
mcqs.why: At the conquest of Makkah he forgave the entire population instead of punishing them, so amnesty here means a general forgiveness for past offences.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, what does the Holy Quran assure believers in Al-Baqarah 2:153?
options: That the patient will be given wealth without measure
That Allah is with the patient who seek help through patience and prayer
That believers should take revenge on their enemies
That prayer removes the need for patience
mcqs.why: The solved answer states that the Quran teaches believers to seek help through patience and prayer and assures them that Allah is with the patient.

mcqs.q: How long did the boycott of Banu Hashim in the valley of Shab-Abi-Talib last?
options: One year
Two years
Five years
Three years
mcqs.why: The lesson says he endured three years of scarcity of food and water in Shab-Abi-Talib with no means of income, yet remained calm and never thought of revenge.

mcqs.q: What happened when the Muslim army entered Makkah after the conquest?
options: No house was robbed and no man or woman was insulted
Every house was searched for weapons
The worst enemies were punished at once
The people of Makkah were forced to leave the city
mcqs.why: The solved answer says the army entered humbly and peacefully, no house was robbed and no man or woman was insulted, and a general amnesty was granted.

mcqs.q: Why did Rabbi Zaid demand repayment of the loan days before it was due?
options: Because he urgently needed the money for trade
Because he wanted to test the tolerance of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)
Because the loan period had already ended
Because Hazrat Umar had asked him to do so
mcqs.why: Rabbi Zaid deliberately behaved harshly before the due date to test whether tolerance and perseverance would take precedence over anger in the Prophet.

mcqs.q: What extra amount was given to Rabbi Zaid along with the repayment of his loan?
options: Ten Sa'a of dates
Twenty Sa'a of wheat
Twenty Sa'a of dates
Thirty Sa'a of dates
mcqs.why: The Prophet ordered that the loan be repaid with twenty Sa'a of dates extra, and this kindness moved Rabbi Zaid to accept Islam.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Dictionary meanings and parts of speech

  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'frightened'.
    Ans: Meaning: feeling fear; afraid and worried. Part of speech: Adjective (abbreviation: adj.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'harsh'.
    Ans: Meaning: rough, severe and unkind; cruel in manner or words. Part of speech: Adjective (abbreviation: adj.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'tolerance'.
    Ans: Meaning: the ability or willingness to endure opinions or behaviour that one dislikes or disagrees with. Part of speech: Noun (abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'convey'.
    Ans: Meaning: to communicate or make known; to transport or carry. Part of speech: Verb (abbreviation: v.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'violence'.
    Ans: Meaning: physical force intended to hurt, damage or kill somebody or something. Part of speech: Noun (abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'reward'.
    Ans: Meaning: something given to somebody in return for good work, a service or an achievement. Part of speech: Noun (abbreviation: n.); it is also used as a Verb.
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'honesty'.
    Ans: Meaning: the quality of being honest, truthful and free from deceit. Part of speech: Noun (abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'insult'.
    Ans: Meaning: a rude remark or action that offends somebody. Part of speech: Noun (abbreviation: n.); it is also used as a Verb, meaning to say or do something rude and offensive.

Vocabulary B — Synonyms

  • Q: Give a synonym of 'truth'.
    Ans: Fact; reality.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'rude'.
    Ans: Impolite; ill-mannered.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'sincere'.
    Ans: Honest; genuine.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'fear'.
    Ans: Fright; dread.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'kindness'.
    Ans: Compassion; generosity.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'forgive'.
    Ans: Pardon; excuse.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'argument'.
    Ans: Debate; dispute.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'swell'.
    Ans: Expand; bulge; grow larger.

Grammar A — Change the sentences from singular to plural or from plural to singular

  • Q: Change into plural: 'A book is a good friend.'
    Ans: Books are good friends.
  • Q: Change into plural: 'A small car is a great vehicle.'
    Ans: Small cars are great vehicles.
  • Q: Change into singular: 'Are the students in the classrooms?'
    Ans: Is the student in the classroom?
  • Q: Change into singular: 'These glasses aren't for those women to wear.'
    Ans: This glass isn't for that woman to wear. Note: 'glasses' here means drinking glasses; if spectacles are meant, the singular is 'This pair of glasses isn't for that woman to wear.'
  • Q: Change into plural: 'The brush is under the chair.'
    Ans: The brushes are under the chairs.

Grammar B — Concrete or abstract nouns

  • Q: Identify whether 'love' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Abstract noun.
  • Q: Identify whether 'book' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Concrete noun.
  • Q: Identify whether 'girl' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Concrete noun.
  • Q: Identify whether 'intelligence' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Abstract noun.
  • Q: Identify whether 'mouse' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Concrete noun.
  • Q: Identify whether 'loyalty' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Abstract noun.
  • Q: Identify whether 'laptop' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Concrete noun.
  • Q: Identify whether 'peace' is a concrete or abstract noun.
    Ans: Abstract noun.

Grammar C — Countable or uncountable nouns, with sentences

  • Q: Identify whether 'coffee' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Uncountable noun. Sentence: I drink a cup of coffee every morning.
  • Q: Identify whether 'tea' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Uncountable noun. Sentence: She poured some hot tea into the cup.
  • Q: Identify whether 'boy' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Countable noun. Sentence: Three boys are playing in the park.
  • Q: Identify whether 'soap' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Uncountable noun. Sentence: Wash your hands with soap before eating.
  • Q: Identify whether 'table' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Countable noun. Sentence: There are two tables in our classroom.
  • Q: Identify whether 'car' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Countable noun. Sentence: My uncle has bought a new car.
  • Q: Identify whether 'honey' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Uncountable noun. Sentence: Honey is sweet and good for health.
  • Q: Identify whether 'keyboard' is countable or uncountable, and use it in a sentence.
    Ans: Countable noun. Sentence: This computer has a new keyboard.

Grammar D — Fill in the blanks with a noun (chairs, information, hair, luggage, furniture)

  • Q: I don't have much ____, it's just two small bags.
    Ans: luggage
  • Q: They are going to tell you all you want to know. They are going to give you a lot of ____.
    Ans: information
  • Q: There is room for everybody to sit down. There are a lot of ____.
    Ans: chairs
  • Q: We have no ____, not even a bed or a table.
    Ans: furniture
  • Q: 'What does Arif look like?' He's got a long beard and very short ____.
    Ans: hair

Grammar E — Complete the sentences with collective nouns (flock, herd, swarm, bouquet, gang)

  • Q: A ____ of locusts attacked the crops.
    Ans: swarm
  • Q: A ____ of birds is always a beautiful sight.
    Ans: flock
  • Q: They welcomed the chief guest with a ____ of flowers.
    Ans: bouquet
  • Q: As we drove down the countryside, we saw a ____ of sheep grazing in the fields.
    Ans: herd
  • Q: The ____ of thieves has been arrested by the police.
    Ans: gang

Grammar — Nouns that change meaning in the plural form (Activity: use the words in sentences)

  • Q: Use 'arm' (part of body) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: He broke his left arm while playing cricket.
  • Q: Use 'arms' (weapons) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: The soldiers laid down their arms and surrendered.
  • Q: Use 'glass' (a drinking container) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Please give me a glass of water.
  • Q: Use 'glasses' (glasses for eyes) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: My grandfather wears glasses for reading.
  • Q: Use 'content' (in a state of peaceful state of mind) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: After finishing his work, he sat content under the tree.
  • Q: Use 'contents' (the things that are included in something) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: The contents of the parcel were checked carefully.
  • Q: Use 'spectacle' (a visually striking performance) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: The fireworks were a grand spectacle to watch.
  • Q: Use 'spectacles' (a pair of glasses) in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: She cleaned her spectacles with a soft cloth.

Grammar G — Pick out noun phrases from the sentences

  • Q: Pick out the noun phrase in: 'I expect our team to win.'
    Ans: Our team.
  • Q: Pick out the noun phrase in: 'Do you know his age?'
    Ans: His age.
  • Q: Pick out the noun phrase in: 'Your coming poses a problem for us.'
    Ans: A problem (the phrase 'your coming' also functions as a noun phrase, the subject of the sentence).
  • Q: Pick out the noun phrase in: 'His parents hoped for his success.'
    Ans: His parents (and 'his success' is also a noun phrase).
  • Q: Pick out the noun phrase in: 'She would not admit her guilt.'
    Ans: Her guilt.

mcqs.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'tolerance'?
options: Adjective
Noun
Verb
Adverb
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise gives tolerance as a noun meaning the ability or willingness to endure opinions or behaviour that one dislikes or disagrees with.

mcqs.q: Which word is a synonym of 'forgive'?
options: Debate
Pardon
Dread
Expand
mcqs.why: The synonyms exercise lists pardon and excuse as synonyms of forgive, while debate belongs to argument and dread belongs to fear.

mcqs.q: Which word is a synonym of 'rude'?
options: Genuine
Honest
Impolite
Compassion
mcqs.why: The synonyms exercise gives impolite and ill-mannered as synonyms of rude, which describes rough, severe and unkind behaviour in manner or words.

mcqs.q: The noun 'love' is an example of which kind of noun?
options: Concrete noun
Abstract noun
Collective noun
Proper noun
mcqs.why: Love names a feeling that cannot be seen or touched, so the grammar exercise classifies love as an abstract noun, unlike book or girl.

mcqs.q: The noun 'coffee' is an example of which kind of noun?
options: Countable noun
Proper noun
Uncountable noun
Collective noun
mcqs.why: The exercise classifies coffee as uncountable and uses it in the sentence I drink a cup of coffee every morning, counting the cups rather than the coffee.

mcqs.q: What is the correct plural form of 'A book is a good friend.'?
options: Books is good friends.
A books are good friend.
Book are a good friends.
Books are good friends.
mcqs.why: In the plural, a book becomes books, is becomes are, and friend becomes friends, giving the correct sentence Books are good friends.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence with the correct collective noun: 'A ____ of locusts attacked the crops.'
options: swarm
flock
herd
bouquet
mcqs.why: The collective nouns exercise uses swarm for locusts, while flock is used for birds, herd for sheep and bouquet for flowers.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence with the correct collective noun: 'A ____ of birds is always a beautiful sight.'
options: gang
bouquet
flock
swarm
mcqs.why: The exercise pairs birds with flock, so a flock of birds is the correct collective noun phrase in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct noun: 'I don't have much ____, it's just two small bags.'
options: information
chairs
furniture
luggage
mcqs.why: Bags carried while travelling are called luggage, an uncountable noun, so much luggage correctly completes the sentence about two small bags.

mcqs.q: In which sentence does 'arms' mean weapons?
options: He broke his left arm while playing cricket.
The soldiers laid down their arms and surrendered.
Please give me a glass of water.
She cleaned her spectacles with a soft cloth.
mcqs.why: The activity explains that arm means a part of the body, while arms in the plural means weapons, as in soldiers laying down their arms and surrendering.

mcqs.q: What is the noun phrase in the sentence 'I expect our team to win.'?
options: To win
Our team
I expect
Win the match
mcqs.why: The grammar exercise identifies our team as the noun phrase because it is a group of words built around the noun team and acts as the object.

mcqs.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'convey'?
options: Noun
Adjective
Verb
Adverb
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise gives convey as a verb meaning to communicate or make known, and also to transport or carry something.

mcqs.q: The noun 'intelligence' is an example of which kind of noun?
options: Abstract noun
Concrete noun
Countable noun
Collective noun
mcqs.why: Intelligence names a quality of the mind that cannot be touched or seen, so the exercise classifies it as an abstract noun like loyalty and peace.

mcqs.q: The noun 'keyboard' is an example of which kind of noun?
options: Uncountable noun
Abstract noun
Countable noun
Collective noun
mcqs.why: A keyboard is a separate object that can be counted, and the exercise uses it in the sentence This computer has a new keyboard, so it is countable.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct noun: 'We have no ____, not even a bed or a table.'
options: hair
information
luggage
furniture
mcqs.why: Beds and tables are items of furniture, an uncountable noun, so We have no furniture correctly completes the sentence in the exercise.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: A. Write a paragraph on the 'Patience of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)' using specific words, vivid verbs, modifiers etc. Use appropriate supporting details and transitional devices.
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the finest model of patience for the whole world. First, during the three long years of boycott at Shab-Abi-Talib, he silently endured hunger, thirst and social rejection, yet he never cursed his persecutors. Moreover, when Rabbi Zaid rudely grabbed him by the edges of his cloak and demanded his loan before time, he smiled calmly, restrained Hazrat Umar, and ordered that the man be repaid with twenty Sa'a of dates extra. Similarly, at the conquest of Makkah he forgave the very people who had tormented him for years. Thus, his patience was not weakness but a powerful strength that melted the hardest hearts and turned enemies into believers.
  • Q: B. Analyse the first paragraph in the text to identify the theme.
    Ans: The first paragraph of the text defines tolerance as a fair and objective attitude towards those whose lifestyle differs from ours, and as the virtue that enables a person to forbear negative remarks and actions with patience and calmness. Its theme is that tolerance, forgiveness, patience and compassion are the central qualities of the life of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him). The paragraph supports this theme by stating that it was his tolerance that let him forgive his worst enemies, and that the Holy Quran describes him as Rahmatul-lil-Alameen, a mercy unto the whole mankind and the universe.
  • Q: C. Discuss tolerance with reference to the current world scenario. Write a paragraph of at least 100 words.
    Ans: Tolerance is badly needed in the current world, where people of different religions, cultures and opinions often fail to live together in peace. Intolerance gives birth to hatred, aggression, hasty reactions and violence, and it divides families, societies and even nations. On the other hand, tolerance creates an atmosphere in which everyone can live safely and practise his own way of life without fear. If we follow the example of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him), who forgave his worst enemies and answered harshness with kindness, we can settle our differences through patience and dialogue instead of fighting. In short, tolerance is one of the surest paths to peace, happiness and the pleasure of Allah in the modern world.
  • Q: D. Write down the summary of the lesson 'Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) the Model of Tolerance'.
    Ans: Tolerance means bearing the opinions, remarks and actions of others with patience and calmness, and Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) is its perfect example. During the three-year boycott at Shab-Abi-Talib he endured hunger and hardship without thinking of revenge. At the conquest of Makkah he entered the city peacefully, granted a general amnesty to all its people and forgave even Abu Sufyan and his wife. When Rabbi Zaid harshly demanded his loan before it was due, the Prophet repaid him with twenty Sa'a extra, and this kindness led the Rabbi to embrace Islam. His tolerance knew no bounds, and he always showed kindness in the face of harsh treatment.
  • Q: E. Translate the following passage from English into Urdu: 'Tolerance means the ability or willingness to endure the existence of opinions or behaviour that one dislikes or disagrees with...'
    Ans: Note: This exercise requires translation into Urdu; translations are not reproduced in these English-only solved notes.

mcqs.q: According to the model paragraph on patience, how long did the boycott at Shab-Abi-Talib last?
options: Three long years
One long year
Two long years
Seven long years
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says that during the three long years of boycott at Shab-Abi-Talib he silently endured hunger, thirst and social rejection.

mcqs.q: According to the model paragraph, what did the Prophet do when Rabbi Zaid grabbed him by the edges of his cloak?
options: He ordered Hazrat Umar to punish the Rabbi
He smiled calmly, restrained Hazrat Umar, and ordered repayment with twenty Sa'a of dates extra
He demanded the loan be cancelled
He left the place in anger
mcqs.why: The paragraph states that he smiled calmly, restrained Hazrat Umar, and ordered repayment with twenty Sa'a of dates extra despite the rude demand.

mcqs.q: Which transitional device introduces the second example in the model paragraph on patience?
options: Similarly
Thus
Moreover
First
mcqs.why: The paragraph uses First for the boycott, Moreover for the Rabbi Zaid incident, Similarly for Makkah, and Thus for the concluding statement.

mcqs.q: What is the theme identified in the analysis of the first paragraph of the text?
options: That tolerance should be shown only to Muslims
That debate is the best way to settle disputes
That wealth and power bring lasting peace
That tolerance, forgiveness, patience and compassion are the central qualities of the life of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him)
mcqs.why: The analysis says the theme is that tolerance, forgiveness, patience and compassion are the central qualities of his life, supported by the title Rahmatul-lil-Alameen.

mcqs.q: According to the analysis, how does the first paragraph define tolerance?
options: As a period when people can give up weapons without punishment
As a fair and objective attitude towards those whose lifestyle differs from ours
As professional advice about a problem
As the quality of continuing despite difficulties
mcqs.why: The analysis states that the first paragraph defines tolerance as a fair and objective attitude towards those whose lifestyle differs from ours.

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph on tolerance in the current world, intolerance gives birth to what?
options: Patience and dialogue
Peace and happiness
Hatred, aggression, hasty reactions and violence
Safety and freedom
mcqs.why: The paragraph says intolerance gives birth to hatred, aggression, hasty reactions and violence, and divides families, societies and even nations.

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph on tolerance in the current world, what does tolerance create?
options: An atmosphere in which everyone can live safely and practise his own way of life without fear
A reason to avoid people of other cultures
A need to answer harshness with harshness
A division between families and nations
mcqs.why: The paragraph contrasts intolerance with tolerance, which creates an atmosphere where everyone can live safely and practise his own way of life without fear.

mcqs.q: According to the summary of the lesson, whom did the Prophet forgive at the conquest of Makkah?
options: Only the members of Banu Hashim
Only Rabbi Zaid
No one, because he took revenge
Even Abu Sufyan and his wife, along with the entire population
mcqs.why: The summary says he granted a general amnesty to all the people of Makkah and forgave even Abu Sufyan and his wife instead of taking revenge.

mcqs.q: How does the summary of the lesson describe his tolerance at the end?
options: His tolerance was limited to times of peace
His tolerance knew no bounds, and he always showed kindness in the face of harsh treatment
His tolerance ended after the conquest of Makkah
His tolerance depended on the behaviour of others
mcqs.why: The summary closes by saying his tolerance knew no bounds and he always showed kindness in the face of harsh treatment, as shown in every incident.

mcqs.q: What conclusion does the model paragraph on patience draw about his patience?
options: It was a sign of weakness in difficult times
It lasted only during the boycott years
It was not weakness but a powerful strength that melted the hardest hearts and turned enemies into believers
It was useful only for settling debts
mcqs.why: The paragraph concludes Thus, his patience was not weakness but a powerful strength that melted the hardest hearts and turned enemies into believers.

Listening and Speaking

  • Q: Listening and Speaking — Share with the class an act of tolerance you have performed recently.
    Ans: This is an oral classroom activity with no written answer.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-Reading

  • Q: Q1. Iqbal wants to see the qualities of an eagle (shaheen) in his young nation. What are the qualities of an eagle that make it superior to other birds?
    Ans: The eagle, or shaheen, flies higher than other birds and hunts its own prey instead of eating what others have killed. It has sharp eyesight, great courage and complete independence, and it never makes a low nest or settles in one place for long. It is always restless for a higher flight, which is why Iqbal chose it as the symbol of the ideal youth.

Glossary

  • Q: Define 'exploration'.
    Ans: The act of travelling through a place in order to find out something about it or look for something in it.
  • Q: Define 'innovation'.
    Ans: The introduction of new things, ideas or ways of doing something.
  • Q: Define 'invention'.
    Ans: The ability to have new and interesting ideas.
  • Q: Define 'Hamlet'.
    Ans: A character from a Shakespearean play who would take too much time in thinking before taking an action.
  • Q: Define 'perpetual'.
    Ans: Continuing for a long period of time without interruption.
  • Q: Define 'foresight'.
    Ans: The ability to predict what is likely to happen and to use this to prepare for the future.
  • Q: Define 'enthusiastic'.
    Ans: Feeling or showing a lot of excitement and interest about somebody or something.
  • Q: Define 'emperor'.
    Ans: The ruler of an empire.
  • Q: Define 'thy'.
    Ans: An English word that means 'your'.
  • Q: Define 'forge'.
    Ans: To put a lot of effort into making something successful or strong so that it will last.
  • Q: Define 'brilliance'.
    Ans: Intense brightness of light; exceptional talent or intelligence.
  • Q: Define 'nova'.
    Ans: A star showing a sudden large increase in brightness and then suddenly returning to its original state.
  • Q: Define 'inspiration'.
    Ans: A sudden brilliant or timely idea.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. How is the youth the standard bearer of a nation?
    Ans: The young generation is the standard bearer of any nation because the future of the nation rests on its shoulders. If the energy of the youth is channelised in the proper direction, it can bring a sea change in the social, political and economic fabric of the nation. For this reason Iqbal focused on the creative energy of the youth in his poetry.
  • Q: Q2. According to Iqbal, how can the youth change themselves?
    Ans: According to Iqbal, the youth can change themselves by knowing themselves, that is, by developing Khudi, for absolute Khudi is infinitely creative and 'Know thyself and success shall be thine'. They must become strong believers in Ishq, the creative and dynamic energy of perpetual struggle, and like the shaheen keep flying higher and deeper in search of new worlds. A young man who becomes emperor of himself can then lead the world in his own direction.
  • Q: Q3. Read the 3rd paragraph and write down the key idea.
    Ans: The key idea of the third paragraph of the lesson is that Iqbal's youth is never contented with what he has created or invented. The spirit of Ishq, another name for perpetual struggle, spurs him to go beyond the star that he has discovered with his foresight. His motive is to pursue his intellectual and spiritual goals and then continue his journey beyond those goals.
  • Q: Q4. What is the main idea of the lesson?
    Ans: The main idea of the lesson is that youth was the main focus of Iqbal and the symbol of hope and the future of the nation. Iqbal wants the youth to become Mard-e-Momin, Mujahid and Shaheen, men of Khudi and Ishq, who are dynamic, creative and men of action, so that they can lead the Muslim Ummah to self-sufficiency, independence and progress.
  • Q: Q5. According to Iqbal, the youth shouldn't confine to material achievement. Express your view on this statement.
    Ans: I agree with this view of Iqbal. The life of his youth is dynamic and is not confined to limited material achievement and the enjoyment of it; instead, he enjoys the creative journey of exploration, discovery, inventions and innovations. Material gains alone cannot give lasting honour or happiness to a person or a nation. A youth who aims only at wealth stops growing, while a youth who pursues intellectual and spiritual goals keeps rising from one star to a new nova of brilliance and inspiration.

Comprehension B — Choose the correct answer

  • Q: Q1. His sublime poetry and philosophy inspired millions of Muslims. The opposite of the word 'sublime' in this sentence means ______.
    Options: beautiful / inspiring / uplifting / irrational
    Ans: irrational
  • Q: Q2. Whether he is in the battlefield or in the company of friend, he is pure in head and heart. In this sentence 'he' refers to ______.
    Options: the youth / Iqbal / shaheen / the author
    Ans: the youth
  • Q: Q3. 'Know thyself and success shall be thine' means that ______.
    Options: your desire to know who others are and what they want is the real success in life / your desire to know your nation and what they want is the real success in life / your desire to know who you are and what you want is the real success in life / your desire to know the worldly needs and to achieve them is the real success in life
    Ans: your desire to know who you are and what you want is the real success in life
  • Q: Q4. The youth of Iqbal is not a thinking Hamlet but a man of action. In this sentence 'Hamlet' symbolises a person who ______.
    Options: is taking prompt action / is talking too much / is taking quick decision / is taking too much time in making decision
    Ans: is taking too much time in making decision

mcqs.q: His sublime poetry and philosophy inspired millions of Muslims. The opposite of the word 'sublime' in this sentence means ______.
options: beautiful
irrational
inspiring
uplifting
mcqs.why: Beautiful, inspiring and uplifting are close in spirit to sublime, while irrational is unrelated to its elevated sense and is the book's keyed opposite here.

mcqs.q: Whether he is in the battlefield or in the company of friend, he is pure in head and heart. In this sentence 'he' refers to ______.
options: Iqbal
shaheen
the youth
the author
mcqs.why: The sentence describes Iqbal's ideal young man, who stays pure in head and heart both on the battlefield and among friends, so he refers to the youth.

mcqs.q: 'Know thyself and success shall be thine' means that ______.
options: your desire to know who others are and what they want is the real success in life
your desire to know your nation and what they want is the real success in life
your desire to know the worldly needs and to achieve them is the real success in life
your desire to know who you are and what you want is the real success in life
mcqs.why: Thyself means yourself, so the saying teaches self-knowledge through Khudi: knowing who you are and what you want is the real success in life.

mcqs.q: The youth of Iqbal is not a thinking Hamlet but a man of action. In this sentence 'Hamlet' symbolises a person who ______.
options: is taking too much time in making decision
is taking prompt action
is talking too much
is taking quick decision
mcqs.why: The glossary describes Hamlet as a character who takes too much time thinking before acting, the opposite of Iqbal's youth who is a man of action.

mcqs.q: Which quality of the eagle (shaheen) is stated in the pre-reading answer?
options: It makes a low nest and settles in one place
It hunts its own prey instead of eating what others have killed
It flies lower than other birds
It depends on others for its food
mcqs.why: The pre-reading answer says the shaheen flies higher than other birds and hunts its own prey instead of eating what others have killed, showing independence.

mcqs.q: Why is the youth called the standard bearer of a nation?
options: Because the youth carry flags in national ceremonies
Because the youth are the largest part of the population
Because the future of the nation rests on its shoulders
Because the youth follow the older generation in everything
mcqs.why: The answer explains that the young generation is the standard bearer because the future of the nation rests on its shoulders and its energy can bring a sea change.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, what is Ishq in Iqbal's thought?
options: A name for material success and enjoyment
The creative and dynamic energy of perpetual struggle
A reason to rest after achieving a goal
The ability to predict the future
mcqs.why: The lesson calls Ishq another name for perpetual struggle, the creative and dynamic energy that spurs youth to go beyond every star they discover.

mcqs.q: What does the old English word 'thy' mean?
options: My
His
Your
Their
mcqs.why: The glossary defines thy as an English word that means your, as in the saying Know thyself and success shall be thine.

mcqs.q: What is 'foresight' according to the glossary?
options: Intense brightness of light
A star showing a sudden increase in brightness
A sudden brilliant or timely idea
The ability to predict what is likely to happen and to use this to prepare for the future
mcqs.why: The glossary defines foresight as the ability to predict what is likely to happen and to use this to prepare for the future, unlike nova or inspiration.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the lesson 'Iqbal's Message to Youth'?
options: Youth was the main focus of Iqbal and the symbol of hope and the future of the nation
Youth should confine themselves to material achievement
Youth should think for a long time before every action
Youth should settle in one place like other birds
mcqs.why: The main idea answer states that youth was the main focus of Iqbal and the symbol of hope and future, called to become Mard-e-Momin, Mujahid and Shaheen.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — Use the following words in sentences of your own

  • Q: Use 'nation' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Our nation can progress only when its youth work hard with honesty.
  • Q: Use 'battlefield' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Many brave soldiers sacrificed their lives on the battlefield for their country.
  • Q: Use 'determination' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: With firm determination, she completed her studies despite many difficulties.
  • Q: Use 'symbol' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: The shaheen is a symbol of courage, freedom and high ambition.
  • Q: Use 'motive' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: His only motive behind helping the poor was to please Allah.
  • Q: Use 'confined' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Success cannot be confined to wealth alone; it also means knowledge and character.
  • Q: Use 'direction' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Good teachers give the right direction to the energy of the youth.
  • Q: Use 'goals' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Every student should set clear goals and struggle hard to achieve them.

Vocabulary A — Complete the sentences with the correct prefix (dis-, in-, mis-, re-, un-)

  • Q: I just can't believe it! The story is ____believable!
    Ans: un- (unbelievable)
  • Q: No, that answer is ____correct. It is wrong.
    Ans: in- (incorrect)
  • Q: Let's look at this information again. We should ____view it before the test.
    Ans: re- (review)
  • Q: I saw Alina just a moment ago, but now I can't find her! She just ____appeared!
    Ans: dis- (disappeared)
  • Q: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't hear you correctly. I ____understood you.
    Ans: mis- (misunderstood)

Vocabulary B — Complete the words by using the suffixes from the list (-ness, -able, -ment, -ful, -less)

  • Q: Fazila can't stay still. She always wants to move! She is rest____.
    Ans: -less (restless)
  • Q: Rashida is very intelligent! She's ador____!
    Ans: -able (adorable)
  • Q: Maleeha can't remember anything! She's very forget____!
    Ans: -ful (forgetful)
  • Q: I appreciate your great attitude. I am really thank____.
    Ans: -ful (thankful)
  • Q: The best thing about her is her kind____.
    Ans: -ness (kindness)

Grammar A — Pronouns: choose the appropriate options to complete the sentences

  • Q: Q1. We all told the boss that we wanted to have our salaries paid in advance but he just ignored ______.
    Options: us / we / our / his
    Ans: us
  • Q: Q2. When the man asked me how I had got his address, I told him that I was given it by a relative of ______.
    Options: me / his / he / him
    Ans: his
  • Q: Q3. Although no one in the room seemed to follow ______ said by the speaker, he never intended to simplify his language.
    Options: anything / anybody / nothing / anyone
    Ans: anything
  • Q: Q4. I hope you will enjoy yourself at the re-union party this weekend because I won't be able to be there ______.
    Options: myself / mine / oneself / yourself
    Ans: myself
  • Q: Q5. We decided to do all the cooking ______ instead of hiring a catering company for the party.
    Options: of our own / oneself / by ourselves / ours
    Ans: by ourselves

Grammar B — Fill in the blanks with who / whom / that / which / when / where / whose / why

  • Q: The shop ____ I go to is closed.
    Ans: which / that
  • Q: Your shop, ____ will probably be shut down next year, is really old.
    Ans: which
  • Q: I've met most of the people ____ are eager to take part in the competition.
    Ans: who / that
  • Q: Do you know the reason ____ our offer was rejected?
    Ans: why
  • Q: Do you remember the town ____ you were born in?
    Ans: where

Grammar C — Put the indefinite pronouns into the correct blanks

  • Q: Can't you hear that ____ is knocking on the door?
    Ans: someone
  • Q: I was wondering if you would like ____ to drink.
    Ans: something
  • Q: The family members have been badly injured in the accident. Is there ____ to help them?
    Ans: anyone
  • Q: Seema has just checked the internet; however, she couldn't find the article ____.
    Ans: anywhere
  • Q: Unfortunately, this plant is already dead and there is ____ we can do about it.
    Ans: nothing

Grammar D — Underline the pronoun and circle the antecedent

  • Q: Identify the pronoun and its antecedent in: 'Saima walked to the park. She enjoyed jumping on the trampoline.'
    Ans: Pronoun: She. Antecedent: Saima.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun and its antecedent in: 'Shama loves to walk on the beach. She watches the sunset often.'
    Ans: Pronoun: She. Antecedent: Shama.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun and its antecedent in: 'Dawood enjoys playing basketball. He knows that it is his favorite sport.'
    Ans: Pronoun: He (also 'it' and 'his'). Antecedent: Dawood.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun and its antecedent in: 'Abrar, Jamal and Manan enjoy playing cricket. They love teamwork.'
    Ans: Pronoun: They. Antecedent: Abrar, Jamal and Manan.
  • Q: Identify the pronoun and its antecedent in: 'The shopper couldn't find his car in the parking lot.'
    Ans: Pronoun: his. Antecedent: the shopper.

Grammar E — Anaphoric and cataphoric reference in the last paragraph

  • Q: E. Underline the references used in the last paragraph of the lesson and specify whether it is cataphoric or anaphoric reference.
    Ans: In the last paragraph ('It can be concluded that youth was the main focus of Iqbal. He declares youth a symbol of hope and future of the nation. If young generation is ready to contribute to the progress and prosperity of the Umma, the day is not far off when the whole Muslim community will rise as mighty power which no nation of the world will be able to subdue.'), the references are anaphoric: 'He' refers back to Iqbal, mentioned earlier in the paragraph; 'the nation' refers back to the nation whose youth are being discussed; and the relative pronoun 'which' refers back to the 'mighty power' of the Muslim community. No cataphoric reference is used in this paragraph, because every pronoun and reference looks back to a noun introduced before it.

mcqs.q: We all told the boss that we wanted to have our salaries paid in advance but he just ignored ______.
options: we
our
us
his
mcqs.why: Ignored needs an object pronoun, and the people ignored are we, whose object form is us, so he just ignored us is correct.

mcqs.q: When the man asked me how I had got his address, I told him that I was given it by a relative of ______.
options: me
he
him
his
mcqs.why: The relative belongs to the man, so the possessive pronoun his is needed: a relative of his means a relative of the man.

mcqs.q: Although no one in the room seemed to follow ______ said by the speaker, he never intended to simplify his language.
options: anything
anybody
nothing
anyone
mcqs.why: What was said is a thing, not a person, so the indefinite pronoun anything correctly completes the sentence about following the speaker's words.

mcqs.q: I hope you will enjoy yourself at the re-union party this weekend because I won't be able to be there ______.
options: mine
oneself
yourself
myself
mcqs.why: The speaker talks about himself with I as the subject, so the reflexive pronoun must be myself to match the first person subject.

mcqs.q: We decided to do all the cooking ______ instead of hiring a catering company for the party.
options: of our own
by ourselves
oneself
ours
mcqs.why: With the subject we, the correct reflexive expression is by ourselves, meaning without help, instead of hiring a catering company.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence with the correct prefix: 'I just can't believe it! The story is ____believable!'
options: in-
dis-
un-
mis-
mcqs.why: The prefix exercise forms unbelievable with un-, because the story is so surprising that it cannot be believed.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence with the correct prefix: 'No, that answer is ____correct. It is wrong.'
options: re-
in-
un-
dis-
mcqs.why: The prefix exercise forms incorrect with in-, which gives the opposite meaning needed for an answer that is stated to be wrong.

mcqs.q: Complete the word with the correct suffix: 'Fazila can't stay still. She always wants to move! She is rest____.'
options: -ness
-ful
-able
-less
mcqs.why: The suffix exercise forms restless with -less, describing a person who cannot stay still and always wants to move.

mcqs.q: Complete the word with the correct suffix: 'The best thing about her is her kind____.'
options: -ness
-able
-ment
-less
mcqs.why: Kindness is formed by adding -ness to kind, turning the adjective into a noun naming the quality praised in the sentence.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with who / whom / that / which / when / where / whose / why: 'The shop ____ I go to is closed.'
options: who
which
whose
when
mcqs.why: A shop is a thing, so the relative pronoun which, also given as that in the exercise, correctly links the clause to the shop.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with who / whom / that / which / when / where / whose / why: 'Do you know the reason ____ our offer was rejected?'
options: where
which
why
who
mcqs.why: The noun reason needs the relative adverb why, so Do you know the reason why our offer was rejected is the correct completion.

mcqs.q: Put the correct indefinite pronoun in the blank: 'Can't you hear that ____ is knocking on the door?'
options: something
someone
nothing
anywhere
mcqs.why: Knocking is done by a person who is not identified, so the indefinite pronoun someone correctly fills the blank in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Put the correct indefinite pronoun in the blank: 'Unfortunately, this plant is already dead and there is ____ we can do about it.'
options: something
anyone
somewhere
nothing
mcqs.why: Because the plant is already dead, the exercise answer is nothing: there is nothing we can do about it now.

mcqs.q: In 'Saima walked to the park. She enjoyed jumping on the trampoline.', the antecedent of 'She' is ______.
options: the park
Saima
the trampoline
jumping
mcqs.why: The pronoun exercise identifies She as the pronoun and Saima as its antecedent, the noun the pronoun stands for and refers back to.

mcqs.q: What kind of reference is used in the last paragraph of the lesson, where 'He' refers back to Iqbal?
options: Cataphoric reference
Anaphoric reference
No reference at all
A reference to a later noun
mcqs.why: The answer explains that the references are anaphoric because every pronoun looks back to a noun introduced before it, and no cataphoric reference is used.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: Discuss Iqbal's youth with reference to today's Pakistani youth. Write a paragraph of at least 100 words.
    Ans: Iqbal's youth is a Mard-e-Momin, a Mujahid and a Shaheen who believes in Khudi and Ishq, knows himself, and struggles perpetually to discover new worlds instead of resting on material success. Today's Pakistani youth have the same energy, talent and love for their country, and they are shining in education, sports, science and technology. However, many of them are distracted by unemployment, a weak direction and materialism, and they waste their creative energy. If our youth adopt Iqbal's message, channelise their energy in the proper direction and become men of action, pure in head and heart, they can bring a sea change in the social, political and economic fabric of Pakistan and lead the nation to the height of self-sufficiency and independence.
  • Q: D. Look at the mind-map and describe youth from Iqbal's perspective. (Mind-map points: representative of the nation; enthusiastic in action; have the best knowledge; optimistic person; pure in head and heart.)
    Ans: From Iqbal's perspective, youth are the representatives of the nation and its symbol of hope and future. His ideal young man is enthusiastic in action, mild in speech and pure in head and heart, whether he is on the battlefield or in the company of friends. He is an optimistic person who has the best knowledge, develops Khudi, and keeps striving beyond every goal he achieves. Such youth can lead the nation to progress, prosperity and independence.
  • Q: E. Translate the following passage from English to Urdu: 'These are the views of Iqbal about the youth of the nation...'
    Ans: Note: This exercise requires translation into Urdu; translations are not reproduced in these English-only solved notes.

mcqs.q: According to the writing answer, Iqbal's youth is described as which combination?
options: A thinker, a poet and a traveller
A Mard-e-Momin, a Mujahid and a Shaheen
A teacher, a ruler and a trader
A Hamlet, a dreamer and a settler
mcqs.why: The paragraph describes Iqbal's youth as a Mard-e-Momin, a Mujahid and a Shaheen who believes in Khudi and Ishq and knows himself.

mcqs.q: According to the writing answer, in what two things does Iqbal's youth believe?
options: Khudi and Ishq
Wealth and fame
Rest and comfort
Speed and power
mcqs.why: The paragraph says Iqbal's youth believes in Khudi and Ishq, knows himself, and struggles perpetually to discover new worlds.

mcqs.q: According to the writing answer, in which fields are today's Pakistani youth shining?
options: Only in sports and music
Only in trade and farming
Education, sports, science and technology
Politics and debate only
mcqs.why: The paragraph states that today's Pakistani youth have energy and talent and are shining in education, sports, science and technology.

mcqs.q: According to the writing answer, what distracts many of today's youth?
options: Too much knowledge and direction
Unemployment, a weak direction and materialism
Lack of energy and talent
Love for their country
mcqs.why: The paragraph says many youth are distracted by unemployment, a weak direction and materialism, and so waste their creative energy.

mcqs.q: According to the writing answer, what can youth bring if they channelise their energy in the proper direction?
options: A sea change in the social, political and economic fabric of Pakistan
A quick increase in personal wealth only
An end to all education and struggle
A life confined to material success
mcqs.why: The paragraph concludes that such youth can bring a sea change in the social, political and economic fabric of Pakistan and lead it to self-sufficiency.

mcqs.q: According to the mind-map description, youth from Iqbal's perspective are ______.
options: Settlers who avoid struggle
Representatives of the nation
Followers with no knowledge
People confined to material gains
mcqs.why: The mind-map description begins by calling youth the representatives of the nation and its symbol of hope and future in Iqbal's perspective.

mcqs.q: According to the mind-map, Iqbal's ideal young man is ______ in action.
options: Slow
Hesitant
Enthusiastic
Careless
mcqs.why: One mind-map point is enthusiastic in action, and the description repeats that his ideal young man is enthusiastic in action and mild in speech.

mcqs.q: According to the mind-map description, Iqbal's youth is pure in head and heart ______.
options: Only when he is alone
Only on the battlefield
Only among strangers
Whether he is on the battlefield or in the company of friends
mcqs.why: The description says he is pure in head and heart whether he is on the battlefield or in the company of friends, in every situation of life.

mcqs.q: According to the mind-map, which quality belongs to Iqbal's youth?
options: He is an optimistic person who has the best knowledge
He is a pessimistic person with little knowledge
He rests after his first success
He avoids every new goal
mcqs.why: The mind-map lists optimistic person and have the best knowledge, and the description says he keeps striving beyond every goal he achieves.

mcqs.q: According to the mind-map description, how is Iqbal's ideal young man in speech?
options: Harsh in speech
Mild in speech
Silent in speech
Boastful in speech
mcqs.why: The description states that his ideal young man is enthusiastic in action, mild in speech and pure in head and heart.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking

  • Q: Listening and Speaking — Recite a poem of Allama Muhammad Iqbal in front of the class; share in groups Allama Iqbal as the dreamer of Pakistan.
    Ans: This is an oral classroom activity with no written answer.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-Reading

  • Q: Q1. Who do you think a leader is?
    Ans: A leader is a person who guides and inspires others towards a common goal. A true leader is honest, determined and selfless, takes wise decisions in difficult times, and works for the welfare of the people rather than for personal gain.
  • Q: Q2. Why do you think Quaid-e-Azam is a great leader?
    Ans: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is a great leader because, by the force of his determination and leadership, he won a separate homeland, Pakistan, for the Muslims of the subcontinent who had once been a defeated group with little to hope for. He was a man of strong feelings, firm principles and great faith, and he taught his people unity, equality and tolerance.

Glossary

  • Q: Define 'dignified'.
    Ans: Calm and serious and deserving respect.
  • Q: Define 'empire'.
    Ans: A group of countries or states that are controlled by one ruler or government.
  • Q: Define 'stern'.
    Ans: Serious and often disapproving; expecting somebody to obey you.
  • Q: Define 'stretched'.
    Ans: Being longer; spread out over a long distance.
  • Q: Define 'slogan'.
    Ans: A word or phrase that is easy to remember, used for example by a political party or in advertising to attract people's attention or to suggest an idea quickly.
  • Q: Define 'vast'.
    Ans: Extremely large in area, size, amount, etc.
  • Q: Define 'cheering'.
    Ans: Loud shouting that shows support, praise or encouragement for somebody.
  • Q: Define 'foreign'.
    Ans: In or from a country that is not your own.
  • Q: Define 'leadership'.
    Ans: The state or position of being a person who leads a group of people, especially the head of a country, an organization, etc.
  • Q: Define 'homeless'.
    Ans: People who have no home.
  • Q: Define 'excitement'.
    Ans: A feeling of great enthusiasm and eagerness.
  • Q: Define 'refuge'.
    Ans: The state of being safe or sheltered; protection from danger.
  • Q: Define 'violence'.
    Ans: Behaviour involving physical force intended to hurt or damage.
  • Q: Define 'determination'.
    Ans: Firmness of purpose; the quality of continuing to try to achieve something despite difficulties.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Describe the person who had come out of the aeroplane at Mauripur, Karachi, on August 7, 1947.
    Ans: The person who first stepped out of the aeroplane was a tall and dignified man wearing a pure white Sherwani. He was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder and first Governor General of the new country, Pakistan. A vast, excited crowd welcomed him, roaring with one voice, 'Pakistan Zindabad! Pakistan Zindabad!'
  • Q: Q2. Why did the crowd roar in one voice, 'Pakistan Zindabad!'?
    Ans: The crowd roared 'Pakistan Zindabad!' because their great leader, Quaid-e-Azam, who had won Pakistan for them, had arrived among them. The people were full of joy and excitement at the creation of their new country, and everyone pushed forward to welcome him and to get as close to him as possible in order to see him clearly.
  • Q: Q3. Why had people become homeless?
    Ans: People had become homeless because India and Pakistan had become separate countries. Millions of people had to leave their homes to reach their new homeland, and thousands were attacked and killed on the roads and railways. In Pakistan's first year, half a million Indian Muslims were either killed or imprisoned, and six and a half million people left their homes and took refuge in Pakistan due to Indian atrocities.
  • Q: Q4. Why did the Quaid-e-Azam look satisfied?
    Ans: The Quaid-e-Azam looked satisfied because he knew that the greater part of his work was done. By the force of his determination and leadership, a people who had once been a defeated group, with little to hope for, in an empire ruled by a foreign power, had become the greatest of the Muslim States and the 5th largest nation in the world. Seventy million people, who once had no country to call their own, had become a nation with great ideals and a great faith.
  • Q: Q5. What did the Quaid tell the people about equal rights?
    Ans: A few days after he landed in Karachi, Muhammad Ali Jinnah told his people that everyone in Pakistan was free to go to his temples, mosques or any other place of worship. He said that whatever religion or caste a person belonged to, all were citizens of one state. He was reminding them of the Prophet's (peace be upon him) teaching that all men are equal in the eyes of Allah.
  • Q: Q6. Find a sentence from the text, having cause and effect.
    Ans: The sentence is: 'Six and half million people left their homes and took refuge in Pakistan due to Indian atrocities.' Here the cause is the Indian atrocities, and the effect is that six and a half million people left their homes and took refuge in Pakistan.
  • Q: Q7. Identify a sentence from text, expressing an opinion.
    Ans: The sentence is: 'Perhaps he was thinking of the millions of people who had become homeless when India and Pakistan became separate countries.' The word 'Perhaps' shows that this is the writer's opinion or guess about what the Quaid was thinking, not a certain fact.

Comprehension B — Choose the correct answer for the following

  • Q: Q1. 'As he drove through the great sea of people that stretched from the airport to the city.' In this sentence the metaphor 'sea of people' conveys the idea that ____.
    Options: the people were moving like waves of the sea / there was a very great number of people / people were standing in a large area of salty water / a large number of people gathered near the sea
    Ans: there was a very great number of people
  • Q: Q2. 'As soon as he appeared the whole crowd roared with one voice, "Pakistan Zindabad!"' Using the comparison clue, the word 'roared' in this sentence means ____.
    Options: an angry voice / a long, deep voice / an irritated voice / an annoyed voice
    Ans: a long, deep voice
  • Q: Q3. 'Through all the excitement of those first days in the life of the young nation.' In this sentence the phrase 'young nation' represents ____.
    Options: newly developed country / undeveloped country / not fully formed country / an advanced country
    Ans: newly developed country
  • Q: Q4. Quaid-e-Azam, the man who had made it possible, remained calm, serious and sober after independence because ____.
    Options: he was thinking of the millions of people who had become homeless / he was thinking of ways to run the newly born nation / he was thinking about his own family and friends / he was thinking of the ways to accommodate millions of people
    Ans: he was thinking of the millions of people who had become homeless
  • Q: Q5. 'Muhammad Ali Jinnah was at this time tired and far from well.' In this sentence the phrase 'far from well' refers to ____.
    Options: ill or ailing / bedridden or disabled / cruel or infirm / injured or hurt
    Ans: ill or ailing

Comprehension C — What do you understand by the following phrases. Explain

  • Q: Give the meaning of the phrase 'the cheers and tears of joy'.
    Ans: It means the happy shouts and the tears of the people, which showed their extreme happiness. The crowd was so overjoyed at the creation of Pakistan and the arrival of the Quaid that people cheered loudly and wept with joy at the same time.
  • Q: Give the meaning of the phrase 'far from well'.
    Ans: It means ill or ailing; not in good health. At the time of independence, Muhammad Ali Jinnah was tired and quite unwell, yet he continued to work for the new country.
  • Q: Give the meaning of the phrase 'had become a nation'.
    Ans: It means that seventy million Muslims, who once had no country to call their own, had now become one united nation with their own independent state, Pakistan. They had gained a national identity, with great ideals and a great faith.
  • Q: Give the meaning of the phrase 'enemy of today may be friend of tomorrow'.
    Ans: It means that relations between countries or people can change with time, so hatred should not be kept forever. Although the Quaid was shocked at the violence and atrocities, he still extended the hand of friendship towards India, hoping that the enemy of today might become the friend of tomorrow.

Comprehension D — Use the following words in sentences of your own

  • Q: Use 'excitement' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: There was great excitement among the students when the result was announced.
  • Q: Use 'ideal' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Quaid-e-Azam is my ideal because of his honesty and determination.
  • Q: Use 'rarely' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: He rarely shows his feelings in public.
  • Q: Use 'vast' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: A vast crowd had gathered at the airport to welcome the leader.
  • Q: Use 'unity' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Unity, faith and discipline are the guiding principles of our nation.

mcqs.q: 'As he drove through the great sea of people that stretched from the airport to the city.' In this sentence the metaphor 'sea of people' conveys the idea that ____.
options: the people were moving like waves of the sea
people were standing in a large area of salty water
there was a very great number of people
a large number of people gathered near the sea
mcqs.why: Sea is used as a metaphor for a vast quantity, so sea of people means there was a very great number of people from the airport to the city.

mcqs.q: 'As soon as he appeared the whole crowd roared with one voice, "Pakistan Zindabad!"' Using the comparison clue, the word 'roared' in this sentence means ____.
options: a long, deep voice
an angry voice
an irritated voice
an annoyed voice
mcqs.why: Roared compares the crowd's shout to a deep roar, so it means a long, deep voice raised together in the slogan Pakistan Zindabad.

mcqs.q: 'Through all the excitement of those first days in the life of the young nation.' In this sentence the phrase 'young nation' represents ____.
options: undeveloped country
not fully formed country
an advanced country
newly developed country
mcqs.why: Young here means newly come into being, so young nation represents the newly developed country Pakistan in its first days after independence.

mcqs.q: Quaid-e-Azam, the man who had made it possible, remained calm, serious and sober after independence because ____.
options: he was thinking of ways to run the newly born nation
he was thinking of the millions of people who had become homeless
he was thinking about his own family and friends
he was thinking of the ways to accommodate millions of people
mcqs.why: The text says that through all the excitement he remained calm, serious and sober because he was thinking of the millions who had become homeless.

mcqs.q: 'Muhammad Ali Jinnah was at this time tired and far from well.' In this sentence the phrase 'far from well' refers to ____.
options: bedridden or disabled
cruel or infirm
ill or ailing
injured or hurt
mcqs.why: The phrases exercise explains far from well as ill or ailing and not in good health, yet the Quaid continued to work for the new country.

mcqs.q: When and where did Quaid-e-Azam land, as described in the lesson?
options: On 14 August 1947 at Lahore
On 7 August 1947 at Mauripur, Karachi
On 7 August 1947 at Delhi
On 14 August 1947 at Mauripur, Karachi
mcqs.why: The lesson and its summary state that on 7 August 1947 Quaid-e-Azam landed at Mauripur, Karachi, where a vast crowd welcomed him.

mcqs.q: How is the person who first stepped out of the aeroplane described?
options: A short man wearing a dark suit
A tall and dignified man wearing a pure white Sherwani
A tired man wearing a uniform
A young man wearing a white cap
mcqs.why: The answer describes the first person out of the aeroplane as a tall and dignified man wearing a pure white Sherwani, Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

mcqs.q: How many people left their homes and took refuge in Pakistan in the first year, according to the lesson?
options: Half a million people
Seventy million people
Six and a half million people
One million people
mcqs.why: The lesson states that six and a half million people left their homes and took refuge in Pakistan due to Indian atrocities in the first year.

mcqs.q: Why did the Quaid-e-Azam look satisfied, according to the lesson?
options: Because he knew that the greater part of his work was done
Because the crowd had welcomed him loudly
Because he had reached Karachi safely
Because he was no longer tired or unwell
mcqs.why: He looked satisfied because he knew the greater part of his work was done: a defeated people had become a great nation by his determination and leadership.

mcqs.q: What word in the sentence 'Perhaps he was thinking of the millions of people who had become homeless...' shows it is an opinion?
options: Millions
Homeless
Perhaps
Thinking
mcqs.why: The answer explains that Perhaps shows the sentence is the writer's opinion or guess about what the Quaid was thinking, not a certain fact.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary E — Find the meaning of the following words from the dictionary and identify the part of speech

  • Q: Define 'ferocity'.
    Ans: Fierce and violent cruelty; savage fierceness.
  • Q: Identify the part of speech of 'ferocity'.
    Ans: Noun
  • Q: Define 'remind'.
    Ans: To cause somebody to remember something; to make somebody think of something again.
  • Q: Identify the part of speech of 'remind'.
    Ans: Verb
  • Q: Define 'determination'.
    Ans: Firmness of purpose; the quality of being determined to do something despite difficulties.
  • Q: Identify the part of speech of 'determination'.
    Ans: Noun
  • Q: Define 'crowd'.
    Ans: A large number of people gathered together in one place.
  • Q: Identify the part of speech of 'crowd'.
    Ans: Noun
  • Q: Define 'sober'.
    Ans: Serious, calm and sensible; not affected by alcohol.
  • Q: Identify the part of speech of 'sober'.
    Ans: Adjective

Vocabulary F — Consult a thesaurus and find out the antonyms of the following words

  • Q: Give an antonym of 'serious'.
    Ans: Trivial; frivolous; light-hearted.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'violence'.
    Ans: Peace; non-violence; calm.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'weakness'.
    Ans: Strength; power.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'delight'.
    Ans: Sorrow; displeasure; misery.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'harmony'.
    Ans: Discord; conflict; disharmony.

Grammar — Article A: Fill in the article a, an or the where necessary. Insert X where no article is used

  • Q: I like ____ blue T-shirt over there better than ____ red one.
    Ans: the, the
  • Q: Their car does 150 miles ____ hour.
    Ans: an
  • Q: Where's ____ USB drive I lent you last week?
    Ans: the
  • Q: Do you still live in ____ Bannu?
    Ans: X
  • Q: Is your mother working in ____ old office building?
    Ans: an

Grammar — Verbs A: Which of the three sentences containing a modal auxiliary verb has the same meaning as the original one?

  • Q: Q1. They are able to speak English well.
    Options: They can speak English well. / They may speak English well. / They must speak English well.
    Ans: They can speak English well.
  • Q: Q2. There is a possibility of rain tomorrow.
    Options: It may rain tomorrow. / It must rain tomorrow. / It will rain tomorrow.
    Ans: It may rain tomorrow.
  • Q: Q3. Do I have to clean the kitchen?
    Options: Can I clean the kitchen? / Must I clean the kitchen? / Should I clean the kitchen?
    Ans: Must I clean the kitchen?
  • Q: Q4. Are you able to drive a tractor?
    Options: Can you drive a tractor? / Must you drive a tractor? / Should you drive a tractor?
    Ans: Can you drive a tractor?
  • Q: Q5. We are not allowed to swim when the red flag is flying.
    Options: We must not swim when the red flag is flying. / We need not swim when the red flag is flying. / We should not swim when the red flag is flying.
    Ans: We must not swim when the red flag is flying.

Grammar — Verbs B: Find the regular verb in each line

  • Q: Q1. Find the regular verb: read, feel, play, see.
    Ans: play (play – played – played). The others are irregular: read – read – read, feel – felt – felt, see – saw – seen.
  • Q: Q2. Find the regular verb: listen, do, go, make.
    Ans: listen (listen – listened – listened). The others are irregular: do – did – done, go – went – gone, make – made – made.
  • Q: Q3. Find the regular verb: know, help, say, think.
    Ans: help (help – helped – helped). The others are irregular: know – knew – known, say – said – said, think – thought – thought.
  • Q: Q4. Find the regular verb: like, write, forget, eat.
    Ans: like (like – liked – liked). The others are irregular: write – wrote – written, forget – forgot – forgotten, eat – ate – eaten.
  • Q: Q5. Find the regular verb: take, bring, cut, clean.
    Ans: clean (clean – cleaned – cleaned). The others are irregular: take – took – taken, bring – brought – brought, cut – cut – cut.

Grammar — Verbs C: Decide whether the verbs in colour are transitive or intransitive

  • Q: Q1. 'She was crying all day long.' Is the verb 'was crying' transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Intransitive. 'Was crying' has no object; 'all day long' only tells how long she cried.
  • Q: Q2. 'We showed her the photo album.' Is the verb 'showed' transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Transitive. 'Showed' has objects: 'her' and 'the photo album'.
  • Q: Q3. 'The doctor advised me to exercise regularly.' Is the verb 'advised' transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Transitive. 'Advised' has the object 'me'.
  • Q: Q4. 'It was raining at that time.' Is the verb 'was raining' transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Intransitive. 'Was raining' has no object.
  • Q: Q5. 'She laughed at the joke.' Is the verb 'laughed' transitive or intransitive?
    Ans: Intransitive. 'Laughed' has no direct object; 'at the joke' is a prepositional phrase, not an object.

mcqs.q: They are able to speak English well.
options: They may speak English well.
They must speak English well.
They should speak English well.
They can speak English well.
mcqs.why: Are able to expresses ability, which the modal can also expresses, so They can speak English well keeps the same meaning as the original.

mcqs.q: There is a possibility of rain tomorrow.
options: It may rain tomorrow.
It must rain tomorrow.
It will rain tomorrow.
It need not rain tomorrow.
mcqs.why: Possibility is expressed by may, so It may rain tomorrow matches the original, while must and will express certainty instead of possibility.

mcqs.q: Do I have to clean the kitchen?
options: Can I clean the kitchen?
Must I clean the kitchen?
Should I clean the kitchen?
May I clean the kitchen?
mcqs.why: Have to expresses obligation, which must also expresses in a question, so Must I clean the kitchen has the same meaning as the original.

mcqs.q: Are you able to drive a tractor?
options: Must you drive a tractor?
Should you drive a tractor?
Can you drive a tractor?
May you drive a tractor?
mcqs.why: Are you able to asks about ability, and can is the modal of ability, so Can you drive a tractor keeps the same meaning.

mcqs.q: We are not allowed to swim when the red flag is flying.
options: We need not swim when the red flag is flying.
We should not swim when the red flag is flying.
We can swim when the red flag is flying.
We must not swim when the red flag is flying.
mcqs.why: Not allowed to expresses prohibition, which must not also expresses, while need not means it is not necessary and can means the opposite.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct article: 'Their car does 150 miles ____ hour.'
options: a
an
the
X (no article)
mcqs.why: Hour begins with a vowel sound, so the article exercise uses an: Their car does 150 miles an hour.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct article: 'Do you still live in ____ Bannu?'
options: a
an
the
X (no article)
mcqs.why: No article is used before the name of a town, so the exercise marks X for Do you still live in Bannu with no article.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct article: 'Is your mother working in ____ old office building?'
options: a
an
the
X (no article)
mcqs.why: Old begins with a vowel sound and the building is not uniquely specified with the, so the exercise answer is an old office building.

mcqs.q: Find the regular verb in this group: read, feel, play, see.
options: read
feel
play
see
mcqs.why: Play is regular because it forms play, played, played by adding -ed, while read, feel and see are irregular verbs.

mcqs.q: Find the regular verb in this group: take, bring, cut, clean.
options: take
bring
cut
clean
mcqs.why: Clean is regular because it forms clean, cleaned, cleaned, while take, bring and cut change their forms irregularly.

mcqs.q: In 'We showed her the photo album.', the verb 'showed' is ______.
options: Intransitive, because it has no object
Transitive, because it has the objects 'her' and 'the photo album'
Intransitive, because it is in the past tense
Transitive, because it has no object
mcqs.why: The exercise calls showed transitive because it takes objects: her and the photo album receive the action of showing.

mcqs.q: In 'She was crying all day long.', the verb 'was crying' is ______.
options: Transitive, because it has an object
Intransitive, because it has no object
Transitive, because it names a person
Intransitive, because it has two objects
mcqs.why: Was crying has no object and all day long only tells how long she cried, so the exercise classifies it as an intransitive verb.

mcqs.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'ferocity'?
options: Verb
Adjective
Noun
Adverb
mcqs.why: The vocabulary exercise defines ferocity as fierce and violent cruelty and identifies it as a noun, like determination and crowd.

mcqs.q: What is an antonym of 'violence' given in the thesaurus exercise?
options: Strength
Peace
Sorrow
Discord
mcqs.why: The antonyms exercise gives peace, non-violence and calm as opposites of violence, while strength is the antonym of weakness.

mcqs.q: What does 'determination' mean according to the lesson?
options: A word or phrase that is easy to remember
Protection from danger
Firmness of purpose; the quality of continuing to try to achieve something despite difficulties
A feeling of great enthusiasm and eagerness
