lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-Reading

  • Q: Q1. What comes in your mind when you hear the word technology?
    Ans: When I hear the word technology, I think of machines, computers, mobile phones and the internet that make our work easier and faster. Technology means the practical use of scientific knowledge in daily life. It is present everywhere, from the kitchen and bedroom at home to offices, hospitals, farms and transport.
  • Q: Q2. When do you think technology began?
    Ans: Technology began in the earliest days of human life, when man first made simple tools from stone, discovered fire and invented the wheel. Since then it has developed step by step through the ages. Modern electronic technology, however, has grown very fast in the last hundred years.
  • Q: Q3. Name a few technological things that we use in our daily life.
    Ans: We use many technological things in our daily life, such as mobile phones, computers, the internet, television, refrigerators, washing machines and electric fans. We also use cars, buses and aeroplanes for transport. In hospitals, modern electronic machines are used for tests and treatment.

Glossary

  • Q: Define 'disrupt'.
    Ans: To make it difficult for something to continue in the normal way.
  • Q: Define 'benefit'.
    Ans: An advantage that something gives you; a helpful and useful effect that something has.
  • Q: Define 'drought'.
    Ans: A long period of time when there is little or no rain.
  • Q: Define 'proprietors'.
    Ans: The owner of a business, a hotel, etc.
  • Q: Define 'traits'.
    Ans: A particular quality in your personality.
  • Q: Define 'genes'.
    Ans: A unit inside a cell which controls a particular quality in a living thing that has been passed on from its parents.
  • Q: Define 'notch'.
    Ans: A level on a scale, often marking quality or achievement.
  • Q: Define 'ailments'.
    Ans: An illness that is not very serious.
  • Q: Define 'bulkiness'.
    Ans: Large and difficult to move or carry.
  • Q: Define 'conceive'.
    Ans: To form an idea, a plan, etc. in your mind; to imagine something.
  • Q: Define 'stagnant'.
    Ans: Not developing, growing or changing.

Comprehension — Answer the Following Questions

  • Q: Q1. What is the role of technology in daily life?
    Ans: Technology plays a vital role in our daily life and life without it is very strenuous, if not impossible. Technological equipment is present in every part of our home and office, from the kitchen and bedroom to the living room and bathroom. Its uses have spread to health science, communication, agriculture, architecture, engineering and transportation, and it has brought progress to society as a whole.
  • Q: Q2. Discuss how you use technology at home and in your personal life.
    Ans: At home I use technology in almost every room: in the kitchen for cooking and keeping food fresh, and in other rooms for light, fans, television and entertainment. In my personal life I use a mobile phone and the internet to talk to family and friends through calls, e-mails and social media. I also store my photos, documents and study material safely on storage devices instead of keeping bulky files of paper.
  • Q: Q3. How does technology help transportation?
    Ans: Technology has made transportation very fast and efficient, which is a basic need of modern life because time is money. Advanced means of transport like cars, trains and aeroplanes take us to work, carry goods from place to place and help us go shopping and visit friends and families. Both businesses and individuals have greatly benefitted from the new technologies in the travel industry.
  • Q: Q4. What is the importance of technology in agriculture?
    Ans: Technology has been of great benefit to the agricultural industry because farmers can now determine climatic changes and the conditions that favour various plants. With agricultural biotechnology, plants have been engineered to survive in drought conditions, and crops can even be grown in a desert. Through genetic engineering, scientists have introduced traits into existing genes to make crops resistant to droughts and pests.
  • Q: Q5. How is technology being used to generate cheap electricity?
    Ans: Technology helps us generate electricity from natural forces in cheap and clean ways. Large dams store excess water and use that water to generate power, while wind is also being used to generate electricity. Solar energy has been converted into power which is used in homes and businesses, and fire is tamed to heat homes and process industrial materials.
  • Q: Q6. What is the impact of technology on medicine?
    Ans: Technology has greatly improved the health sciences industry because modern electronic equipment has improved the quality of treatment people receive at health institutions. It has increased the survival chances of patients suffering from various ailments. Another great benefit is that doctors can now discover most health problems while they are still in the developing stages and treat them before they develop into advanced stages.
  • Q: Q7. Does technology impact culture and society? How?
    Ans: Yes, technology has a deep impact on culture and society. The internet has changed the world into a global village, so people from different regions share ideas, customs and ways of life through video calls, e-mails and social media. Its positive effects have brought progress and allowed society to reach new heights that were never conceived of before; without science and technology we are left stagnant.

Comprehension — Choose the Correct Answer

  • Q: Q1. The invention and use of internet have reduced the world into a global village. 'Global village' refers to the world as a single community linked by ______.
    Options: transportation / telecommunication / medicine / agriculture
    Ans: telecommunication
  • Q: Q2. Communications are made a lot easier by ______.
    Options: transportation / pigeons / mobile phones / electricity
    Ans: mobile phones
  • Q: Q3. Another importance of technology in our daily lives is that it has eliminated the bulkiness associated with paperwork. 'Bulkiness associated with paperwork' means massive paperwork that is difficult to ______.
    Options: be written / understand / moved from one place to another / be read
    Ans: moved from one place to another
  • Q: Q4. Time is money, so we must have fast and efficient means of transport. 'Time is money' means ______.
    Options: time is easily available, we should not hurry to do things / time is valuable, it's better to utilize it properly / time is cheap, we should waste it / time is difficult to be found, it's costly
    Ans: time is valuable, it's better to utilize it properly
  • Q: Q5. Large amount of data usually involved in research can be easily accessed through ______.
    Options: internet / libraries / telephone / people
    Ans: internet

Comprehension — Use the Following Words in Sentences of Your Own

  • Q: Use 'technology' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Modern technology has made communication across the globe quick and easy.
  • Q: Use 'agriculture' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Agriculture is the backbone of the economy of Pakistan.
  • Q: Use 'transportation' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Transportation has become very fast and efficient in recent times.
  • Q: Use 'fertile' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: Floods carry away the fertile top soil of the farmland.
  • Q: Use 'invention' in a sentence of your own.
    Ans: The invention of the internet has changed the world into a global village.

mcqs.q: The invention and use of internet have reduced the world into a global village. 'Global village' refers to the world as a single community linked by ______.
options: transportation
telecommunication
medicine
agriculture
mcqs.why: The lesson states that the internet has linked people across regions through telecommunication, turning the world into a single community called a global village.

mcqs.q: Communications are made a lot easier by ______.
options: transportation
pigeons
mobile phones
electricity
mcqs.why: The lesson explains that mobile phones have made communication a lot easier, allowing instant contact with family and friends anywhere in the world.

mcqs.q: Another importance of technology in our daily lives is that it has eliminated the bulkiness associated with paperwork. 'Bulkiness associated with paperwork' means massive paperwork that is difficult to ______.
options: be written
understand
moved from one place to another
be read
mcqs.why: Bulkiness means large and difficult to move or carry, so massive paperwork is difficult to be moved from one place to another, unlike compact digital storage.

mcqs.q: Time is money, so we must have fast and efficient means of transport. 'Time is money' means ______.
options: time is easily available, we should not hurry to do things
time is valuable, it's better to utilize it properly
time is cheap, we should waste it
time is difficult to be found, it's costly
mcqs.why: The idiom means time is valuable and should be utilised properly, which is why the lesson stresses fast and efficient means of transport.

mcqs.q: Large amount of data usually involved in research can be easily accessed through ______.
options: internet
libraries
telephone
people
mcqs.why: The lesson says large amounts of research data can be easily accessed through the internet, rather than only through libraries, telephones or people.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, life without technology is described as what?
options: very strenuous, if not impossible
very easy and comfortable
completely unchanged and simple
useful only inside offices
mcqs.why: The comprehension answer states that technology plays a vital role and life without it is very strenuous, if not impossible.

mcqs.q: Through genetic engineering, scientists have introduced traits into existing genes to make crops resistant to what?
options: floods and storms only
cold and darkness
droughts and pests
heat and strong winds
mcqs.why: The lesson says genetic engineering introduces traits into existing genes so that crops become resistant to droughts and pests.

mcqs.q: How do large dams help to generate cheap electricity, according to the lesson?
options: They burn coal to produce power
They store excess water and use that water to generate power
They collect sunlight on their walls
They stop rivers from flowing forever
mcqs.why: The lesson explains that large dams harbor excess water and use that stored water to generate power cheaply and cleanly.

mcqs.q: What is one great benefit of technology in medicine mentioned in the lesson?
options: Doctors no longer need any training
Patients never fall ill again
Medicines have become completely free
Doctors can discover most health problems while they are still in the developing stages
mcqs.why: The lesson says doctors can now discover most health problems in their developing stages and treat them before they become advanced.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'stagnant' mean in the glossary of this lesson?
options: Developing very quickly
Not developing, growing or changing
Moving from place to place
Full of new inventions
mcqs.why: The glossary defines stagnant as not developing, growing or changing, which is how the lesson describes society without science and technology.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary C — Phrases from the Text with the Same Meaning

  • Q: Give the phrase from the text meaning the same as 'genetic modification'.
    Ans: Genetic engineering. In the text, scientists introduce traits into existing genes through genetic engineering to make crops resistant to droughts and pests.
  • Q: Give the phrase from the text meaning the same as 'store water'.
    Ans: Harbor excess water. The text says that large dams can harbor excess water and use that water to generate power.
  • Q: Give the phrase from the text meaning the same as 'calling'.
    Ans: Video calls. The text says that people from different geographical regions can virtually communicate through video calls, e-mails and social media platforms.

Vocabulary D — Antonyms (Consult a Thesaurus)

  • Q: Give an antonym of 'store'.
    Ans: Use up.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'desert'.
    Ans: Oasis.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'friend'.
    Ans: Enemy.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'delay'.
    Ans: Advance.
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'benefit'.
    Ans: Harm.

Grammar — Identify the Phrases and State Their Kind

  • Q: Q1. Identify the phrase in 'He was a man of great wealth.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'of great wealth'. It is an Adjective Phrase, because it qualifies the noun 'man'.
  • Q: Q2. Identify the phrase in 'The principal was an old man of friendly disposition.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'of friendly disposition'. It is an Adjective Phrase, because it qualifies the noun 'man'.
  • Q: Q3. Identify the phrase in 'The workers belonged to a tribe dwelling in the hills.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'dwelling in the hills'. It is an Adjective Phrase, because it qualifies the noun 'tribe'.
  • Q: Q4. Identify the phrase in 'There I met a boy with red hair.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'with red hair'. It is an Adjective Phrase, because it qualifies the noun 'boy'.
  • Q: Q5. Identify the phrases in 'Only a man with plenty of money can buy a car of such beauty and power.' and state their kind.
    Ans: The phrases are 'with plenty of money' and 'of such beauty and power'. Both are Adjective Phrases: the first qualifies the noun 'man' and the second qualifies the noun 'car'.
  • Q: Q6. Identify the phrase in 'He was a young man of great promise.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'of great promise'. It is an Adjective Phrase, because it qualifies the noun 'man'.
  • Q: Q7. Identify the phrase in 'He wore a turban made of gold.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'made of gold'. It is an Adjective Phrase, because it qualifies the noun 'turban'.
  • Q: Q8. Identify the phrase in 'He ran with great speed.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'with great speed'. It is an Adverb Phrase, because it modifies the verb 'ran' and tells how he ran.

Revision Exercise 1 — Underline the Adjectives

  • Q: Q1. Identify the adjective in 'The team has had enough practice.'
    Ans: Enough. It is an adjective of quantity describing 'practice'.
  • Q: Q2. Identify the adjective in 'She did not eat any fruit.'
    Ans: Any. It is an adjective of quantity describing 'fruit'.
  • Q: Q3. Identify the adjective in 'He is a noisy boy.'
    Ans: Noisy. It is an adjective of quality describing 'boy'.
  • Q: Q4. Identify the adjective in 'They showed much patience.'
    Ans: Much. It is an adjective of quantity describing 'patience'.
  • Q: Q5. Identify the adjective in 'This is a Pakistani cloth.'
    Ans: Pakistani. It is a proper adjective describing 'cloth'.

Revision Exercise 2 — Change the Words into Adjectives with Comparative and Superlative Degrees

  • Q: Q1. Change 'love' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Lovely — more lovely — most lovely.
  • Q: Q2. Change 'grace' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Graceful — more graceful — most graceful.
  • Q: Q3. Change 'music' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Musical — more musical — most musical.
  • Q: Q4. Change 'juice' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Juicy — juicier — juiciest.
  • Q: Q5. Change 'fool' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Foolish — more foolish — most foolish.
  • Q: Q6. Change 'dust' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Dusty — dustier — dustiest.
  • Q: Q7. Change 'nation' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: National. It is an absolute adjective and has no comparative or superlative degree in normal use.
  • Q: Q8. Change 'child' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Childish — more childish — most childish.
  • Q: Q9. Change 'danger' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Dangerous — more dangerous — most dangerous.
  • Q: Q10. Change 'comfort' into an adjective and write its comparative and superlative degrees.
    Ans: Comfortable — more comfortable — most comfortable.

Revision Exercise 3 — Use the Correct Degree of Adjective

  • Q: This is the ____ tree in the garden. (tall)
    Ans: tallest
  • Q: She is a ____ woman. (wise)
    Ans: wise
  • Q: He is the ____ of all brothers. (young)
    Ans: youngest
  • Q: Prevention is ____ than cure. (good)
    Ans: better
  • Q: Your composition is the ____ of all. (bad)
    Ans: worst

Revision Exercise 4 — Complete the Sentences Using Proper Order of Adjectives

  • Q: Q1. All the students liked the ______ teacher.
    Options: handsome new English / English new handsome / new handsome English
    Ans: handsome new English
  • Q: Q2. He recently married a ______ woman.
    Options: young beautiful Punjabi / beautiful young Punjabi / beautiful Punjabi young
    Ans: beautiful young Punjabi
  • Q: Q3. This is a ______ movie.
    Options: new Pakistani wonderful / wonderful Pakistani new / wonderful new Pakistani
    Ans: wonderful new Pakistani
  • Q: Q4. He is a ______ player.
    Options: brave smart pakistani / Pakistani brave smart / smart brave Pakistani
    Ans: smart brave Pakistani
  • Q: Q5. It's in the ______ container.
    Options: large blue metal / blue large metal / blue metal large
    Ans: large blue metal

Revision Exercise 5 — Underline the Adverb and Identify the Question It Answers

  • Q: Q1. Identify the adverbs in 'As he ran quickly, he suddenly stumbled.' and state which question each answers.
    Ans: 'Quickly' answers How? (how he ran), and 'suddenly' answers How? (in what manner he stumbled). Both are adverbs of manner.
  • Q: Q2. Identify the adverb in 'Weather forecasters, frequently make mistakes.' and state which question it answers.
    Ans: 'Frequently' answers How often? It is an adverb of frequency.
  • Q: Q3. Identify the adverbs in 'If you will wait here, Mr. Khan will see you shortly.' and state which question each answers.
    Ans: 'Here' answers Where? (adverb of place), and 'shortly' answers When? (adverb of time).
  • Q: Q4. Identify the adverbs in 'The extremely fierce storm damaged the town extensively.' and state which question each answers.
    Ans: 'Extremely' answers To what extent or degree? and 'extensively' also answers To what extent or degree? Both are adverbs of degree.
  • Q: Q5. Identify the adverbs in 'The load shifted slightly, and the truck lurched dangerously.' and state which question each answers.
    Ans: 'Slightly' answers To what extent or degree? (adverb of degree), and 'dangerously' answers How? (adverb of manner).

Revision Exercise 6 — Complete the Sentences by Choosing the Correct Degree of Adverb

  • Q: My younger brother plays hockey ____ than me. (well/better)
    Ans: better
  • Q: She sings ____. (well/best)
    Ans: well
  • Q: She works ____ than me. (more quickly/quickly)
    Ans: more quickly
  • Q: He listened to me ____. (more carefully/carefully)
    Ans: carefully
  • Q: The player hit the ball ____. (forcefully/more forcefully)
    Ans: forcefully

Revision Exercise 7 — Use the Following Degrees of Adverb in Sentences

  • Q: Use 'more carefully' in a sentence.
    Ans: You should drive more carefully on this busy road.
  • Q: Use 'most carefully' in a sentence.
    Ans: Of all the students, Ahmed wrote his paper most carefully.
  • Q: Use 'less expensive' in a sentence.
    Ans: This bicycle is less expensive than that one.
  • Q: Use 'least expensive' in a sentence.
    Ans: This is the least expensive watch in the shop.
  • Q: Use 'less fairly' in a sentence.
    Ans: The second match was judged less fairly than the first.
  • Q: Use 'least fairly' in a sentence.
    Ans: Of all the teams, our team was treated least fairly in the tournament.
  • Q: Use 'better' in a sentence.
    Ans: She sings better than her sister.
  • Q: Use 'best' in a sentence.
    Ans: He performed best in the final match.
  • Q: Use 'worse' in a sentence.
    Ans: The weather today is worse than yesterday.
  • Q: Use 'worst' in a sentence.
    Ans: He played worst in the last game of the season.

Revision Exercise 8 — Change the Sentences Using Adverbial Phrases in Place of the Adverbs

  • Q: Q1. Change 'He answered me rudely.' by using an adverbial phrase in place of the adverb.
    Ans: He answered me in a rude manner.
  • Q: Q2. Change 'The stone fell here.' by using an adverbial phrase in place of the adverb.
    Ans: The stone fell in this place.
  • Q: Q3. Change 'She is sleeping now.' by using an adverbial phrase in place of the adverb.
    Ans: She is sleeping at this moment.
  • Q: Q4. Change 'She attempted the paper carefully.' by using an adverbial phrase in place of the adverb.
    Ans: She attempted the paper with great care.
  • Q: Q5. Change 'My brother drives carefully.' by using an adverbial phrase in place of the adverb.
    Ans: My brother drives with care.

Revision Exercise 9 — Fill in the Blanks with Suitable Prepositions

  • Q: He is fond ____ tea.
    Ans: of
  • Q: She was angry ____ me.
    Ans: with
  • Q: Let us hope ____ the best.
    Ans: for
  • Q: They were absent ____ the class.
    Ans: from
  • Q: He will reach in ____ twenty minutes.
    Ans: about
  • Q: My village is ____ the river.
    Ans: across
  • Q: The earth moves ____ the sun.
    Ans: around
  • Q: They are sitting ____ the tree.
    Ans: beneath
  • Q: There is a river ____ the two cities.
    Ans: between
  • Q: Wait ____ tomorrow.
    Ans: till

Revision Exercise 10 — Use the Following Prepositional Phrases in Sentences

  • Q: Use 'abide by' in a sentence.
    Ans: Every citizen must abide by the laws of the country.
  • Q: Use 'absent from' in a sentence.
    Ans: He was absent from school yesterday because of illness.
  • Q: Use 'accused of' in a sentence.
    Ans: The man was accused of theft and taken to the police station.
  • Q: Use 'appear before' in a sentence.
    Ans: The accused will appear before the judge tomorrow.
  • Q: Use 'care for' in a sentence.
    Ans: She does not care for tea in the evening.
  • Q: Use 'died of' in a sentence.
    Ans: The patient died of a heart attack.

Revision Exercise 11 — Simple or Compound Sentence

  • Q: Q1. State whether 'It is very hot in the afternoon.' is a simple or a compound sentence.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has only one clause and no conjunction joining two clauses.
  • Q: Q2. State whether 'I'm living now but I will be back in an hours time.' is a simple or a compound sentence, and name the conjunction.
    Ans: Compound sentence. The conjunction is 'but', which joins two independent clauses.
  • Q: Q3. State whether 'Dad took out a thousand rupees note and gave it to the cashier.' is a simple or a compound sentence.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has one subject, 'Dad', with two verbs joined by 'and', so it is a single clause with a compound predicate.
  • Q: Q4. State whether 'The fishermen went out in the morning and came back with a lot of fish.' is a simple or a compound sentence.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has one subject, 'The fishermen', with two verbs joined by 'and', so it is a single clause.
  • Q: Q5. State whether 'Rahim said good bye to everyone.' is a simple or a compound sentence.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has only one clause.
  • Q: Q6. State whether 'Every country celebrated the new year.' is a simple or a compound sentence.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has only one clause.
  • Q: Q7. State whether 'We were planning to go to the zoo but our car broke down on the way.' is a simple or a compound sentence, and name the conjunction.
    Ans: Compound sentence. The conjunction is 'but', which joins two independent clauses.
  • Q: Q8. State whether 'Ms. Naheed was not feeling well, so she went to see the doctor.' is a simple or a compound sentence, and name the conjunction.
    Ans: Compound sentence. The conjunction is 'so', which joins two independent clauses.
  • Q: Q9. State whether 'Uncle Khan is teaching me to drive.' is a simple or a compound sentence.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has only one clause.
  • Q: Q10. State whether 'Would you like to go to the museum or to the zoo?' is a simple or a compound sentence.
    Ans: Simple sentence. It has only one clause; 'or' joins two phrases, not two clauses.

Revision Exercise 12 — Identify the Phrases and State Their Kind

  • Q: Q1. Identify the phrase in 'You can buy it in all places.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'in all places'. It is an Adverb Phrase, because it modifies the verb 'buy' and tells where it can be bought.
  • Q: Q2. Identify the phrase in 'He replied in a very rude manner.' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'in a very rude manner'. It is an Adverb Phrase, because it modifies the verb 'replied' and tells how he replied.
  • Q: Q3. Identify the phrase in 'How does he live without any worries?' and state its kind.
    Ans: The phrase is 'without any worries'. It is an Adverb Phrase, because it modifies the verb 'live' and tells how he lives.

Revision Exercise 13 — Underline the Clauses and State Their Kind

  • Q: Q1. Identify the clause in 'The angler said that he hadn't caught any fish that morning.' and state whether it is an adjective clause, adverb clause or noun clause.
    Ans: The clause is 'that he hadn't caught any fish that morning'. It is a Noun Clause, because it works as the object of the verb 'said'.
  • Q: Q2. Identify the clause in 'I wondered if she was free.' and state whether it is an adjective clause, adverb clause or noun clause.
    Ans: The clause is 'if she was free'. It is a Noun Clause, because it works as the object of the verb 'wondered'.
  • Q: Q3. Identify the clause in 'Though he didn't receive formal schooling, he is clever and industrious.' and state whether it is an adjective clause, adverb clause or noun clause.
    Ans: The clause is 'Though he didn't receive formal schooling'. It is an Adverb Clause (of concession), because it modifies the main clause and gives the condition against which he is clever and industrious.
  • Q: Q4. Identify the clause in 'The boys who misbehaved in the class were suspended.' and state whether it is an adjective clause, adverb clause or noun clause.
    Ans: The clause is 'who misbehaved in the class'. It is an Adjective Clause, because it qualifies the noun 'boys'.
  • Q: Q5. Identify the clause in 'He who laughs last laughs best.' and state whether it is an adjective clause, adverb clause or noun clause.
    Ans: The clause is 'who laughs last'. It is an Adjective Clause, because it qualifies the pronoun 'He'.

Revision Exercise 14 — Re-write Using Appropriate Punctuation Marks and Capital Letters

  • Q: Q1. Re-write with correct punctuation and capitals: 'my best friend and his family are moving to swat'
    Ans: My best friend and his family are moving to Swat.
  • Q: Q2. Re-write with correct punctuation and capitals: 'you dont look happy to see me do you'
    Ans: You don't look happy to see me, do you?
  • Q: Q3. Re-write with correct punctuation and capitals: 'you shouldnt have done this to Jameel'
    Ans: You shouldn't have done this to Jameel.
  • Q: Q4. Re-write with correct punctuation and capitals: 'there is a large rain forest in south america'
    Ans: There is a large rain forest in South America.
  • Q: Q5. Re-write with correct punctuation and capitals: 'I have never been to changa manga'
    Ans: I have never been to Changa Manga.

Revision Exercise 15 — Change into Passive Voice

  • Q: Q1. Change into passive voice: 'The teacher praised the boy.'
    Ans: The boy was praised by the teacher.
  • Q: Q2. Change into passive voice: 'Everyone liked the idea.'
    Ans: The idea was liked by everyone.
  • Q: Q3. Change into passive voice: 'Alia sang a song.'
    Ans: A song was sung by Alia.

Revision Exercise 16 — Change Active into Passive and Passive into Active

  • Q: Q1. Change the voice: 'She gave the beggar a five rupee coin.'
    Ans: A five rupee coin was given to the beggar by her. (Passive voice)
  • Q: Q2. Change the voice: 'They are painting the walls.'
    Ans: The walls are being painted by them. (Passive voice)
  • Q: Q3. Change the voice: 'The car has been fixed by the mechanic.'
    Ans: The mechanic has fixed the car. (Active voice)
  • Q: Q4. Change the voice: 'She accepted their invitation with pleasure.'
    Ans: Their invitation was accepted by her with pleasure. (Passive voice)

mcqs.q: All the students liked the ______ teacher.
options: handsome new English
English new handsome
new handsome English
new English handsome
mcqs.why: Adjectives follow the order opinion, age and origin, so handsome (opinion), new (age) and English (origin) is the correct order before teacher.

mcqs.q: He recently married a ______ woman.
options: young beautiful Punjabi
beautiful young Punjabi
beautiful Punjabi young
Punjabi beautiful young
mcqs.why: The correct order is opinion before age before origin, so beautiful young Punjabi places opinion, age and origin in the proper sequence.

mcqs.q: This is a ______ movie.
options: new Pakistani wonderful
wonderful Pakistani new
wonderful new Pakistani
Pakistani wonderful new
mcqs.why: Opinion comes before age and origin, so wonderful new Pakistani is correct: wonderful is opinion, new is age and Pakistani is origin.

mcqs.q: He is a ______ player.
options: brave smart pakistani
Pakistani brave smart
smart brave Pakistani
brave Pakistani smart
mcqs.why: Quality adjectives come before the origin adjective, so smart brave Pakistani keeps both quality words before Pakistani, the origin.

mcqs.q: It's in the ______ container.
options: large blue metal
blue large metal
blue metal large
metal large blue
mcqs.why: Size comes before colour and material, so large blue metal is correct: large is size, blue is colour and metal is material.

mcqs.q: In 'He was a man of great wealth', the phrase 'of great wealth' is which kind of phrase?
options: An Adverb Phrase, because it modifies a verb
A Noun Phrase, because it acts as a subject
An Adjective Phrase, because it qualifies the noun 'man'
A Verb Phrase, because it shows an action
mcqs.why: The solved grammar answer states that of great wealth is an Adjective Phrase because it qualifies the noun man in the sentence.

mcqs.q: In 'He ran with great speed', why is 'with great speed' an Adverb Phrase?
options: It qualifies the noun 'speed'
It modifies the verb 'ran' and tells how he ran
It acts as the object of the sentence
It joins two independent clauses
mcqs.why: The answer explains that with great speed modifies the verb ran and tells how he ran, so it works as an Adverb Phrase.

mcqs.q: In 'This is a Pakistani cloth', the word 'Pakistani' is what kind of adjective?
options: An adjective of quantity
An adjective of number
A demonstrative adjective
A proper adjective
mcqs.why: Pakistani is formed from a proper noun and describes cloth, so the revision answer identifies it as a proper adjective.

mcqs.q: What are the comparative and superlative degrees of the adjective formed from 'juice'?
options: juicy — more juicy — most juicy
juicy — juicier — juiciest
juiceful — juicier — juiciest
juicy — juicyer — juicyest
mcqs.why: Juice becomes juicy, and the exercise gives its degrees as juicier for the comparative and juiciest for the superlative degree.

mcqs.q: Use the correct degree: 'This is the ____ tree in the garden.' (tall)
options: tallest
taller
tall
more tall
mcqs.why: The definite article the with a comparison against all trees in the garden requires the superlative degree, which is tallest.

mcqs.q: In 'Weather forecasters frequently make mistakes', the adverb 'frequently' answers which question?
options: Where?
When exactly?
How often?
To what extent?
mcqs.why: The revision answer states that frequently answers How often and is therefore an adverb of frequency in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: 'He is fond ____ tea.'
options: with
of
for
from
mcqs.why: The fixed prepositional phrase is fond of, as given in the revision exercise on suitable prepositions with fond taking of.

mcqs.q: 'Ms. Naheed was not feeling well, so she went to see the doctor.' This is a compound sentence because:
options: it has only one clause with two verbs
it has no conjunction at all
it describes only one person
the conjunction 'so' joins two independent clauses
mcqs.why: The answer identifies it as compound because so joins two independent clauses that can each stand alone as sentences.

mcqs.q: In 'The angler said that he hadn't caught any fish that morning', the clause 'that he hadn't caught any fish that morning' is:
options: a Noun Clause, working as the object of 'said'
an Adjective Clause, qualifying 'angler'
an Adverb Clause of time
a main clause with no function
mcqs.why: The revision answer states that the clause works as the object of the verb said, which makes it a Noun Clause.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'The teacher praised the boy.'
options: The boy is praised by the teacher.
The boy was praised by the teacher.
The teacher was praised by the boy.
The boy has praised the teacher.
mcqs.why: The active sentence is in the past tense, so the passive form is The boy was praised by the teacher, as given in the exercise.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing E — Essay on a Scientific Discovery of the 21st Century

  • Q: E. Write an essay on any scientific discovery of 21st century.
    Ans: The Discovery of the Higgs Boson. One of the greatest scientific discoveries of the 21st century is the discovery of the Higgs boson, often called the 'God particle'. Scientists had been searching for this tiny particle for almost fifty years, because the theory of physics said that it gives mass to all other particles, but nobody had ever seen it. To find it, thousands of scientists from many countries built the Large Hadron Collider near Geneva, the biggest and most powerful machine in the world, in a tunnel about 27 kilometres long under the ground. In this machine, particles were smashed into each other at nearly the speed of light, and powerful computers recorded the results. On 4 July 2012, the scientists announced that they had found a new particle exactly where the theory had predicted the Higgs boson would be. This discovery completed the picture of how the universe is built and proved that the old theory was correct. It also opened new doors for research in physics, medicine and technology. The discovery shows that with patience, teamwork and technology, human beings can uncover even the deepest secrets of nature.

Writing F — Mind Map and Summary of the Lesson

  • Q: F. Develop a mind map and write down the summary of the lesson 'Technology in Everyday Life'.
    Ans: Mind map: The central idea is 'Technology in Everyday Life'. Its main branches are: (1) Health — modern electronic equipment, better treatment, early discovery of diseases, more survival chances; (2) Communication — internet, global village, video calls, e-mails, social media, mobile phones; (3) Information storage — no bulky paperwork, compact disks and microchips, passwords keep information safe; (4) Agriculture — knowledge of climate, biotechnology, crops in deserts, genetic engineering against drought and pests; (5) Natural forces — dams store water and generate power, wind and solar energy produce electricity; (6) Transportation — cars, trains and aeroplanes, fast and efficient travel. Summary: The importance of technology in our daily lives is undeniable, and life without it is very strenuous, if not impossible. In health sciences, modern equipment has improved treatment and helps doctors discover diseases in their early stages. The internet has turned the world into a global village and made communication instant, while information can now be stored safely on small devices instead of bulky paper files. Technology helps farmers grow better crops through biotechnology and genetic engineering, and it tames natural forces to produce electricity from water, wind and the sun. Fast and efficient transport has become a basic need of life. In short, the positive effects of technology have brought progress to society, and without science and technology we are left stagnant.

Writing G — Translation from English to Urdu

  • Q: G. Translate the following sentence from English to Urdu: 'Transportation is one of the basic areas of technological activity.'
    Ans: Note: This exercise requires translation into Urdu; translations are not reproduced in these English-only solved notes.
  • Q: G. Translate the following sentence from English to Urdu: 'Technology has been of great use is the health industry.'
    Ans: Note: This exercise requires translation into Urdu; translations are not reproduced in these English-only solved notes.
  • Q: G. Translate the following sentence from English to Urdu: 'Communication across the globe is now easy.'
    Ans: Note: This exercise requires translation into Urdu; translations are not reproduced in these English-only solved notes.
  • Q: G. Translate the following sentence from English to Urdu: 'Natural forces affect and disrupt human life and daily economic activates.'
    Ans: Note: This exercise requires translation into Urdu; translations are not reproduced in these English-only solved notes.
  • Q: G. Translate the following sentence from English to Urdu: 'Technology has been of great benefit to agricultural industry.'
    Ans: Note: This exercise requires translation into Urdu; translations are not reproduced in these English-only solved notes.
