lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Look at the picture and predict what the lesson is about?
    Ans: The pictures show an injured young man lying on the ground and a car hitting a motorcyclist. They suggest that the lesson is about accidents and injuries, and about the immediate help, called first aid, that should be given to an injured person before medical help arrives. The lesson is therefore about safety and first aid.

Glossary

  • Q: Define 'collapses'.
    Ans: To fall down or fall in suddenly, often after breaking apart.
  • Q: Define 'choking'.
    Ans: To be unable to breathe because the passage to the lungs is blocked or because one cannot get enough air; to make somebody unable to breathe.
  • Q: Define 'thrust'.
    Ans: To push something or somebody suddenly or violently in a particular direction; to move quickly and suddenly in a particular direction.
  • Q: Define 'elevate'.
    Ans: To give somebody or something a higher position or rank; to raise. In the lesson it means to raise the injured part of the body.
  • Q: Define 'wound'.
    Ans: An injury to part of the body, especially one in which a hole is made in the skin using a weapon.
  • Q: Define 'dislodge'.
    Ans: To force or knock something out of its position.
  • Q: Define 'emergency'.
    Ans: A sudden, serious and dangerous event or situation which needs immediate action to deal with it.
  • Q: Define 'adhesive'.
    Ans: A substance that you use to make things stick together.
  • Q: Define 'lodge'.
    Ans: To make or become firmly fixed or stuck in a place.
  • Q: Define 'nostrils'.
    Ans: Either of the two openings at the end of the nose that you breathe through.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What is first aid?
    Ans: First aid is the help given to a sick or injured person until full medical treatment is available. It is about using common sense in ways that will keep that person safe without doing harm. If a friend has an accident or someone collapses, the first person present becomes the first aider and helps the casualty till help arrives.
  • Q: Q2. Discuss a situation in which you provided first aid to someone.
    Ans: Once during a cricket match, a classmate fell and cut his knee, which started bleeding badly. I stayed calm, made him sit down, placed a clean cloth over the wound and pressed it firmly. I raised his leg a little and sent another boy to call the teacher. The bleeding stopped, and he was then taken to the dispensary for proper dressing.
  • Q: Q3. What will you do if someone cuts his foot and is bleeding?
    Ans: I will not panic; I will take a deep breath to calm down. I will call on the emergency phone number for help and, in the meanwhile, put a cloth over the wound, apply pressure on it and elevate the foot. Pressing the wound and raising it slows down the bleeding until medical help arrives.
  • Q: Q4. You're having lunch with a friend and he begins to choke on some food. How can you help?
    Ans: First, I will make sure he is really choking. If he can talk or cough, it means air is getting through, and I will just let him cough. If he cannot talk or cough, I will do the abdominal thrust: I will stand behind him, wrap my arms around him and quickly pull in and up with my fist. The air forced up will dislodge the piece of food from his throat.
  • Q: Q5. A passenger travelling in bus with you is complaining of breathlessness and a tight pain in the chest. You suspect a heart attack. What should you do?
    Ans: I will call medical help as soon as possible and ask the driver to stop or take the bus towards the nearest hospital. In the meanwhile, I will ease the strain on his heart by making him as comfortable as possible. The best position is a half-sitting position, with his head and shoulders supported and his knees bent. I will not make him lie flat, and I will not press his chest.

Comprehension B — Choose the correct answer

  • Q: Q1. A burn should be immersed or placed under cold water for at least
    Options: 5 minutes / 10 minutes / 15 minutes / 20 minutes
    Ans: 20 minutes
  • Q: Q2. If your friend cut his finger and it bleeds profusely, you should
    Options: put the injured finger in some cold water. / apply direct pressure over the wound. / give him an aspirin / let him bleed till emergency doctor arrives.
    Ans: apply direct pressure over the wound.
  • Q: Q3. What should one do if one's nose bleeds.
    Options: lie upside down / run towards home / give jerks to one's head / press his/her nostrils in finger and thumb
    Ans: press his/her nostrils in finger and thumb
  • Q: Q4. Which one of the following should be avoided if someone gets heart attack:
    Options: call medical help as soon as possible / ease the strain on the heart / rest him/her in half sitting position / press his/her chest
    Ans: press his/her chest

mcqs.q: A burn should be immersed or placed under cold water for at least
options: 10 minutes
20 minutes
5 minutes
15 minutes
mcqs.why: The first aid guidance in the lesson requires a burn to be immersed or placed under cold water for at least twenty minutes to cool it properly.

mcqs.q: If your friend cut his finger and it bleeds profusely, you should
options: put the injured finger in some cold water.
give him an aspirin
apply direct pressure over the wound.
let him bleed till emergency doctor arrives.
mcqs.why: For profuse bleeding the lesson directs the first aider to apply direct pressure over the wound, which slows and stops the flow of blood.

mcqs.q: What should one do if one's nose bleeds.
options: press his/her nostrils in finger and thumb
lie upside down
run towards home
give jerks to one's head
mcqs.why: The lesson instructs that a nosebleed is controlled by pressing the nostrils between finger and thumb, not by lying down or jerking the head.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following should be avoided if someone gets heart attack:
options: call medical help as soon as possible
ease the strain on the heart
rest him/her in half sitting position
press his/her chest
mcqs.why: The comprehension answer on heart attack clearly says not to press the chest, while calling help, easing strain and half-sitting rest are all advised.

mcqs.q: What is first aid, according to the lesson?
options: Treatment given only inside a hospital
The help given to a sick or injured person until full medical treatment is available
A medicine given for every illness
Training given only to doctors and nurses
mcqs.why: The lesson defines first aid as the help given to a sick or injured person until full medical treatment is available, using common sense safely.

mcqs.q: If someone cuts his foot and it is bleeding, what should you do while waiting for help?
options: Make him run to the hospital at once
Leave the wound open to the air
Put a cloth over the wound, apply pressure on it and elevate the foot
Press his chest again and again
mcqs.why: The answer states that you should put a cloth over the wound, apply pressure and elevate the foot, which slows the bleeding until help arrives.

mcqs.q: Your friend is choking but he can still talk or cough. What does this mean and what should you do?
options: It means air is getting through, so just let him cough
It means he needs the abdominal thrust at once
It means he is having a heart attack
It means you should give him water to drink
mcqs.why: The lesson explains that if the person can talk or cough, air is getting through, so you should simply let him cough.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of the abdominal thrust for a person who is choking and cannot talk or cough?
options: To make him sit in a half-sitting position
To stop bleeding from a wound
To cool a burn under cold water
To force air up so it dislodges the piece of food from his throat
mcqs.why: The answer explains that the quick pull in and up forces air up, which dislodges the piece of food stuck in the throat.

mcqs.q: What is the best position for a person suspected of having a heart attack?
options: Lying completely flat on the ground
A half-sitting position, with head and shoulders supported and knees bent
Standing and walking slowly
Sitting with the head hanging down
mcqs.why: The lesson advises a half-sitting position with the head and shoulders supported and knees bent, and warns not to make him lie flat.

mcqs.q: In this lesson, what does the word 'elevate' mean?
options: To press firmly on a wound
To give first aid training
To raise the injured part of the body
To call the emergency number
mcqs.why: The glossary explains that elevate means to raise, and in the lesson it means to raise the injured part of the body, such as a bleeding foot.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Look up the meaning and make sentences

  • Q: Q1. Explain the difference between 'look' and 'search' with sentences.
    Ans: 'Look' means to direct the eyes towards something in order to see it; it does not necessarily involve trying to find anything. 'Search' means to look carefully and thoroughly in order to find something that is lost or hidden. Sentences: Look at the blackboard, please. The police searched the whole house for the stolen goods.
  • Q: Q2. Explain the difference between 'buy' and 'purchase' with sentences.
    Ans: Both words mean to get something by paying money for it. 'Buy' is the common, everyday word used for ordinary things, while 'purchase' is a more formal word, often used for costly things and in business or official writing. Sentences: I bought a notebook from the shop. The school purchased new computers for the laboratory.
  • Q: Q3. Explain the difference between 'hide' and 'conceal' with sentences.
    Ans: 'Hide' means to put something where it cannot be seen or found. 'Conceal' is a more formal word and means to keep something secret, or to carefully prevent it from being seen or known. Sentences: The child hid behind the door. He concealed the letter in his pocket so that no one could see it.
  • Q: Q4. Explain the difference between 'learn' and 'educate' with sentences.
    Ans: 'Learn' means to gain knowledge or a skill by study, practice or experience; the learner does it himself. 'Educate' means to give knowledge and training to another person, usually in a school or college. Sentences: We learn first aid in this class. It is the duty of the state to educate every child.
  • Q: Q5. Explain the difference between 'reward' and 'award' with sentences.
    Ans: A 'reward' is something, often money, given in return for good work, help or service, or offered for finding something lost. An 'award' is a prize, medal or honour formally given by judges or an authority for an achievement. Sentences: A reward of ten thousand rupees was announced for finding the lost bag. She received an award for her bravery.

Vocabulary B — Contextual meanings

  • Q: Give the contextual meaning of 'bleed'.
    Ans: To lose blood from a wound or injury, as when a person cuts his arm and blood flows out of it.
  • Q: Give the contextual meaning of 'accident'.
    Ans: A sudden, unexpected event in which someone is injured, for example a road crash or a fall.
  • Q: Give the contextual meaning of 'burn'.
    Ans: An injury caused by heat or fire on the skin; in the lesson, the injury a person gets from a hot stove.
  • Q: Give the contextual meaning of 'attack'.
    Ans: In 'heart attack', a sudden serious illness in which the heart stops working properly and the person feels tight pain in the chest.
  • Q: Give the contextual meaning of 'pressure'.
    Ans: The force of pressing firmly on something; in the lesson, pressing a cloth firmly on a wound to stop the bleeding.

Grammar — Punctuation: Choose the correct sentence

  • Q: Q1. Choose the correct sentence.
    Options: this is what i ate for breakfast an apple and a bowl of cereal. / This is what I ate for breakfast, an apple and a bowl of cereal. / this is what i ate for breakfast: an apple and a bowl of cereal. / this is what i ate for breakfast, an apple and a bowl of cereal.
    Ans: this is what i ate for breakfast: an apple and a bowl of cereal.
  • Q: Q2. Choose the correct sentence.
    Options: he knocked several times, no one came to the door. / He knocked several times; no one came to the door. / he knocked several times: no one came to the door. / he knocked several times no one came to the door.
    Ans: He knocked several times; no one came to the door.
  • Q: Q3. Choose the correct sentence.
    Options: my sister loves mysteries; my brother likes comics. / My sister loves mysteries, my brother likes comics. / my sister loves mysteries my brother likes comics. / my sister loves mysteries: my brother likes comics.
    Ans: my sister loves mysteries; my brother likes comics.
  • Q: Q4. Choose the correct sentence.
    Options: here is what you need to get at the supermarket bananas bread milk and biscuits. / here is what you need to get at the supermarket: bananas bread milk and biscuits. / here is what you need to get at the supermarket; bananas, bread, milk and biscuits. / Here is what you need to get at the supermarket: bananas, bread, milk and biscuits.
    Ans: Here is what you need to get at the supermarket: bananas, bread, milk and biscuits.
  • Q: Q5. Choose the correct sentence.
    Options: the window was open I looked out over the empty fields. / The window was open, I looked out over the empty fields. / the window was open: I looked out over the empty fields. / the window was open; I looked out over the empty fields.
    Ans: the window was open; I looked out over the empty fields.

Grammar — Exercise: PASTA (comma or semicolon)

  • Q: Throughout the following paragraph you will find a number of empty paired brackets: [ ]. Replace each set of brackets with a comma or a semicolon. Paragraph: PASTA — Pasta[ ] a large family of shaped[ ] dried wheat pastes[ ] is a basic staple in many countries. Its origins are obscure. Rice pastes were known very early in China[ ] pastes made of wheat were used in India and Arabia long before they were introduced into Europe in the 11th or 12th century. According to legend[ ] Marco Polo brought a pasta recipe with him from Asia in 1295. Pasta quickly became a major element in the Italian diet[ ] and its use spread throughout Europe. Pasta is made from durum wheat flour[ ] which makes a strong[ ] elastic dough. Hard durum wheat has the highest wheat protein value. The flour is mixed with water[ ] kneaded to form a thick paste[ ] and then forced through perforated plates or dies that shape it into one of more than 100 different forms.
    Ans: In order, the ten brackets take: 1 comma, 2 comma, 3 comma, 4 semicolon, 5 comma, 6 comma, 7 comma, 8 comma, 9 comma, 10 comma. The paragraph correctly punctuated is: Pasta, a large family of shaped, dried wheat pastes, is a basic staple in many countries. Its origins are obscure. Rice pastes were known very early in China; pastes made of wheat were used in India and Arabia long before they were introduced into Europe in the 11th or 12th century. According to legend, Marco Polo brought a pasta recipe with him from Asia in 1295. Pasta quickly became a major element in the Italian diet, and its use spread throughout Europe. Pasta is made from durum wheat flour, which makes a strong, elastic dough. Hard durum wheat has the highest wheat protein value. The flour is mixed with water, kneaded to form a thick paste, and then forced through perforated plates or dies that shape it into one of more than 100 different forms.

Grammar — Punctuation marks and capital letters

  • Q: Q1. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: river ravi flows through lahore
    Ans: River Ravi flows through Lahore.
  • Q: Q2. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: eiffel tower is the most famous monument in france
    Ans: Eiffel Tower is the most famous monument in France.
  • Q: Q3. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: my brother is a singer
    Ans: My brother is a singer.
  • Q: Q4. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: where have you been all this while
    Ans: Where have you been all this while?
  • Q: Q5. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: you look hot are you ill
    Ans: You look hot. Are you ill?
  • Q: Q6. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: come here at once
    Ans: Come here at once!
  • Q: Q7. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: abrar is a smart boy
    Ans: Abrar is a smart boy.
  • Q: Q8. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: sania couldn't believe her eyes when she saw the bicycle
    Ans: Sania couldn't believe her eyes when she saw the bicycle.
  • Q: Q9. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: india is the seventh largest country in the world
    Ans: India is the seventh largest country in the world.
  • Q: Q10. Rewrite the following sentence using appropriate punctuation marks and capital letters wherever necessary: karachi is the capital of sindh
    Ans: Karachi is the capital of Sindh.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: this is what i ate for breakfast an apple and a bowl of cereal.
This is what I ate for breakfast, an apple and a bowl of cereal.
this is what i ate for breakfast: an apple and a bowl of cereal.
this is what i ate for breakfast, an apple and a bowl of cereal.
mcqs.why: A colon is used here because what follows the colon gives the list of items eaten for breakfast, and a comma alone cannot introduce that list correctly.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: he knocked several times, no one came to the door.
He knocked several times; no one came to the door.
he knocked several times: no one came to the door.
he knocked several times no one came to the door.
mcqs.why: A semicolon correctly joins two closely related independent clauses, whereas a comma alone would create a comma splice between them.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: my sister loves mysteries; my brother likes comics.
My sister loves mysteries, my brother likes comics.
my sister loves mysteries my brother likes comics.
my sister loves mysteries: my brother likes comics.
mcqs.why: The two independent clauses about the sister and brother are correctly joined by a semicolon; a comma alone or a colon would be incorrect here.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: here is what you need to get at the supermarket bananas bread milk and biscuits.
here is what you need to get at the supermarket: bananas bread milk and biscuits.
here is what you need to get at the supermarket; bananas, bread, milk and biscuits.
Here is what you need to get at the supermarket: bananas, bread, milk and biscuits.
mcqs.why: A colon introduces the list of things needed at the supermarket, and the items in the list are correctly separated by commas in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: the window was open I looked out over the empty fields.
The window was open, I looked out over the empty fields.
the window was open: I looked out over the empty fields.
the window was open; I looked out over the empty fields.
mcqs.why: A semicolon correctly joins the two independent clauses about the open window and looking out, while a comma alone would be a comma splice.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'look' and 'search', according to the vocabulary answers?
options: Both words mean exactly the same thing
'Look' means to hide something carefully
'Search' means to look carefully and thoroughly in order to find something lost or hidden
'Search' means to direct the eyes without trying to find anything
mcqs.why: The answer explains that search means to look carefully and thoroughly to find something lost or hidden, while look only directs the eyes.

mcqs.q: How do 'buy' and 'purchase' differ in use?
options: 'Purchase' is the everyday word for ordinary things
'Buy' is used only in official business writing
They can never be used for the same action
'Buy' is the common everyday word, while 'purchase' is more formal and often used for costly things
mcqs.why: The vocabulary answer states that buy is the common everyday word, while purchase is more formal and used for costly things and official writing.

mcqs.q: What is an 'award', as explained in the vocabulary answers?
options: Money offered for finding something lost
A prize, medal or honour formally given by judges or an authority for an achievement
Something given only in return for daily wages
A secret gift hidden in a pocket
mcqs.why: The answer defines an award as a prize, medal or honour formally given by judges or an authority for an achievement, unlike a reward.

mcqs.q: In the lesson, what is the contextual meaning of 'pressure'?
options: The force of pressing firmly on something, such as a cloth on a wound to stop bleeding
A sudden pain in the chest
A substance used to stick things together
An injury caused by heat or fire
mcqs.why: In context, pressure means pressing a cloth firmly on a wound to stop bleeding, as the vocabulary answer explains in detail.

mcqs.q: In 'heart attack', what does the word 'attack' mean in this lesson?
options: An injury on the skin caused by a hot stove
Blood flowing out of a wound
A sudden serious illness in which the heart stops working properly and the person feels tight pain in the chest
The force of pressing on a wound
mcqs.why: The contextual meaning given is a sudden serious illness in which the heart stops working properly, with tight pain in the chest.

mcqs.q: In the PASTA paragraph, the bracket after 'Rice pastes were known very early in China' takes which mark?
options: A comma, because it ends a short phrase
A semicolon, because it joins two independent clauses
A colon, because a list follows it
No mark at all is needed there
mcqs.why: The solved exercise places a semicolon after China because it joins two complete independent clauses about rice pastes and wheat pastes.

mcqs.q: How does the correctly punctuated PASTA paragraph begin?
options: Pasta a large family of shaped dried wheat pastes is a basic staple
Pasta; a large family of shaped, dried wheat pastes; is a basic staple
Pasta, a large family of shaped, dried wheat pastes, is a basic staple in many countries.
Pasta: a large family of shaped dried wheat pastes is a basic staple
mcqs.why: The solved paragraph opens with commas setting off the descriptive phrase: Pasta, a large family of shaped, dried wheat pastes, is a basic staple.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated and capitalised?
options: river ravi flows through lahore
River Ravi flows through Lahore.
river Ravi flows through Lahore
River ravi flows through lahore.
mcqs.why: River begins the sentence and Ravi and Lahore are proper nouns, so River Ravi flows through Lahore is the correctly capitalised sentence.

mcqs.q: Which punctuation mark is needed at the end of 'Where have you been all this while'?
options: A full stop, because it gives information
An exclamation mark, because it is an order
A comma, because the sentence continues
A question mark, because it asks a question
mcqs.why: The sentence asks a direct question beginning with Where, so the exercise correctly ends it with a question mark.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
options: Come here at once!
come here at once
Come here at once
come here at once.
mcqs.why: Come here at once is a sudden command, so it begins with a capital letter and ends with an exclamation mark in the solved exercise.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: A. Write an essay of about 100-150 words on 'Natural Disaster'.
    Ans: A natural disaster is a sudden and terrible event of nature that causes great loss of life and property. Floods, earthquakes, storms, droughts and landslides are common natural disasters. Pakistan has suffered many of them: the earthquake of 2005 and the floods of 2010 and 2022 destroyed thousands of homes, schools, roads and crops, and made millions of people homeless. Natural disasters cannot be stopped, but their damage can be reduced. Strong houses, early warning systems, rescue teams and first aid training can save many lives. The government, the army and welfare organizations should reach the affected people quickly with food, water, tents and medicines. We should also protect forests and rivers, because damaging nature makes disasters worse. With preparation, unity and timely help, a nation can face any natural disaster bravely.
  • Q: B. In your opinion, how should schools be equipped to face floods, earthquake and fire (natural and man-made)?
    Ans: Every school should be prepared for emergencies before they happen. The school building should be strong, with wide exits and an open assembly ground where students can gather safely. There should be fire extinguishers, sand buckets, a first aid kit and stretchers in the school, and teachers and senior students should be trained in first aid and fire drill. Mock drills for earthquake and fire evacuation should be held regularly so that students leave the classrooms in lines without panic. The school should keep the phone numbers of the rescue service, hospital, fire brigade and police displayed in the office. For floods, important records and books should be kept on upper floors, and a safe route to high ground should be known to everyone.
  • Q: C. Translate the following sentences from Urdu to English. (The seven sentences are printed in Urdu script in the book.)
    Ans: 1. I have already applied for the post. 2. I have not received his letter for several days. 3. I have completed my work. 4. Had he come home before it rained? 5. The boys had plucked the flowers before the gardener came. 6. I have known him for three years. 7. He has deceived me.

mcqs.q: According to the model essay, what is a natural disaster?
options: A man-made accident inside a factory
A sudden and terrible event of nature that causes great loss of life and property
A long period without any rain only
A celebration held after heavy rain
mcqs.why: The essay defines a natural disaster as a sudden and terrible event of nature that causes great loss of life and property.

mcqs.q: Which set lists the common natural disasters named in the essay?
options: Theft, fire and road accidents
Examinations, floods and storms
Floods, earthquakes, storms, droughts and landslides
Only floods and earthquakes
mcqs.why: The essay names floods, earthquakes, storms, droughts and landslides as the common natural disasters faced by people.

mcqs.q: Which disasters in Pakistan does the essay specifically mention?
options: The earthquake of 2005 and the floods of 2010 and 2022
The storm of 1999 and the drought of 2015
Only the floods of 2022
The earthquake of 2010 and floods of 2005
mcqs.why: The essay states that the earthquake of 2005 and the floods of 2010 and 2022 destroyed homes, schools, roads and crops in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: According to the essay, how can the damage of natural disasters be reduced?
options: By stopping all rain and earthquakes
By ignoring early warnings
By building only temporary houses
By strong houses, early warning systems, rescue teams and first aid training
mcqs.why: The essay says damage can be reduced through strong houses, early warning systems, rescue teams and first aid training that save lives.

mcqs.q: Who should reach the affected people quickly, and with what, according to the essay?
options: Only shopkeepers, with goods to sell
The government, the army and welfare organizations, with food, water, tents and medicines
Only foreign tourists, with cameras
Neighbours only, with advice and sympathy
mcqs.why: The essay states that the government, army and welfare organizations should reach affected people quickly with food, water, tents and medicines.

mcqs.q: Why does the essay say we should protect forests and rivers?
options: Because damaging nature makes disasters worse
Because forests stop all floods completely
Because rivers provide free electricity
Because trees attract more rainfall every year
mcqs.why: The essay warns that damaging nature makes disasters worse, so protecting forests and rivers is part of facing natural disasters bravely.

mcqs.q: Which equipment should a school keep for emergencies, according to the writing answer?
options: Only extra chairs and tables
Fire extinguishers, sand buckets, a first aid kit and stretchers
Only sports goods and musical instruments
Extra textbooks and registers only
mcqs.why: The answer lists fire extinguishers, sand buckets, a first aid kit and stretchers among the equipment every prepared school should keep.

mcqs.q: Why should mock drills for earthquake and fire evacuation be held regularly in schools?
options: So that students can leave the classrooms in lines without panic
So that students learn to run as fast as possible
So that classes can be cancelled often
So that teachers can test new equipment only
mcqs.why: The answer explains that regular mock drills teach students to leave classrooms in lines without panic during a real emergency.

mcqs.q: Where should the phone numbers of the rescue service, hospital, fire brigade and police be kept in a school?
options: Hidden inside a locked cupboard
Written only in the head teacher's diary
Displayed in the school office
Sent home only once a year
mcqs.why: The answer states that these emergency phone numbers should be displayed in the office so they can be used at once when needed.

mcqs.q: How should a school prepare its records and choose its safety arrangements for floods?
options: Keep records on the ground floor near the door
Keep important records and books on upper floors, and know a safe route to high ground
Close the school for the whole rainy season
Store all books in the assembly ground
mcqs.why: For floods, the answer advises keeping important records and books on upper floors and knowing a safe route to high ground.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking

  • Q: Listening and Speaking — Work in pairs and express your personal ideas / feelings / emotions on effects of calamities and how can it be minimized. Share your views in front of the class.
    Ans: This is an oral classroom activity with no written answer.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. What do the pictures below have in common?
    Ans: All the pictures show old women with wrinkled faces and grey hair. What they have in common is old age: each woman has lived a long life, her youthful beauty has faded, and her face shows experience, patience and the marks of a lifetime of work.
  • Q: Q2. What does the phrase 'respect your elders' mean?
    Ans: The phrase means that we should honour, obey and care for people who are older than us, especially our parents, grandparents and teachers. Elders have more experience and wisdom than us, so we should listen to them, speak to them politely and value their advice.
  • Q: Q3. How do you show respect to your elders?
    Ans: We show respect to our elders by greeting them politely, listening to them without interrupting, and helping them in their daily work. We should sit with them, look after them in illness and old age, and never speak to them rudely or raise our voice before them. Their prayers and advice are a blessing for us.

Glossary

  • Q: Define 'radiance'.
    Ans: A special bright quality that shows in somebody's face, for example because they are very happy or healthy.
  • Q: Define 'travail'.
    Ans: An unpleasant experience or situation that involves a lot of hard work, difficulties and suffering.
  • Q: Define 'brood'.
    Ans: A person's child or children.
  • Q: Define 'ruined'.
    Ans: Destroyed or severely damaged so that only parts remain.

Comprehension A — Read out the text and answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Who does the poet praise in the poem 'The Old Woman'? Explain how.
    Ans: The poet praises an old woman, that is, old age itself. He does not praise youthful beauty; instead he praises the calm and holy beauty of her aged face. He compares her face to a white candle in a holy place and to the spent radiance of the winter sun, and praises her still, peaceful thoughts, showing that a life of hard work, fully completed, deserves honour and respect.
  • Q: Q2. What does a white candle represent in the poem 'The Old Woman'?
    Ans: The white candle represents purity, holiness and gentle, peaceful light. Just as a white candle burns calmly and sacredly in a holy place, the face of the old woman shines with a pure and sacred beauty. It also suggests a life that has spread light around itself and is now quiet, dignified and near its end.
  • Q: Q3. What is the message in the poem 'The Old Woman'? Explain briefly.
    Ans: The message of the poem is that old age has its own beauty, dignity and peace, and the old deserve our respect. A woman whose work of life is finished, whose children are grown and gone, and whose thoughts have become calm like still water, is not ugly or useless. True beauty lies in a life well spent, not in youth alone.
  • Q: Q4. Why does the poet compare old woman to a 'white candle in a holy place', the winter sun and the water under a ruined mill in the poem 'The Old Woman'?
    Ans: Each comparison brings out one quality of the old woman. She is like a white candle in a holy place because her aged face has a pure, sacred and calm beauty. She is like the spent radiance of the winter sun because her strength and youthful glow are fading, yet she still gives soft light and warmth born of long experience. Her thoughts are like the waters under a ruined mill because, now that the busy mill of her active life has stopped, her mind is perfectly still, deep and peaceful.
  • Q: Q5. Do you like this poem 'The Old Woman'? Why?
    Ans: Yes, I like this poem very much. Its language is simple, yet its similes are beautiful and easy to picture: a white candle, the winter sun and still water under a ruined mill. It changes our way of looking at old people: instead of seeing wrinkles and weakness, we begin to see holiness, experience and peace, and we learn to respect our elders.
  • Q: Q6. What words in the poem help establish imagery?
    Ans: The words and phrases that create pictures in the reader's mind are: 'white candle', 'holy place', 'aged face', 'spent radiance', 'winter sun', 'travail done', 'brood gone' and 'waters under a ruined mill'. These images appeal to the sense of sight and make us see the calm face of the old woman, soft fading light and quiet, still water.
  • Q: Q7. How many lines and stanzas are there in this poem?
    Ans: There are 12 lines in the poem, arranged in 3 stanzas. Each stanza has 4 lines.

Comprehension B — Choose the correct option

  • Q: Q1. Poet's comparison of old woman to a white candle is made in the form of __________.
    Options: personification / simile / alliteration / metaphor
    Ans: simile
  • Q: Q2. The poet compares the old woman with 'the spent radiance of the winter's sun'. What does it mean?
    Options: old woman is weak but with rich experience of life / old woman is strong and with wide experience of life / old woman is symbol of beauty and sunshine / old woman is symbol of success and growth
    Ans: old woman is weak but with rich experience of life
  • Q: Q3. 'Her brood gone from her' means __________.
    Options: her beauty gone / her children gone / her strength gone / her wealth gone
    Ans: her children gone
  • Q: Q4. The poet says that 'As the waters under a ruined mill'. What does it mean?
    Options: to emphasize that there is steadiness and maturity in the life of an old woman / to point out that it is very difficult for old women to show whether they feel confident or not / to suggest that old women do not usually have the feeling of hope / to indicate that wide range of experience is an extra ornaments in the life of old lady
    Ans: to emphasize that there is steadiness and maturity in the life of an old woman
  • Q: Q5. What does 'travail done' mean based on the poem?
    Options: difficulties of an old woman neither vanished nor runs away / laborious life of an old woman / calmness and wisdom in the life of an old woman / natural beauty vanished in an old woman
    Ans: laborious life of an old woman

mcqs.q: Poet's comparison of old woman to a white candle is made in the form of __________.
options: personification
simile
alliteration
metaphor
mcqs.why: The comparison uses as and so, as a white candle in a holy place, so is the beauty of an aged face, which is the form of a simile.

mcqs.q: The poet compares the old woman with 'the spent radiance of the winter's sun'. What does it mean?
options: old woman is weak but with rich experience of life
old woman is strong and with wide experience of life
old woman is symbol of beauty and sunshine
old woman is symbol of success and growth
mcqs.why: Spent radiance means her youthful strength and glow are fading like the winter sun, so she is weak yet rich with the experience of a long life.

mcqs.q: 'Her brood gone from her' means __________.
options: her beauty gone
her children gone
her strength gone
her wealth gone
mcqs.why: The glossary defines brood as a person's children, so her brood gone from her means her children have grown up and gone from her.

mcqs.q: The poet says that 'As the waters under a ruined mill'. What does it mean?
options: to emphasize that there is steadiness and maturity in the life of an old woman
to point out that it is very difficult for old women to show whether they feel confident or not
to suggest that old women do not usually have the feeling of hope
to indicate that wide range of experience is an extra ornaments in the life of old lady
mcqs.why: Still waters under a ruined mill show a mind at complete rest, emphasising the steadiness and maturity in the life of an old woman.

mcqs.q: What does 'travail done' mean based on the poem?
options: difficulties of an old woman neither vanished nor runs away
laborious life of an old woman
calmness and wisdom in the life of an old woman
natural beauty vanished in an old woman
mcqs.why: Travail means hard work, difficulties and suffering, so travail done refers to the laborious life of the old woman now being finished.

mcqs.q: Who does the poet praise in the poem 'The Old Woman', and how?
options: A young beautiful woman, for her youthful charm
An old woman, that is old age itself, praising the calm and holy beauty of her aged face
A mother, only for raising many children
A winter scene, for its cold and silence
mcqs.why: The answer states that the poet praises an old woman, old age itself, not youthful beauty but the calm and holy beauty of her aged face.

mcqs.q: What is the message of the poem 'The Old Woman'?
options: Old people are useless and should be ignored
Youth is the only form of true beauty
Old age has its own beauty, dignity and peace, and the old deserve our respect
Old age brings only pain and loneliness
mcqs.why: The message explained in the answers is that old age has its own beauty, dignity and peace, and a life well spent deserves respect.

mcqs.q: How many lines and stanzas are there in the poem 'The Old Woman'?
options: 9 lines in 3 stanzas
12 lines in 3 stanzas, with 4 lines in each stanza
12 lines in 4 stanzas
16 lines in 4 stanzas
mcqs.why: The comprehension answer states clearly that the poem has 12 lines arranged in 3 stanzas, and each stanza has 4 lines.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'travail' mean in the glossary?
options: A bright quality shown in a happy face
A person's child or children
Destroyed so that only parts remain
An unpleasant experience involving a lot of hard work, difficulties and suffering
mcqs.why: The glossary defines travail as an unpleasant experience or situation involving hard work, difficulties and suffering in a person's life.

mcqs.q: Which phrase from the poem helps to establish imagery of soft, fading light?
options: 'spent radiance of the winter sun'
'respect your elders'
'brood gone from her' only as a sound
'ruined mill' as a place name
mcqs.why: Spent radiance of the winter sun is listed among the image-making phrases because it pictures soft, fading light like the old woman's glow.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • Q: A. Identify the similes in the poem 'The Old Woman'.
    Ans: There are three similes in the poem, all made with 'as' and 'so': (1) 'As a white candle / In a holy place, / So is the beauty / Of an aged face.' (2) 'As the spent radiance / Of the winter sun, / So is a woman / With her travail done.' (3) 'And her thoughts as still / As the waters / Under a ruined mill.'
  • Q: B. Which lines of the poem 'The Old Woman' indicate imagery?
    Ans: Almost all the lines create imagery, especially: 'As a white candle in a holy place' (image of calm, sacred light); 'So is the beauty of an aged face' (image of the wrinkled old face); 'As the spent radiance of the winter sun' (image of soft, fading light); and 'As the waters under a ruined mill' (image of deep, still water). These lines appeal to the sense of sight and create clear mental pictures.
  • Q: C. Pick out rhyming words from the poem 'The Old Woman'.
    Ans: The rhyming pairs at the ends of lines are: place — face (stanza 1); sun — done (stanza 2); still — mill (stanza 3).

Grammar A — Active and Passive voice: Change into the passive voice

  • Q: Q1. Change into the passive voice: I have finished the job.
    Ans: The job has been finished by me.
  • Q: Q2. Change into the passive voice: They built this house in 1990.
    Ans: This house was built by them in 1990.
  • Q: Q3. Change into the passive voice: He has bought a new car.
    Ans: A new car has been bought by him.
  • Q: Q4. Change into the passive voice: I wrote a letter.
    Ans: A letter was written by me.
  • Q: Q5. Change into the passive voice: They sent the parcel on Monday.
    Ans: The parcel was sent by them on Monday.
  • Q: Q6. Change into the passive voice: The police caught the thief yesterday.
    Ans: The thief was caught by the police yesterday.
  • Q: Q7. Change into the passive voice: She baked a cake.
    Ans: A cake was baked by her.
  • Q: Q8. Change into the passive voice: I read a book.
    Ans: A book was read by me.
  • Q: Q9. Change into the passive voice: She gave the beggar a five rupee coin.
    Ans: The beggar was given a five rupee coin by her. (Also: A five rupee coin was given to the beggar by her.)

Grammar B — Change active to passive and passive to active

  • Q: Q1. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: The thieves have been arrested by the police.
    Ans: The police have arrested the thieves. (Passive changed to Active)
  • Q: Q2. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: The marvelous performance delivered by the children enthralled us.
    Ans: We were enthralled by the marvelous performance delivered by the children. (Active changed to Passive)
  • Q: Q3. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: He has been invited to their party.
    Ans: They have invited him to their party. (Passive changed to Active; the doer is not named in the original sentence, so 'They' is supplied.)
  • Q: Q4. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: We have shipped your order.
    Ans: Your order has been shipped by us. (Active changed to Passive)
  • Q: Q5. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: The girl recited the poem beautifully.
    Ans: The poem was recited beautifully by the girl. (Active changed to Passive)
  • Q: Q6. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: The guests enjoyed the party.
    Ans: The party was enjoyed by the guests. (Active changed to Passive)
  • Q: Q7. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: The child impressed everyone with his polite manners.
    Ans: Everyone was impressed by the child with his polite manners. (Active changed to Passive)
  • Q: Q8. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: A girl from Bannu won the first prize.
    Ans: The first prize was won by a girl from Bannu. (Active changed to Passive)
  • Q: Q9. Rewrite, changing the active sentences to passive and passive sentences to active: The readers like the latest book of the writer.
    Ans: The latest book of the writer is liked by the readers. (Active changed to Passive)

mcqs.q: How many similes are there in the poem 'The Old Woman'?
options: One simile
Two similes
Three similes
Four similes
mcqs.why: The vocabulary answer identifies three similes, all made with as and so: the white candle, the winter sun and the waters under a ruined mill.

mcqs.q: In the first simile, the beauty of an aged face is compared to what?
options: A white candle in a holy place
The spent radiance of the winter sun
The waters under a ruined mill
A bright lamp in a market place
mcqs.why: The first simile reads: As a white candle in a holy place, so is the beauty of an aged face, comparing her face to the candle.

mcqs.q: In the third simile, the old woman's thoughts are compared to what?
options: A white candle in a holy place
The spent radiance of the winter sun
A fast flowing river in summer
The waters under a ruined mill
mcqs.why: The third simile says her thoughts are as still as the waters under a ruined mill, picturing a mind that is deep and peaceful.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words rhymes at the end of the lines in the first stanza?
options: sun — done
still — mill
place — face
candle — holy
mcqs.why: The rhyming answer lists place and face as the rhyming pair at the ends of the lines in the first stanza of the poem.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words rhymes in the second stanza?
options: place — face
still — mill
face — sun
sun — done
mcqs.why: The second stanza ends its rhyming lines with sun and done, as listed in the rhyming words answer for this poem.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words rhymes in the third stanza?
options: still — mill
sun — done
place — face
mill — sun
mcqs.why: The third stanza's rhyming pair is still and mill, matching her still thoughts with the waters under the ruined mill.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'I have finished the job.'
options: The job is finished by me.
The job has been finished by me.
The job was being finished by me.
I have been finished by the job.
mcqs.why: The present perfect active becomes has been finished in the passive, giving The job has been finished by me, as in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'They built this house in 1990.'
options: This house is built by them in 1990.
This house has been built by them in 1990.
This house was built by them in 1990.
This house will be built by them in 1990.
mcqs.why: Built is past tense, so the passive uses was built: This house was built by them in 1990, exactly as the grammar answer gives.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'He has bought a new car.'
options: A new car has been bought by him.
A new car was bought by him yesterday.
A new car is bought by him.
He has been bought by a new car.
mcqs.why: Has bought in the present perfect becomes has been bought, so a new car has been bought by him in the passive voice.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The police caught the thief yesterday.'
options: The thief is caught by the police yesterday.
The thief has caught the police yesterday.
The thief was caught by the police yesterday.
The thief will be caught by the police yesterday.
mcqs.why: Caught is past tense, so the passive form is was caught: The thief was caught by the police yesterday, as solved in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'She baked a cake.'
options: A cake is baked by her.
A cake was baked by her.
A cake has been baked by her daily.
She was baked by a cake.
mcqs.why: Baked is in the past tense, so the correct passive sentence is A cake was baked by her, following the pattern of the exercise.

mcqs.q: Change into the active voice: 'The thieves have been arrested by the police.'
options: The police have arrested the thieves.
The police has arresting the thieves.
The thieves have arrested the police.
The police were arrested by the thieves.
mcqs.why: Removing been and restoring the doer as subject gives the active sentence The police have arrested the thieves, as in the answer.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'We have shipped your order.'
options: Your order is shipped by us yesterday.
Your order has been shipped by us.
We have been shipped by your order.
Your order was shipping by us.
mcqs.why: Have shipped in the present perfect becomes has been shipped, so your order has been shipped by us in the passive voice.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The girl recited the poem beautifully.'
options: The poem is recited beautifully by the girl.
The poem was recited beautifully by the girl.
The girl was recited by the poem beautifully.
The poem has reciting by the girl.
mcqs.why: Recited is past tense, so the passive is was recited: The poem was recited beautifully by the girl, as given in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Change into the passive voice: 'A girl from Bannu won the first prize.'
options: The first prize is won by a girl from Bannu.
The first prize has been won by a girl from Bannu.
A girl from Bannu was won by the first prize.
The first prize was won by a girl from Bannu.
mcqs.why: Won is past tense, so the passive uses was won: The first prize was won by a girl from Bannu, exactly as solved in the exercise.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: a. Paraphrase the first and third stanza of the poem The Old Woman.
    Ans: First stanza: The beauty of an old woman's face is just like a white candle burning in a holy place. Her face is pure, calm and sacred, and it shines with a quiet holiness. Third stanza: Her children have grown up and left her, and now her mind is at complete rest. Her thoughts are as calm and still as the water that lies quietly under an old, ruined mill which no longer works.
  • Q: b. Write the summary of the poem The Old Woman.
    Ans: In this poem Joseph Campbell praises the beauty of old age. He says that the face of an old woman is beautiful like a white candle burning in a holy place: pure, calm and sacred. Like the soft, fading light of the winter sun, she has spent her strength in a long life of hard work, and now her labour is finished. Her children have grown up and left her, and her thoughts have become still and peaceful like the quiet water under a ruined mill. The poem teaches us that old age is dignified and beautiful, and that the old deserve love and respect.
  • Q: c. Write an essay of about 100 words on 'Appreciating and Respecting Elders.'
    Ans: Elders are the most precious treasure of a family. They have spent their whole lives working for us, and their experience is a guiding light for the young. Appreciating and respecting them is both our moral and religious duty. We should greet our elders politely, listen to their advice, and help them in their daily needs. We must never be rude to them, especially to our parents and grandparents, who deserve our service in their old age. A society that honours its elders remains united, wise and blessed, while the young who ignore them lose the benefit of their prayers and experience. Respecting elders costs nothing, but it earns us their love, their prayers and success in life.

mcqs.q: According to the paraphrase, what is the beauty of an old woman's face like in the first stanza?
options: Like a white candle burning in a holy place: pure, calm and sacred
Like a bright noon sun in summer
Like a fast river after rain
Like a lamp in a busy bazaar
mcqs.why: The paraphrase of the first stanza says her face is like a white candle in a holy place, pure, calm, sacred and shining with quiet holiness.

mcqs.q: According to the paraphrase of the third stanza, why is the old woman's mind at complete rest?
options: Because she has forgotten her whole life
Because her children have grown up and left her, and her thoughts are still like water under a ruined mill
Because she sleeps for the whole day
Because the mill near her house still works
mcqs.why: The paraphrase explains that her children have grown and left her, and her thoughts are as calm and still as water under a ruined mill.

mcqs.q: Who is the poet of 'The Old Woman', as named in the summary?
options: William Wordsworth
Emily Dickinson
Joseph Campbell
Leigh Hunt
mcqs.why: The summary begins by stating that in this poem Joseph Campbell praises the beauty of old age through the figure of the old woman.

mcqs.q: According to the summary, what has the old woman spent in her long life of hard work?
options: Her wealth and property
Her beauty only
Her strength, like the soft fading light of the winter sun
Her time in travel and rest
mcqs.why: The summary says that like the soft, fading light of the winter sun, she has spent her strength in a long life of hard work.

mcqs.q: How does the model essay describe elders at its opening?
options: As a burden on the family
As the most precious treasure of a family
As people who need no help at all
As strangers living in the family
mcqs.why: The essay opens by calling elders the most precious treasure of a family, whose experience is a guiding light for the young.

mcqs.q: Appreciating and respecting elders is described in the essay as what kind of duty?
options: Only a school duty
An optional social custom
Both our moral and religious duty
A duty only for grown-up children
mcqs.why: The essay states that appreciating and respecting elders is both our moral and our religious duty, not merely an optional custom.

mcqs.q: According to the essay, how should we treat our elders in daily life?
options: Greet them politely, listen to their advice and help them in their daily needs
Speak to them only when necessary
Leave them alone in their old age
Correct them whenever they advise us
mcqs.why: The essay advises greeting elders politely, listening to their advice and helping them in their daily needs, and never being rude to them.

mcqs.q: Which elders does the essay say especially deserve our service in their old age?
options: Only our teachers at school
Only elderly neighbours
Our parents and grandparents
Only elders who are wealthy
mcqs.why: The essay stresses that we must never be rude especially to our parents and grandparents, who deserve our service in their old age.

mcqs.q: What happens to a society that honours its elders, according to the essay?
options: It remains united, wise and blessed
It becomes weak and dependent
It forgets its own traditions
It earns money without any work
mcqs.why: The essay says a society that honours its elders remains united, wise and blessed, while those who ignore elders lose their prayers.

mcqs.q: What does the essay conclude that respecting elders costs and earns?
options: It costs a lot of money but earns fame
It costs time but earns property
It costs nothing, but it earns us their love, their prayers and success in life
It costs nothing and earns nothing at all
mcqs.why: The essay concludes that respecting elders costs nothing, but it earns us their love, their prayers and success in life.
