chapters.title: Unit 13: Letter to the Newspaper Editor

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Glossary

  • Q: Define 'actualities'.
    Ans: The state of something existing in reality; the real facts of a situation.
  • Q: Define 'influence'.
    Ans: The effect that somebody or something has on the way a person thinks or behaves, or on the way that something works or develops.
  • Q: Define 'distortion'.
    Ans: A change in the shape, appearance or sound of something so that it is strange or not clear; in the letter, presenting facts in a twisted and untrue form.
  • Q: Define 'tender'.
    Ans: An offer to carry out work, supply goods, or buy land, shares, or another asset at a stated fixed price.
  • Q: Define 'epidemic'.
    Ans: (Of something bad) occurring more and more frequently in a particular place; a disease spreading widely in an area.
  • Q: Define 'sectarian'.
    Ans: Connected with the differences that exist between groups of people who have different religious views.
  • Q: Define 'communal'.
    Ans: Shared by, or for the use of, a number of people, especially people who live together.
  • Q: Define 'divisive'.
    Ans: Causing people to be split into groups that disagree with or oppose each other.
  • Q: Define 'esteemed'.
    Ans: Held in great respect and admiration; having a good opinion of somebody, as in 'your esteemed paper'.
  • Q: Define 'overseer'.
    Ans: A person whose job is to make sure that other workers do their work; a supervisor or watchdog.

Comprehension A — Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. What is media? Explain with references from text.
    Ans: The word media is derived from 'medium', which means a carrier or mode. Media denotes anything specifically designed to reach a large audience or viewers. The term was first used with the advent of newspapers and magazines, but with the passage of time it broadened with the inventions of radio, TV, cinemas and the Internet. Its duty is to inform, educate and entertain the people, and today it has become almost as necessary as food and clothing.
  • Q: Q2. What is meant by misuse of media? How can it be stopped?
    Ans: Misuse of media means using its great power for wrong purposes: inducing baseless ideas through advertisements and forcing people to buy harmful or substandard products, creating unnecessary sensation and distorting the truth to attract attention, spreading sectarian, communal and divisive trends, and running after money instead of spreading education. It can be stopped if the media performs its noble mission of enlightening people honestly, if the authorities boost its positive influences and curb its negative impacts, and if the government and the general public try their hardest to use the media positively.
  • Q: Q3. How should students take benefits from internet and avoid its bad effects?
    Ans: Students should use the Internet mainly for information and education: for study material, research, learning new skills and knowing the current situation around the world. They should fix a time limit for it and prefer useful websites and educational programmes. To avoid its bad effects, they should stay away from baseless and harmful content, time-wasting entertainment and attractive advertisements of substandard products. They should verify news before believing or sharing it, because media can also distort the truth.
  • Q: Q4. Do you think television is useful source of information? Why.
    Ans: Yes, television is a very useful source of information. It affects the eyes, the ears and the mind simultaneously, so its influence is stronger than that of print alone. It informs people about the latest happenings around them and the world, covering weather, politics, war, health, finance, science, fashion and music. Dedicated news channels let people watch the latest news whenever and wherever they want, and educational programmes can teach thousands of students at a very little cost.
  • Q: Q5. How can media bring about religious harmony?
    Ans: Media can bring about religious harmony by performing its noble mission of enlightening people and by discouraging sectarian, communal and divisive trends, as the letter requests. It reaches a large number of people at the same time, so it can build public opinion in favour of tolerance, unity and mutual respect. If it plays its role honestly, it will be a great force in building the nation and in bringing the common man close to others instead of dividing people into hostile groups.
  • Q: Q6. Find out transitional devices in the text.
    Ans: The transitional devices used in the letter are: Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly, Furthermore, Moreover, Lastly, However and Therefore. Other linking expressions used are 'Since', 'Because of' and 'In perspective of the above actualities'. These devices arrange the writer's points in order and connect one idea smoothly with the next.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'media' mean, according to the lesson?
options: A carrier or mode designed to reach a large audience
A type of newspaper advertisement only
A government department that controls news
A machine used for printing magazines
mcqs.why: The lesson explains that media is derived from 'medium', meaning a carrier or mode, and denotes anything designed to reach a large audience or viewers.

mcqs.q: What is the duty of the media, as stated in the lesson?
options: To sell harmful and substandard products
To create sensation and distort the truth
To run after money instead of spreading education
To inform, educate and entertain the people
mcqs.why: The solved answer states clearly that the duty of media is to inform, educate and entertain the people, and that it has become almost as necessary as food and clothing.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is given as a misuse of media?
options: Informing people about weather and health
Distorting the truth to attract attention and create sensation
Providing educational programmes at little cost
Reporting the latest happenings around the world
mcqs.why: Misuse includes creating unnecessary sensation and distorting the truth to attract attention, along with baseless advertisements and spreading divisive trends.

mcqs.q: Why is television described as a very useful source of information?
options: It affects only the ears, so people can listen while working
It is cheaper than newspapers and magazines
It affects the eyes, the ears and the mind simultaneously
It shows only entertainment and fashion programmes
mcqs.why: Television affects the eyes, the ears and the mind at the same time, so its influence is stronger than print alone and it covers news, weather, health, science and more.

mcqs.q: Which set correctly lists transitional devices used in the letter?
options: Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly, Furthermore, Moreover, Lastly, However, Therefore
Ownership, anticipation, authority, enhancement
Simile, metaphor, personification, imagery
Dear Sir, Yours faithfully, Subject, Date
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly, Furthermore, Moreover, Lastly, However and Therefore as the transitional devices that arrange the points in order.

mcqs.q: What does 'distortion' mean in the letter?
options: Presenting facts in a twisted and untrue form
An offer to carry out work at a fixed price
A disease spreading widely in an area
Something shared by people who live together
mcqs.why: In the glossary, distortion in the letter means presenting facts in a twisted and untrue form, changing them so they are strange or not clear.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'epidemic' mean?
options: Held in great respect and admiration
A disease spreading widely in an area, or something bad occurring more and more frequently
A person who supervises other workers
Causing people to split into disagreeing groups
mcqs.why: The glossary defines epidemic as something bad occurring more and more frequently in a particular place, especially a disease spreading widely in an area.

mcqs.q: In the phrase 'your esteemed paper', what does 'esteemed' mean?
options: Divisive and communal
Twisted and unclear
Held in great respect and admiration
Limited and restricted
mcqs.why: Esteemed means held in great respect and admiration, which is why the writer uses it respectfully for the newspaper in the letter to the editor.

mcqs.q: How can the misuse of media be stopped, according to the lesson?
options: By banning newspapers, radio and television completely
By the media honestly enlightening people while authorities curb its negative impacts
By allowing advertisements of substandard products freely
By stopping all educational programmes on television
mcqs.why: The answer says misuse can be stopped if media performs its noble mission honestly, authorities boost positive influences and curb negative impacts, and the public uses media positively.

mcqs.q: How should students use the Internet to benefit and avoid its bad effects?
options: Use it mainly for study material and research, fix a time limit and verify news before sharing
Spend unlimited time on entertainment and attractive advertisements
Believe and share every news item without checking it
Use it only for buying substandard products online
mcqs.why: Students should use the Internet mainly for information and education, fix a time limit, prefer useful websites, and verify news before believing or sharing it.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A — Meaning and part of speech

  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'ownership'.
    Ans: Meaning: the state or fact of owning something; legal possession of property. Part of speech: Noun (dictionary abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'anticipation'.
    Ans: Meaning: the action of expecting something to happen and looking forward to it; expectation. Part of speech: Noun (dictionary abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'authority'.
    Ans: Meaning: the power or right to give orders, make decisions and control others; a person or body that has this power. Part of speech: Noun (dictionary abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'enhancement'.
    Ans: Meaning: an increase or improvement in the quality, value or extent of something. Part of speech: Noun (dictionary abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'marketing'.
    Ans: Meaning: the activity of promoting and selling products or services, including advertising and market research. Part of speech: Noun (dictionary abbreviation: n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning and part of speech of 'advertisement'.
    Ans: Meaning: a public notice, picture or short film that promotes a product, service or event and tries to persuade people to buy or attend it. Part of speech: Noun (dictionary abbreviation: n.).

Vocabulary B — Antonyms

  • Q: Give an antonym of 'hardest'.
    Ans: easiest
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'truth'.
    Ans: falsehood (also: untruth, lie)
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'substandard'.
    Ans: superior (also: high-quality, above standard)
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'baseless'.
    Ans: well-founded (also: grounded, justified)
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'advantage'.
    Ans: disadvantage
  • Q: Give an antonym of 'extensive'.
    Ans: limited (also: narrow, restricted)

Grammar — Complete the sentences using transition words

  • Q: The dog barked all night ____ the neighbors had no sleep.
    Ans: consequently
  • Q: Humera bought a new dress ____ she also bought shoes and a purse.
    Ans: furthermore
  • Q: The police had no clues for the case ____ tips were still coming in.
    Ans: nonetheless
  • Q: I have five hundred rupees ____ I don't want to spend it.
    Ans: however
  • Q: We got up early this morning ____ we were sleepy all day.
    Ans: therefore
  • Q: The band played her favourite song ____ it was the whole audience's favorite song.
    Ans: indeed
  • Q: Sania forgot about the test ____ she didn't do well on it.
    Ans: as a result
  • Q: They had salad before dinner ____ they were still hungry when the main course arrived.
    Ans: even so

Grammar — Include Quotation Marks Where Needed

  • Q: Q1. Include quotation marks where needed: Javed blurted out, I'll go last, I really don't mind.
    Ans: Javed blurted out, "I'll go last, I really don't mind."
  • Q: Q2. Include quotation marks where needed: Javed said, Nobody else wants to go last.
    Ans: Javed said, "Nobody else wants to go last."
  • Q: Q3. Include quotation marks where needed: Sara stammered, I really don't want to go to bed!
    Ans: Sara stammered, "I really don't want to go to bed!"
  • Q: Q4. Include quotation marks where needed: The odds are, we'll come in last, sighed Abrar, but at least we'll finish.
    Ans: "The odds are, we'll come in last," sighed Abrar, "but at least we'll finish."
  • Q: Q5. Include quotation marks where needed: Do you think the cake is done? Inquired her mother.
    Ans: "Do you think the cake is done?" inquired her mother.

Grammar — Dash or Hyphen

  • Q: Q1. Write whether to use a dash or hyphen, then re-write the sentence: There are thirty five players on the team.
    Ans: Hyphen (compound number). Rewritten: There are thirty-five players on the team.
  • Q: Q2. Write whether to use a dash or hyphen, then re-write the sentence: The Beach Boys (a popular 60's band) gave a performance.
    Ans: Dash (the dash separates a group of words added as an explanation). Rewritten: The Beach Boys — a popular 60's band — gave a performance.
  • Q: Q3. Write whether to use a dash or hyphen, then re-write the sentence: One third of the people did not show up for the event.
    Ans: Hyphen (compound fraction used as one quantity). Rewritten: One-third of the people did not show up for the event.

Grammar — Insert hyphens where needed

  • Q: Q1. Insert hyphens where needed and tell what rule supports the usage: Ali's dad is thirty seven years old.
    Ans: Ali's dad is thirty-seven years old. Rule: compound number.
  • Q: Q2. Insert hyphens where needed and tell what rule supports the usage: Does Khan have a sister in law?
    Ans: Does Khan have a sister-in-law? Rule: compound word.
  • Q: Q3. Insert hyphens where needed and tell what rule supports the usage: Jacky is my well trained dog.
    Ans: Jacky is my well-trained dog. Rule: compound word (compound adjective before a noun).
  • Q: Q4. Insert hyphens where needed and tell what rule supports the usage: This textbook has twenty two chapters.
    Ans: This textbook has twenty-two chapters. Rule: compound number.
  • Q: Q5. Insert hyphens where needed and tell what rule supports the usage: After dinner we visited my great grandmother.
    Ans: After dinner we visited my great-grandmother. Rule: compound word.
  • Q: Q6. Insert hyphens where needed and tell what rule supports the usage: A dash is a punctuation mark used to separate a group of words, not parts of words like a hyphen (the word 'parts' is printed divided across the end of the line).
    Ans: A dash is a punctuation mark used to separate a group of words, not parts of words like a hyphen. (In the book the word 'parts' is itself divided across two lines as 'pa-rts'; the hyphen joins the divided syllables.) Rule: dividing syllables.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning and part of speech of 'ownership'?
options: The activity of promoting products; verb
The state or fact of owning something; noun
The power to give orders; adjective
An improvement in quality; adverb
mcqs.why: Ownership means the state or fact of owning something or legal possession of property, and the lesson identifies it as a noun, abbreviated n.

mcqs.q: What does 'anticipation' mean?
options: The action of expecting something to happen and looking forward to it
The state of owning property legally
A public notice promoting a product
The power to control other people
mcqs.why: Anticipation is defined as the action of expecting something to happen and looking forward to it, that is, expectation, and it is a noun.

mcqs.q: 'Authority' means the power or right to give orders, make decisions and control others. What is its part of speech?
options: Adjective
Adverb
Verb
Noun
mcqs.why: The vocabulary answer gives authority as a noun, abbreviated n., meaning the power or right to give orders, make decisions and control others.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of 'enhancement'?
options: A decrease in the value of something
An increase or improvement in the quality, value or extent of something
The activity of selling products in a market
A notice that persuades people to attend an event
mcqs.why: Enhancement means an increase or improvement in the quality, value or extent of something, and it is listed in the lesson as a noun.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'hardest'?
options: Easiest
Most difficult
Toughest
Strongest
mcqs.why: The antonyms exercise gives easiest as the opposite of hardest, pairing the superlative hardest with its direct opposite in degree.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'truth'?
options: Honesty
Falsehood
Accuracy
Reality
mcqs.why: The lesson gives falsehood, also untruth or lie, as the antonym of truth, because falsehood means the opposite of what is true.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'substandard'?
options: Inferior
Defective
Superior
Below standard
mcqs.why: Substandard means below the required standard, so its antonym given in the lesson is superior, also expressed as high-quality or above standard.

mcqs.q: What is the antonym of 'baseless'?
options: Groundless
Unfounded
Well-founded
Unsupported
mcqs.why: Baseless means without a foundation or reason, so the lesson gives well-founded, grounded or justified as its correct opposite.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence with the correct transition word: 'The dog barked all night ____ the neighbors had no sleep.'
options: Furthermore
Consequently
Nonetheless
Indeed
mcqs.why: Consequently shows a result: because the dog barked all night, the result was that the neighbours had no sleep, as given in the grammar exercise.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: 'Humera bought a new dress ____ she also bought shoes and a purse.'
options: However
Therefore
Furthermore
Even so
mcqs.why: Furthermore adds another related point: besides the new dress, Humera also bought shoes and a purse, so an additive transition is required.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: 'The police had no clues for the case ____ tips were still coming in.'
options: Consequently
As a result
Furthermore
Nonetheless
mcqs.why: Nonetheless means in spite of that: although the police had no clues, tips were still coming in, which is the contrast the sentence expresses.

mcqs.q: Which sentence has quotation marks placed correctly?
options: Javed blurted out, I'll go last, I really don't mind.
Javed blurted out, "I'll go last, I really don't mind."
"Javed blurted out, I'll go last," I really don't mind.
Javed "blurted out," I'll go last, I really don't mind.
mcqs.why: Direct speech must be enclosed in quotation marks, so Javed's exact words, I'll go last, I really don't mind, are placed inside the quotation marks.

mcqs.q: Which sentence has quotation marks placed correctly?
options: Do you think the cake is done? Inquired her mother.
"Do you think the cake is done?" inquired her mother.
Do you think "the cake is done?" inquired her mother.
"Do you think the cake is done? Inquired her mother."
mcqs.why: The question spoken by the mother is direct speech and goes inside quotation marks, while the reporting words inquired her mother stay outside them.

mcqs.q: How should 'There are thirty five players on the team' be rewritten?
options: There are thirty — five players on the team.
There are thirtyfive players on the team.
There are thirty-five players on the team.
There are thirty, five players on the team.
mcqs.why: Thirty-five is a compound number, and compound numbers are joined with a hyphen, not a dash, as the lesson's dash-or-hyphen exercise explains.

mcqs.q: In 'Does Khan have a sister in law?', where are hyphens needed and why?
options: Sister-in-law, because it is a compound word
Sister in-law, because it is a compound number
No hyphen is needed in this sentence
Sister-in law, because it divides syllables
mcqs.why: Sister-in-law is a compound word, and the lesson's rule is that the parts of such a compound word are joined together with hyphens.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Applications, Emails and Letters

  • Q: Q1. State the format of a formal letter as given in the book.
    Ans: A formal letter is written in the following order: 1. Your address (sender's address) at the top. 2. Date. 3. Recipient's address. 4. Greetings, beginning with 'Dear Sir / Madam' etc. 5. Your letter (the body: introduction, main points and conclusion). 6. Closing farewell, such as 'Yours sincerely' or 'Yours faithfully', followed by your name. Formal letters are written to ask for information, to offer thanks, congratulations or condolences, to ask advice or express a view, and to give a reference.
  • Q: Q2. Give the model application printed in the book under 'Writing Applications'.
    Ans: The Principal, Government High School, Hayatabad Peshawar. Subject: Request for a Recreational Trip Sir, With due respect I request you to allow our Grade 9th-A to go to Nathiagali on a recreational trip. Since exams are over, we want to enjoy and relax. It is requested to kindly arrange a recreational trip for us. I shall be very grateful for this act of kindness. Yours obedient student Saad Inam (Monitor) 9th-A Date: Dec. 12, 2017
  • Q: Q3. Compare formal and informal emails as explained in the book.
    Ans: Purpose: a formal email carries business and important messages for business and work colleagues; an informal email carries informal messages for friends and family. Style: a formal email is professional, with accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar, and no slang, exclamation marks or smileys, for example 'Thank you for your prompt response.' An informal email is friendly and accuracy is less important, for example 'Thx 4 email, will call you l8r!' Beginning and ending: a formal email starts and ends appropriately ('Dear Mr/Mrs ...', 'Dear Sir/Madam', and closes with 'Yours sincerely' if you know the name, 'Yours faithfully' if you do not, or 'Regards / Kind regards'); an informal email has no fixed rules and may begin with 'Hi / Hello' and end with 'Best wishes / kind regards / love'. Contractions: formal emails avoid contractions ('I am', 'We are', 'You are', 'Will not', 'Was not'); informal emails freely use them ('I'm', 'We're', 'You're', 'Won't', 'Wasn't').
  • Q: A. Write an application to your principal for remission of fine.
    Ans: The Principal, Government High School, Hayatabad, Peshawar. Subject: Application for Remission of Fine Sir, With due respect, I beg to state that a fine of Rs. 200 has been imposed on me by my class teacher for remaining absent from school for three days last week. I was absent because my mother was seriously ill and there was no one else at home to look after her. My absence was therefore genuine and unavoidable, and my attendance record is otherwise regular and satisfactory. It is, therefore, humbly requested that the fine imposed on me may kindly be remitted. I assure you that I shall be careful and regular in future. I shall be highly grateful for this act of kindness. Yours obediently, Ahmad Ali Class 9th-A, Roll No. 15 Date: March 10, 2018
  • Q: B. Write an email to your friend congratulating him / her on success in exam.
    Ans: From: ahmad.ali@example.com To: bilal.khan@example.com Subject: Congratulations on Your Brilliant Success Hi Bilal, I hope you're fine. I was overjoyed to hear that you have passed your examination with distinction and stood first in your class. Congratulations! Your hard work has truly paid off. I'm so proud of you. Please convey my regards to your parents; they must be very happy too. Let's meet this weekend and celebrate together — the treat is on you this time! Please write soon and tell me about your future plans. Best wishes, Ahmad
  • Q: C. Write an email to Editor of a Newspaper on road accidents and rash driving.
    Ans: From: ahmad.ali@example.com To: The Editor, The Frontier Post, Peshawar Subject: Road Accidents and Rash Driving Dear Sir, I am writing to draw the attention of the authorities and the public, through your esteemed newspaper, to the alarming increase in road accidents caused by rash driving in our city. Every day, young and untrained drivers, overloaded vehicles and motorcyclists without helmets race on busy roads, ignoring traffic signals and speed limits. As a result, precious lives are lost and many people are injured for life. The main causes are careless driving, use of mobile phones while driving, driving without a licence and poor enforcement of traffic rules. I request the traffic police to take strict action against rash drivers, cancel the licences of repeat offenders and launch an awareness campaign, especially for the youth. I also appeal to parents not to hand over vehicles to underage children. I look forward to the publication of this letter in your newspaper. Yours faithfully, Ahmad Ali Hayatabad, Peshawar
  • Q: D. Write a letter to Director, Peshawar Development Authority (PDA) to take measures to improve sanitary conditions in your area. Follow the format of a formal letter.
    Ans: House No. 45, Street No. 3, Hayatabad, Peshawar. March 10, 2018 The Director, Peshawar Development Authority (PDA), Peshawar. Subject: Request to Improve Sanitary Conditions in Our Area Dear Sir, I would like to draw your kind attention to the poor sanitary conditions in our area. Heaps of garbage are lying in the streets and are not removed for weeks. The drains are blocked and overflowing, and dirty water collects on the roads, giving off a foul smell. Stray dogs feed on the waste, and the whole locality is threatened by diseases such as malaria, dengue and cholera. The residents have complained to the local staff many times, but no action has been taken so far. It is requested that your department kindly take immediate measures: regular removal of garbage, cleaning and repair of drains, placement of dustbins at suitable points, and fumigation spray in the area. We shall be grateful for prompt action in this matter. Yours faithfully, Ahmad Ali (Resident, Hayatabad, Peshawar)

mcqs.q: What comes first in the format of a formal letter, as given in the book?
options: The date
The recipient's address
Your address, the sender's address, at the top
The closing farewell and your name
mcqs.why: The formal letter format begins with your address at the top, followed by the date, the recipient's address, the greeting, the body and the closing.

mcqs.q: Which closing is used in a formal letter?
options: Best wishes and love
Yours sincerely or Yours faithfully, followed by your name
Thx 4 your letter, see you l8r
Hi and Hello
mcqs.why: A formal letter ends with a closing farewell such as Yours sincerely or Yours faithfully, followed by the writer's name, as the format answer states.

mcqs.q: In the model application in the book, what does Saad Inam request?
options: Remission of a fine of Rs. 200
Permission for Grade 9th-A to go to Nathiagali on a recreational trip
Improvement of sanitary conditions in Hayatabad
Leave for three days because his mother is ill

mcqs.q: How do formal emails treat contractions, according to the book?
options: They avoid contractions and write I am, We are and Will not in full
They freely use I'm, We're and Won't
They use contractions only in the subject line
They replace contractions with smileys and slang
mcqs.why: Formal emails avoid contractions and write forms in full, such as I am, We are, You are, Will not and Was not, unlike informal emails.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is given as an example of a formal email style?
options: Thx 4 email, will call you l8r!
Thank you for your prompt response.
Hi! See you soon, love Ahmad
Will call u l8r, best wishes
mcqs.why: Thank you for your prompt response is the book's example of formal style: professional, with accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar and no slang.

mcqs.q: In the application for remission of fine, why was Ahmad Ali absent for three days?
options: He had gone on a recreational trip to Nathiagali
His mother was seriously ill and there was no one else at home to look after her
He was preparing for his examinations at home
He was taking part in a school sports competition
mcqs.why: Ahmad Ali states he was absent because his mother was seriously ill and no one else was at home to look after her, so his absence was genuine and unavoidable.

mcqs.q: How much fine was imposed on Ahmad Ali in the remission application?
mcqs.why: The application states that a fine of Rs. 200 was imposed by his class teacher for remaining absent from school for three days last week.

mcqs.q: In the congratulatory email, what success did Bilal achieve?
options: He won a recreational trip to Nathiagali
He passed his examination with distinction and stood first in his class
He was appointed monitor of 9th-A
He got remission of his school fine
mcqs.why: Ahmad congratulates Bilal because he passed his examination with distinction and stood first in his class, and says his hard work has truly paid off.

mcqs.q: According to the email to the Editor on road accidents, which is a main cause of accidents?
options: Wearing helmets and following speed limits
Strict enforcement of traffic rules
Careless driving and use of mobile phones while driving
Cancelling the licences of repeat offenders
mcqs.why: The email lists careless driving, use of mobile phones while driving, driving without a licence and poor enforcement of traffic rules as the main causes.

mcqs.q: In the letter to the Director, PDA, which problem is described in the area?
options: Overloaded vehicles racing on busy roads
Students wasting time on the Internet
Shortage of dustbins in the school only
Heaps of garbage in the streets and blocked, overflowing drains
mcqs.why: The letter describes heaps of garbage lying in the streets for weeks and drains blocked and overflowing, threatening diseases such as malaria, dengue and cholera.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. What is biodiversity?
    Ans: Biodiversity means the variety of all living things — plants, animals and micro-organisms — found in a place, together with the different habitats and ecosystems they live in. The greater the variety of species in an area, the richer its biodiversity is.
  • Q: Q2. What is ecosystem?
    Ans: An ecosystem is a natural system in which living organisms (plants, animals and micro-organisms) interact with each other and with their non-living surroundings, such as water, soil, air and sunlight. A forest, a river and a desert are all examples of ecosystems.
  • Q: Q3. What do you mean by endangered species?
    Ans: Endangered species are species of animals or plants that are in serious danger of becoming extinct, that is, of disappearing from the Earth completely. Their numbers have fallen very low because of hunting, loss of habitat and other threats, so they need special protection to survive.

Glossary

  • Q: Define 'inadequate'.
    Ans: Not enough; not good enough.
  • Q: Define 'engagement'.
    Ans: An arrangement to do something at a particular time, especially something official or something connected with your job.
  • Q: Define 'mainstreaming'.
    Ans: To make a particular idea or opinion accepted by most people.
  • Q: Define 'preserving'.
    Ans: To keep a particular quality, feature, etc.; to make sure that something is kept.
  • Q: Define 'endemic'.
    Ans: Regularly found in a particular place or among a particular group of people and difficult to get rid of.
  • Q: Define 'woodland'.
    Ans: An area of land that is covered with trees.
  • Q: Define 'potential'.
    Ans: That can develop into something or be developed in the future.
  • Q: Define 'diversion'.
    Ans: The act of changing the direction that somebody or something is following, or what something is used for.
  • Q: Define 'cetacean'.
    Ans: A marine mammal of the Order of Cetacea, e.g. a whale, a dolphin, etc.
  • Q: Define 'extirpation'.
    Ans: To remove or destroy totally.

Comprehension — A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Describe the natural beauty of Pakistan.
    Ans: Pakistan is blessed with great natural beauty. It has indigenous wildlife, the beautiful mountains of the Himalayas and K-2, the second tallest mountain in the world, the deserts of Cholistan and Thar, and man-made forests like the Changa Manga forest, besides several natural resources in Balochistan. Four seasons bloom each year to their fullest, and an average rainfall of 12–14 inches per year makes Pakistan a very fertile agricultural land.
  • Q: Q2. How can we preserve Pakistan's fauna and flora?
    Ans: We can preserve Pakistan's fauna and flora by protecting natural habitats, stopping deforestation, overgrazing and poaching, and by using natural resources at sustainable rates instead of over-exploiting them. The government has already short-listed 6 parks for the protection of biodiversity, and Pakistan has 14 National Parks, 99 Wildlife Sanctuaries and 96 Game Reserves for preserving and conserving biodiversity. Public awareness and strict enforcement of wildlife laws are also necessary.
  • Q: Q3. Name some endangered species of animals and plants in Pakistan.
    Ans: Endangered animals in Pakistan include the snow leopard, small populations of tigers in the lower subtropical regions, the Asian elephant, hog deer, Asiatic wild ass, woolly flying squirrel, Kashmir musk deer and the fishing cat. The markhor, the national animal, is also on the brink of extinction, while the red-headed vulture is the bird most at risk of extinction and the Indus River dolphin is a seriously threatened freshwater species. Among plants, the juniper forests of Balochistan, one of the oldest juniper ecosystems of the world, are threatened by the parasitic dwarf mistletoe.
  • Q: Q4. Search the internet and find about the endangered peacocks.
    Ans: The peacock found in Pakistan is the Indian peafowl, which lives mainly in the Tharparkar area of Sindh, where it is loved and protected by local people as a symbol of beauty. In recent years its numbers have fallen because of hunting, collection of its eggs, loss of its desert habitat and outbreaks of viral diseases, which killed large numbers of peacocks in Thar. Because of these threats the peacock is treated as an endangered and protected bird in Pakistan, and hunting it is banned.
  • Q: Q5. How can we contribute as individuals to save nature?
    Ans: As individuals we can plant trees and protect the ones already growing, avoid wasting water, and keep our surroundings clean. We should never hunt or buy products made from endangered animals, and we should discourage others from cutting trees or harming wildlife. By spreading awareness in our families and communities and supporting national parks and conservation efforts, each of us can help save nature.
  • Q: Q6. What type of challenges is Pakistan facing while preserving nature?
    Ans: Pakistan faces many challenges in preserving nature. These include political instability, lack of technical and institutional capacity, lack of financial resources, lack of awareness, insufficient access to local knowledge and legal impediments. Limited public and stakeholder participation, lack of mainstreaming of biodiversity with other sectors, lack of transfer of technology and expertise, inadequate engagement of the scientific community, poverty, increasing population, climate change and natural disasters are the other major challenges named in the lesson.

mcqs.q: What is biodiversity?
options: The variety of all living things in a place, together with their habitats and ecosystems
Only the variety of animals found in a forest
The study of mountains and deserts only
A list of endangered animals in Pakistan
mcqs.why: Biodiversity means the variety of all living things, plants, animals and micro-organisms, in a place together with the different habitats and ecosystems they live in.

mcqs.q: What is an ecosystem?
options: A national park protected by the government
A natural system where living organisms interact with each other and their non-living surroundings
A place where only micro-organisms can survive
A man-made forest planted for timber
mcqs.why: An ecosystem is a natural system in which living organisms interact with each other and with non-living surroundings such as water, soil, air and sunlight.

mcqs.q: What are endangered species?
options: Species that are found regularly in one place
Species kept safely in national parks
Species that have become extinct long ago
Species in serious danger of becoming extinct, whose numbers have fallen very low
mcqs.why: Endangered species are animals or plants in serious danger of becoming extinct because their numbers have fallen very low through hunting and loss of habitat.

mcqs.q: Which facts about Pakistan's natural beauty are stated in the lesson?
options: K-2 is the tallest mountain in the world and rainfall is 30 inches a year
K-2 is the second tallest mountain in the world and average rainfall is 12-14 inches per year
Pakistan has no deserts and no man-made forests
Balochistan has no natural resources at all
mcqs.why: The lesson names the Himalayas and K-2, the second tallest mountain in the world, the Cholistan and Thar deserts, Changa Manga forest and 12-14 inches of average yearly rainfall.

mcqs.q: How many National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries and Game Reserves does Pakistan have, according to the lesson?
options: 6 National Parks, 14 Sanctuaries and 96 Reserves
14 National Parks, 99 Wildlife Sanctuaries and 96 Game Reserves
99 National Parks, 96 Sanctuaries and 14 Reserves
14 National Parks, 14 Sanctuaries and 14 Reserves
mcqs.why: The solved answer states Pakistan has 14 National Parks, 99 Wildlife Sanctuaries and 96 Game Reserves for preserving and conserving biodiversity.

mcqs.q: Which bird is described as most at risk of extinction, and which animal is Pakistan's national animal?
options: The peacock is most at risk; the snow leopard is the national animal
The red-headed vulture is most at risk; the markhor is the national animal
The fishing cat is most at risk; the Asian elephant is the national animal
The woolly flying squirrel is most at risk; the hog deer is the national animal
mcqs.why: The lesson says the red-headed vulture is the bird most at risk of extinction, while the markhor, the national animal, is also on the brink of extinction.

mcqs.q: What threatens the juniper forests of Balochistan?
options: The parasitic dwarf mistletoe
Overgrazing by markhors only
The Indus River dolphin
Dwarf forests planted in Changa Manga
mcqs.why: Among plants, the juniper forests of Balochistan, one of the oldest juniper ecosystems in the world, are threatened by the parasitic dwarf mistletoe.

mcqs.q: What is the peacock found in Pakistan, and where does it mainly live?
options: The green peafowl, living mainly in Changa Manga forest
The Indian peafowl, living mainly in the Tharparkar area of Sindh
The Indian peafowl, living mainly in Chitral Valley
The white peafowl, living mainly in Balochistan
mcqs.why: The peacock found in Pakistan is the Indian peafowl, which lives mainly in the Tharparkar area of Sindh, where local people love and protect it.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is named as a challenge Pakistan faces in preserving nature?
options: Too much public awareness about biodiversity
Political instability and lack of financial resources
Excess transfer of technology and expertise
A decreasing population and stable climate
mcqs.why: The challenges named include political instability, lack of technical and institutional capacity, lack of financial resources, lack of awareness and legal impediments.

mcqs.q: What does 'cetacean' mean?
options: A parasitic plant that feeds on juniper trees
An area of land covered with trees
A marine mammal of the order Cetacea, such as a whale or dolphin
Something that can develop in the future
mcqs.why: The glossary defines a cetacean as a marine mammal of the Order Cetacea, for example a whale or a dolphin.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — B. Find the meaning of the following words from the dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviation used

  • Q: Give the meaning of 'threat' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: a statement of an intention to inflict pain, injury, damage or other hostile action on someone; a person or thing likely to cause damage or danger. Part of speech: Noun (n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'specie' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: money in the form of coins rather than notes. (Note: 'specie' is different from 'species', which means a group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals.) Part of speech: Noun (n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'financial' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: relating to money or how money is managed. Part of speech: Adjective (adj.).
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'stakeholder' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: a person or group that has an interest in, or is affected by, an organisation, project or activity, such as the conservation of biodiversity. Part of speech: Noun (n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'parasite' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: an animal or plant that lives in or on another animal or plant of a different species and feeds from it. Part of speech: Noun (n.).
  • Q: Give the meaning of 'exposed' and identify its part of speech.
    Ans: Meaning: not protected or covered; left open to harm, weather or view. Part of speech: Adjective (adj.); it is also the past tense and past participle of the verb 'expose'.

Vocabulary — C. Consult a thesaurus and find out the synonyms of the following words

  • Q: Give a synonym of 'endangered'.
    Ans: Threatened; at risk; in danger of extinction.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'entrapment'.
    Ans: Trapping; capture; snaring.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'extirpation'.
    Ans: Destruction; extermination; complete removal.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'restricted'.
    Ans: Limited; confined; controlled.
  • Q: Give a synonym of 'preserve'.
    Ans: Conserve; protect; save; keep safe.

Grammar — Parentheses: Re-write the following sentences placing parenthesis in the correct place

  • Q: Q1. My mother likes although I don't know why old folk music.
    Ans: My mother likes (although I don't know why) old folk music.
  • Q: Q2. All tiger species especially the South China tiger are endangered.
    Ans: All tiger species (especially the South China tiger) are endangered.
  • Q: Q3. I'll get back to you tomorrow Friday.
    Ans: I'll get back to you tomorrow (Friday).
  • Q: Q4. Which country countries do you want to visit?
    Ans: Which country (countries) do you want to visit?
  • Q: Q5. You put fifty-four 54 books on that shelf.
    Ans: You put fifty-four (54) books on that shelf.

Grammar — Ellipsis: Rewrite each sentence below omitting text and using an ellipsis

  • Q: Q1. We were cautioned by the 8th grade World History teacher Mrs. Petersen not to run in the halls.
    Ans: We were cautioned by Mrs. Petersen ... not to run in the halls.
  • Q: Q2. The important point to make, and I cannot say it too often, is that music and art are important factors in a culture.
    Ans: The important point to make ... is that music and art are important factors in a culture.
  • Q: Q3. He couldn't run fast enough, although he tried with all his might, to catch the carriage as it travelled down the road.
    Ans: He couldn't run fast enough ... to catch the carriage as it travelled down the road.
  • Q: Q4. I thought the party was nice.
    Ans: I thought the party was nice ... (The sentence has no extra words to omit, so the ellipsis is used at the end to show a trailing, unfinished thought, as explained in the lesson.)
  • Q: Q5. Abrar said, "There's nothing inside."
    Ans: Abrar said, "There's nothing inside ..." (The sentence has no extra words to omit, so the ellipsis is used inside the quotation to show a pause or hesitation, as explained in the lesson.)

mcqs.q: What does 'threat' mean, and what is its part of speech?
options: Money in the form of coins; adjective
A statement of intention to inflict pain, injury or damage; noun
Relating to money management; verb
A person interested in a project; adverb
mcqs.why: Threat means a statement of an intention to inflict pain, injury, damage or other hostile action, and the lesson identifies it as a noun, abbreviated n.

mcqs.q: What does 'specie' mean?
options: A group of similar living organisms
Money in the form of coins rather than notes
A plant that feeds on another plant
A danger to wildlife and nature
mcqs.why: Specie means money in the form of coins rather than notes, and the lesson warns it is different from species, which means a group of similar living organisms.

mcqs.q: 'Financial' means relating to money or how money is managed. What is its part of speech?
options: Noun
Verb
Adjective
Adverb
mcqs.why: Financial is identified in the lesson as an adjective, abbreviated adj., because it describes things relating to money or how money is managed.

mcqs.q: What is a 'stakeholder'?
options: An animal that lives on another animal and feeds from it
A person or group that has an interest in, or is affected by, an organisation, project or activity
A marine mammal such as a whale or dolphin
Land that is covered with trees
mcqs.why: A stakeholder is a person or group that has an interest in, or is affected by, an organisation, project or activity such as the conservation of biodiversity.

mcqs.q: What does 'parasite' mean?
options: Something not protected or covered
A synonym of the word preserve
An animal or plant that lives in or on another of a different species and feeds from it
A person who supervises a conservation project
mcqs.why: A parasite is an animal or plant that lives in or on another animal or plant of a different species and feeds from it, and it is a noun.

mcqs.q: What does 'exposed' mean?
options: Kept safe and fully covered
Not protected or covered; left open to harm, weather or view
Regularly found in a particular place
Removed or destroyed totally
mcqs.why: Exposed means not protected or covered and left open to harm, weather or view; it is an adjective and also the past form of the verb expose.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'endangered'?
options: Threatened; at risk; in danger of extinction
Trapping and capture
Limited and confined
Conserved and protected
mcqs.why: The thesaurus exercise gives threatened, at risk and in danger of extinction as synonyms of endangered, all showing a species faces possible disappearance.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'entrapment'?
options: Destruction and extermination
Trapping; capture; snaring
Protection and conservation
Restriction and control
mcqs.why: Entrapment means trapping, capture or snaring, as the thesaurus exercise states, all referring to catching something in a trap.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'extirpation'?
options: Preservation
Protection
Destruction; extermination; complete removal
Limitation
mcqs.why: Extirpation means destruction, extermination or complete removal, matching the glossary definition to remove or destroy totally.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'restricted'?
options: Endangered
Trapped
Destroyed
Limited; confined; controlled
mcqs.why: Restricted means limited, confined or controlled, as given in the thesaurus exercise, because all these words show something kept within limits.

mcqs.q: What is a synonym of 'preserve'?
options: Conserve; protect; save; keep safe
Destroy; exterminate; remove
Trap; capture; snare
Expose; uncover; endanger
mcqs.why: Preserve means conserve, protect, save or keep safe, which matches the lesson's aim of keeping biodiversity safe for the future.

mcqs.q: Which sentence places parentheses correctly?
options: My mother likes although I don't know why (old folk music).
(My mother likes) although I don't know why old folk music.
My mother likes (although I don't know why) old folk music.
My mother (likes although) I don't know why old folk music.
mcqs.why: The added explanation although I don't know why is the parenthetical part, so it is enclosed in parentheses inside the main sentence about old folk music.

mcqs.q: Which sentence places parentheses correctly?
options: You put fifty-four 54 (books) on that shelf.
You put fifty-four (54) books on that shelf.
(You put) fifty-four 54 books on that shelf.
You put (fifty-four 54 books) on that shelf.
mcqs.why: The figure 54 repeats the written number fifty-four as extra information, so it is placed in parentheses immediately after the written number.

mcqs.q: Which rewrite correctly uses an ellipsis to omit text? Original: 'We were cautioned by the 8th grade World History teacher Mrs. Petersen not to run in the halls.'
options: We were cautioned by Mrs. Petersen ... not to run in the halls.
We were cautioned ... by the 8th grade teacher Mrs. Petersen not ...
... We were cautioned by Mrs. Petersen not to run in the halls
We were cautioned by Mrs. Petersen not to run in the halls ... today
mcqs.why: The ellipsis replaces the omitted descriptive words about the teacher, keeping Mrs. Petersen and the warning not to run in the halls, as in the solved answer.

mcqs.q: In 'I thought the party was nice ...', what does the ellipsis at the end show?
options: That a number has been repeated in figures
A trailing, unfinished thought
That a compound word has been joined
That direct speech is being quoted
mcqs.why: The lesson explains that when there are no extra words to omit, an ellipsis at the end shows a trailing, unfinished thought by the speaker.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: A. Write description of Chitral Valley with the help of the given mind map (Describing Places).
    Ans: Chitral Valley is one of the most beautiful valleys of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, lying in the north of Pakistan among the high peaks of the Hindu Kush. If we observe it carefully, we see a narrow green valley through which the Chitral River flows, with terraced fields, orchards of apples, apricots and walnuts, and small villages of stone and wooden houses on both sides. The people of Chitral are peaceful, hospitable and hardworking; they speak Khowar and are famous for their colourful caps, embroidered coats and the lively game of polo played at Shandur, the highest polo ground in the world. The valley is crowned by Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, whose snow-covered top shines above the town. Chitral is significant not only for its scenery but also for its unique Kalash culture, its rich wildlife including the markhor, and its importance as a gateway to the mountain passes of the north. A visit to Chitral leaves a lasting impression of natural beauty and warm hospitality.
  • Q: C. Write a persuasive/argumentative essay on Preservation of Nature.
    Ans: Preservation of Nature Nature is the greatest blessing of Allah for mankind, yet today its survival has become a controversial issue: some people argue that development must come first, while others insist that nature must be protected at all costs. In my clear opinion, preservation of nature must be our first priority, because our life depends on it, because countless species are vanishing, and because a healthy environment is the best gift we can leave for the next generation. First, human life itself depends on nature. Forests give us oxygen and rainfall, rivers give us water, and fertile land gives us food. Pakistan, with its mountains, deserts, forests and the Indus River, is fertile precisely because of this natural balance; if we destroy it, our agriculture and our lives will suffer. Second, our wildlife is disappearing at an alarming rate. The snow leopard, the markhor, the red-headed vulture and the Indus River dolphin are all threatened or endangered because of poaching, deforestation and loss of habitat. Once a species becomes extinct, no wealth can bring it back, so protecting it today is our moral duty. Third, preserving nature is an investment in the future. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries and game reserves not only protect biodiversity but also promote tourism and research. If we fail to act now, as the lesson warns, the next generation will see biodiversity only in pictures, movies and stuffed toys. In conclusion, life, species and the future all demand the same action: preserve nature. The government must enforce conservation laws strictly, and every citizen must plant trees, save water and protect wildlife. Let us act today, before it is too late.

mcqs.q: Where does Chitral Valley lie, according to the description?
options: In the south of Pakistan, in the Thar desert
In the north of Pakistan among the high peaks of the Hindu Kush
On the coast of Balochistan near the sea
In the plains of Punjab near Changa Manga
mcqs.why: The description says Chitral Valley lies in the north of Pakistan among the high peaks of the Hindu Kush and is one of the most beautiful valleys of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

mcqs.q: Which river flows through Chitral Valley?
options: The Indus River
The Chitral River
The Ravi River
The Beas River
mcqs.why: The description observes a narrow green valley through which the Chitral River flows, with terraced fields and orchards on both sides.

mcqs.q: What is Tirich Mir in the description of Chitral?
options: The highest polo ground in the world
A famous Kalash festival of the valley
The highest peak of the Hindu Kush, whose snow-covered top shines above the town
A river that flows through the valley
mcqs.why: Tirich Mir is described as the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, crowning the valley with its snow-covered top shining above the town.

mcqs.q: What language do the people of Chitral speak, according to the description?
options: Pashto
Khowar
Sindhi
Balochi
mcqs.why: The description states the people of Chitral speak Khowar and are famous for their colourful caps, embroidered coats and the game of polo at Shandur.

mcqs.q: What is special about Shandur in the Chitral description?
options: It has the oldest juniper forests in the world
It is the highest polo ground in the world
It is the gateway used by the Indus dolphin
It is where the Kalash people grow walnuts only
mcqs.why: Shandur is named in the description as the highest polo ground in the world, where the lively game of polo associated with Chitral is played.

mcqs.q: What is the writer's clear opinion in the essay 'Preservation of Nature'?
options: Development must always come before nature
Nature should be protected only after all building work
Preservation of nature must be our first priority
Species protection is not a moral duty
mcqs.why: The writer states clearly that preservation of nature must be our first priority because our life depends on it, species are vanishing and the environment is a gift for the next generation.

mcqs.q: According to the essay, why does human life itself depend on nature?
options: Forests give oxygen and rainfall, rivers give water and fertile land gives food
Nature provides only scenery for tourists and photographers
Nature gives people stuffed toys and movies
Nature is needed only for polo grounds and orchards
mcqs.why: The essay argues that forests give oxygen and rainfall, rivers give water and fertile land gives food, so destroying the natural balance would harm agriculture and life.

mcqs.q: Which warning ends the argument about the future in the essay?
options: The next generation will see biodiversity only in pictures, movies and stuffed toys
The next generation will build more national parks automatically
Species once extinct can be brought back with wealth
Tourism will replace the need for conservation laws
mcqs.why: The essay warns that if we fail to act now, the next generation will see biodiversity only in pictures, movies and stuffed toys, exactly as the lesson warns.

mcqs.q: What does the essay say about a species once it becomes extinct?
options: It can be restored by planting more trees
It can be bought back from other countries
No wealth can bring it back, so protecting it today is our moral duty
It returns on its own after a few years
mcqs.why: The essay stresses that once a species becomes extinct, no wealth can bring it back, so protecting threatened species today is our moral duty.

mcqs.q: What action does the conclusion of the essay demand?
options: The government must enforce conservation laws strictly and every citizen must plant trees, save water and protect wildlife
Citizens should wait for tourists to protect nature
Only scientists should work for nature preservation
Development projects should replace national parks
mcqs.why: The conclusion demands strict enforcement of conservation laws by the government and action by every citizen to plant trees, save water and protect wildlife.
