lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Q1. Who was Abou Ben Adhem?
    Ans: Abou Ben Adhem was a pious and kind-hearted man, the hero of Leigh Hunt's poem. In the poem he is shown as a man of deep peace who loved his fellow human beings so sincerely that, although his name was not in the angel's list of those who love the Lord, his name led all the rest in the list of those whom love of God had blessed.

Glossary

  • Q: Define 'peace'.
    Ans: Serenity; mental solace.
  • Q: Define 'bloom'.
    Ans: A flower (usually one on a plant that people admire for its flowers).
  • Q: Define 'writest'.
    Ans: Writes; writing (an old form of 'you write').
  • Q: Define 'thou'.
    Ans: A word meaning 'you', used when talking to only one person who is the subject of the verb (an old form of 'you').
  • Q: Define 'blest'.
    Ans: To ask God to protect somebody or something; the second form of 'bless' (an old form of 'blessed').
  • Q: Define 'vanish'.
    Ans: To disappear suddenly and/or in a way that you cannot explain.
  • Q: Define 'raised'.
    Ans: At a higher level than normal; lifted up.

Comprehension — A. Read out the text and answer the following questions

  • Q: Q1. Why was Abou Ben Adhem's name on top of the list?
    Ans: Abou Ben Adhem's name was on top of the list because he truly loved his fellow men. When the angel told him his name was not among those who love the Lord, he humbly asked to be written as one who loves his fellow men, and the next night the angel showed that his name led all the rest in the list of those whom love of God had blessed. This proves that loving mankind is the truest way of loving God.
  • Q: Q2. What is the main idea of the poem?
    Ans: The main idea of the poem is that the love of mankind is the highest form of the love of God. A person who sincerely loves and serves his fellow human beings is loved and blessed by God even more than those known only for their devotion. True religion, the poem teaches, lies in love and service of humanity.
  • Q: Q3. Describe the character of Abou Ben Adhem in your own words.
    Ans: Abou Ben Adhem is a pious, peaceful and fearless man. The exceeding peace in his heart made him bold enough to question the angel, yet he remained humble and cheerful when he learnt that his name was not in the list. Above all, he is kind and selfless: his one wish is to be counted among those who love their fellow men, which shows the purity and generosity of his character.
  • Q: Q4. Write down the implied and explicit meanings of the poem.
    Ans: The explicit (directly stated) meaning of the poem is the story itself: Abou Ben Adhem wakes up, sees an angel writing the names of those who love the Lord, finds his own name missing, asks to be written as one who loves his fellow men, and the next night finds his name at the top of the list of the blessed. The implied (hidden) meaning is the moral: loving and serving human beings is the best proof of loving God, and God blesses most those who love mankind.
  • Q: Q5. Mention the other words used by the poet to refer to the angel.
    Ans: Besides the word 'angel', the poet refers to the angel as 'the presence in the room' and as 'the vision'. These words describe the angel as a bright, dream-like presence rather than an ordinary person.
  • Q: Q6. Give brief description of the angel in Abou Ben Adhem.
    Ans: The angel appears in Abou Ben Adhem's room in the moonlight, making the room rich and bright like a lily in bloom, and is seen writing in a book of gold. It speaks with a look made of all sweet accord, that is, with complete gentleness and harmony. It answers Abou's questions calmly, writes his request, vanishes, and returns the next night with a great wakening light.

Comprehension — B. Choose the correct option

  • Q: Q1. The poet says, 'may his tribe increase', it means:
    Options: that the number of Abou Ben Adhem's children should increase / that the number of people in Adhem's country should increase / that the number of good people like Abou Ben Adhem should increase / the number of bad people unlike Abou Ben Adhem should increase
    Ans: that the number of good people like Abou Ben Adhem should increase
  • Q: Q2. The words like 'lily in bloom' is:
    Options: simile / metaphor / personification / imagery
    Ans: simile
  • Q: Q3. The name of Abou Ben Adhem was on the top of the list because he:
    Options: loved dreams / loved wealth / loved fellow human beings / loved peace
    Ans: loved fellow human beings
  • Q: Q4. Abou Ben Adhem's room look beautiful and bright because of
    Options: the presence of bright moonlight / the presence of an angel in the room / the blooming lilies in the room / his good deeds
    Ans: the presence of an angel in the room
  • Q: Q5. Abou Ben Adhem 'spoke more low' these words means: Abou Ben Adhem spoke
    Options: boldly / humbly / slowly / firmly
    Ans: humbly

mcqs.q: The poet says, 'may his tribe increase', it means:
options: that the number of Abou Ben Adhem's children should increase
that the number of people in Adhem's country should increase
that the number of good people like Abou Ben Adhem should increase
the number of bad people unlike Abou Ben Adhem should increase
mcqs.why: The prayer means that good people like Abou Ben Adhem, who love their fellow men, should increase in number, not merely his children or countrymen.

mcqs.q: The words like 'lily in bloom' is:
options: metaphor
simile
personification
imagery
mcqs.why: The phrase uses the word like to compare the brightness of the angel's presence in the moonlit room to a blooming lily, which makes it a simile.

mcqs.q: The name of Abou Ben Adhem was on the top of the list because he:
options: loved dreams
loved wealth
loved peace
loved fellow human beings
mcqs.why: Abou led all the rest because he truly loved his fellow men, and the poem teaches that loving mankind is the truest way of loving God.

mcqs.q: Abou Ben Adhem's room look beautiful and bright because of
options: the presence of bright moonlight
the blooming lilies in the room
the presence of an angel in the room
his good deeds
mcqs.why: The room became rich and bright like a lily in bloom because of the angel's presence in the moonlight, writing in a book of gold.

mcqs.q: Abou Ben Adhem 'spoke more low' these words means: Abou Ben Adhem spoke
options: boldly
slowly
humbly
firmly
mcqs.why: Spoke more low means he spoke humbly and in a lower voice, yet cheerfully, when he asked to be written as one who loves his fellow men.

mcqs.q: Who was Abou Ben Adhem?
options: A pious and kind-hearted man, the hero of Leigh Hunt's poem
A king who ruled over a large tribe
An angel who wrote in a book of gold
A poet who wrote about the moonlight
mcqs.why: The pre-reading answer describes Abou Ben Adhem as a pious and kind-hearted man and the hero of Leigh Hunt's poem, a man of deep peace who loved his fellow beings.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the poem?
options: Love of wealth is the highest form of devotion
Love of mankind is the highest form of the love of God
Dreams reveal the names of the blessed
Peace makes a man bold enough to question angels
mcqs.why: The main idea is that love of mankind is the highest form of love of God, and true religion lies in love and service of humanity.

mcqs.q: Besides the word 'angel', which words does the poet use to refer to the angel?
options: 'The presence in the room' and 'the vision'
'The moonlight' and 'the lily'
'The book of gold' and 'the light'
'The tribe' and 'the rest'
mcqs.why: The comprehension answer states the poet also calls the angel the presence in the room and the vision, describing a bright, dream-like presence.

mcqs.q: How is the angel described in the poem?
options: Writing in a book of gold, with a look made of all sweet accord
Carrying a sword and speaking in anger
Standing silently outside the room in darkness
Holding a lily and a list of wealthy men
mcqs.why: The angel is seen in the moonlight writing in a book of gold and speaks with a look made of all sweet accord, that is, complete gentleness and harmony.

mcqs.q: What does the old word 'thou' mean in the poem?
options: Writes or writing
Blessed, in an old form
You, used when talking to one person who is the subject of the verb
Serenity and mental solace
mcqs.why: The glossary explains thou is an old form of you, used when talking to only one person who is the subject of the verb.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • Q: A. Which lines of the poem indicate imagery?
    Ans: Imagery is the use of words that create a picture in the reader's mind. The lines 'And saw, within the moonlight in his room, / Making it rich, and like a lily in bloom, / An angel writing in a book of gold' create a clear visual image of the bright, beautiful room. The line 'It came again with a great wakening light' is another example of visual imagery in the poem.
  • Q: B. Pick out rhyming words from the poem.
    Ans: The poem is written in rhyming couplets. The rhyming words are: increase — peace; room — bloom; gold — bold; said — head; accord — Lord; so — low; still — (the couplet continues) then — men; night — light; blest — rest.
  • Q: C. Identify different figures of speech from the poem.
    Ans: Simile: 'like a lily in bloom' — the angel's brightness in the moonlit room is compared to a blooming lily using the word 'like'. Personification: the vision (angel) is given human qualities — it raises its head, looks and answers questions; peace is also personified in 'Exceeding peace had made Ben Adhem bold', where peace is shown as acting upon him. Imagery: the moonlight, the book of gold and the 'great wakening light' appeal to the sense of sight. Metaphor is used in a mild form in 'a look made of all sweet accord', where the angel's look is described as if it were made of harmony itself.

Grammar — A. Change the following into indirect speech

  • Q: Q1. The girl said, "It gives me great pleasure to be here this evening."
    Ans: The girl said that it gave her great pleasure to be there that evening.
  • Q: Q2. The man said, "I must go as soon as possible."
    Ans: The man said that he had to go as soon as possible.
  • Q: Q3. She said, "I don't want to see any of you; go away."
    Ans: She said that she did not want to see any of them and ordered them to go away.
  • Q: Q4. The teacher says, "If you work hard, you will pass."
    Ans: The teacher says that if you work hard, you will pass. (The reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense, so the tense of the reported speech does not change.)
  • Q: Q5. He said, "I have won."
    Ans: He said that he had won.
  • Q: Q6. He said, "Let's wait for her return."
    Ans: He suggested that they should wait for her return.
  • Q: Q7. Alice said, "How clever I am!"
    Ans: Alice exclaimed with joy that she was very clever.
  • Q: Q8. "Which way did she go?" asked the young man.
    Ans: The young man asked which way she had gone.
  • Q: Q9. He said to me, "Where are you going?"
    Ans: He asked me where I was going.
  • Q: Q10. "Please wait here till I return," she told him.
    Ans: She requested him to wait there till she returned.

Grammar — B. Change the following into direct speech

  • Q: Q1. She told her mother that she was going to the market.
    Ans: She said to her mother, "I am going to the market."
  • Q: Q2. His friends told me that they would go home the following Sunday.
    Ans: His friends said to me, "We will go home next Sunday."
  • Q: Q3. The teacher told he had been very regular in his work.
    Ans: The teacher said, "He has been very regular in his work."
  • Q: Q4. Zarak Khan told me that he had finished his work.
    Ans: Zarak Khan said to me, "I have finished my work."
  • Q: Q5. The teacher said the earth moves around the sun.
    Ans: The teacher said, "The earth moves around the sun." (A universal truth remains in the present tense in both forms.)
  • Q: Q6. He said that she was not going home that day.
    Ans: He said, "She is not going home today."
  • Q: Q7. He asked me if I had brought the pens.
    Ans: He said to me, "Have you brought the pens?"
  • Q: Q8. The boy asked me if that was the place we had visited before.
    Ans: The boy said to me, "Is this the place we visited before?"
  • Q: Q9. The judge told the witness to tell the truth.
    Ans: The judge said to the witness, "Tell the truth."
  • Q: Q10. The prisoner begged the judge to forgive him.
    Ans: The prisoner begged the judge, "Please forgive me."

Revision — Exercise 1: Insert quotation marks where needed

  • Q: Q1. She's been known to sing beautifully, commented Ali.
    Ans: "She's been known to sing beautifully," commented Ali.
  • Q: Q2. The blog entry she posted is called easy recipes.
    Ans: The blog entry she posted is called "Easy Recipes."
  • Q: Q3. The talent show begins immediately after lunch, said Ibrar.
    Ans: "The talent show begins immediately after lunch," said Ibrar.
  • Q: Q4. Did you see the talent show? asked Jan?
    Ans: "Did you see the talent show?" asked Jan.
  • Q: Q5. There might be a rainbow after the rainfall, said our teacher.
    Ans: "There might be a rainbow after the rainfall," said our teacher.

Revision — Exercise 2: Insert hyphens where needed and tell what rule supports the usage

  • Q: Q1. On our way to the vacation of our dreams, we noticed several hitch hikers.
    Ans: On our way to the vacation of our dreams, we noticed several hitch-hikers. Rule: compound word.
  • Q: Q2. When you are proofreading your writing, always remember to put punctuation where needed.
    Ans: When you are proofreading your writing, always remember to put punctuation where needed. No hyphen is needed: 'proofreading' is written as one complete word.
  • Q: Q3. When Irum was twenty nine years old, she got married in Peshawar.
    Ans: When Irum was twenty-nine years old, she got married in Peshawar. Rule: compound number.
  • Q: Q4. The student who studies days in advance usually does excellent on a test.
    Ans: The student who studies days in advance usually does excellent on a test. No hyphen is needed in this sentence.
  • Q: Q5. There are many people that feel self-confident about speaking in front of large crowds.
    Ans: There are many people that feel self-confident about speaking in front of large crowds. The hyphen is already correctly used. Rule: compound word.

Revision — Exercise 3: Rewrite each sentence below omitting text and using an ellipsis

  • Q: Q1. The children played in the playground on all the equipment including the swings, the slide, the monkey bars, and the merry-go-round.
    Ans: The children played in the playground on all the equipment including the swings ...
  • Q: Q2. When we think about it carefully, and we should be careful to think about it, the use of punctuation is a science and an art.
    Ans: When we think about it carefully ... the use of punctuation is a science and an art.
  • Q: Q3. The dog looked at the large cat and then looked away.
    Ans: The dog looked at the ... cat and then looked away.
  • Q: Q4. "No, no, no, no!" exclaimed Horace.
    Ans: "No, no ..." exclaimed Horace. (The repeated words are omitted and the ellipsis shows his speech trailing off.)
  • Q: Q5. The flower arrangement was unusual.
    Ans: The flower arrangement was unusual ... (The sentence has no extra words to omit, so the ellipsis is used at the end to show a trailing, unfinished thought.)

Revision — Exercise 4: Rewrite each sentence placing parentheses in the correct places

  • Q: Q1. I wanted to go on Monday my day off! but no one else did.
    Ans: I wanted to go on Monday (my day off!) but no one else did.
  • Q: Q2. Belize formerly British Honduras is in Central America.
    Ans: Belize (formerly British Honduras) is in Central America.
  • Q: Q3. If you want to be healthy, you must 1 eat good food, 2 get sufficient exercise, and 3 get adequate sleep.
    Ans: If you want to be healthy, you must (1) eat good food, (2) get sufficient exercise, and (3) get adequate sleep.
  • Q: Q4. I need 100 hundred rupees for few days.
    Ans: I need one hundred (100) rupees for few days.
  • Q: Q5. That movie reminded me I remember it well about the adventure we had.
    Ans: That movie reminded me (I remember it well) about the adventure we had.

Revision — Exercise 5: Change the following sentences into indirect speech

  • Q: Q1. He said, "I have got a toothache".
    Ans: He said that he had got a toothache.
  • Q: Q2. Manahil said, "I am very busy now".
    Ans: Manahil said that she was very busy then.
  • Q: Q3. "Hurry up," she said to us.
    Ans: She urged us to hurry up.
  • Q: Q4. "Give me a cup of water," he told her.
    Ans: He told her to give him a cup of water.
  • Q: Q5. She said, "I am going to college."
    Ans: She said that she was going to college.

mcqs.q: Which lines of the poem are given as an example of imagery?
options: 'Know thyself and success shall be thine'
'And saw, within the moonlight in his room, making it rich, and like a lily in bloom, an angel writing in a book of gold'
'I wandered lonely as a cloud'
'Hope is the thing with feathers'
mcqs.why: Those lines create a clear visual picture of the bright room, the moonlight and the angel writing in a book of gold, which is visual imagery as explained in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Which pair is a rhyming pair from the poem?
options: Increase - peace
Gold - men
Night - blest
Room - Lord
mcqs.why: The poem is written in rhyming couplets, and the vocabulary answer lists increase and peace as the rhyming words of the opening couplet.

mcqs.q: In 'Exceeding peace had made Ben Adhem bold', which figure of speech is used?
options: Simile, because peace is compared using like
Personification, because peace is shown as acting upon him
Imagery, because it appeals only to hearing
Metaphor, because peace is called a book of gold
mcqs.why: Peace is personified because it is given the human-like power of acting upon Abou and making him bold, as the figures-of-speech answer explains.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The girl said, "It gives me great pleasure to be here this evening."
options: The girl said that it gave her great pleasure to be there that evening.
The girl said that it gives me great pleasure to be here this evening.
The girl said that it gave me great pleasure to be here that evening.
The girl exclaimed that it gives her great pleasure to be there today.
mcqs.why: In indirect speech gives becomes gave, me becomes her, here becomes there and this evening becomes that evening, as the solved answer shows.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The man said, "I must go as soon as possible."
options: The man said that he must go as soon as possible.
The man said that I had to go as soon as possible.
The man said that he had to go as soon as possible.
The man ordered that he must go as soon as possible.
mcqs.why: Must changes to had to in reported speech and I changes to he, giving he had to go as soon as possible, exactly as the lesson converts it.

mcqs.q: Why does the tense not change in: The teacher says, "If you work hard, you will pass"?
options: Because the sentence states a universal truth about the earth
Because the reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense
Because the sentence is an exclamation of joy
Because the sentence contains a question word
mcqs.why: The lesson notes that when the reporting verb says is in the present tense, the tense of the reported speech does not change in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I have won."
options: He said that he has won.
He said that I have won.
He said that he had won.
He suggested that they should wait.
mcqs.why: Present perfect have won changes to past perfect had won and I changes to he, so the indirect form is he said that he had won.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: "Which way did she go?" asked the young man.
options: The young man asked which way she had gone.
The young man asked which way did she go.
The young man said which way she goes.
The young man exclaimed which way she had gone.
mcqs.why: A question in indirect speech keeps the question word, uses statement order and backshifts the tense, giving asked which way she had gone.

mcqs.q: Change into direct speech: She told her mother that she was going to the market.
options: She said to her mother, "She was going to the market."
She said to her mother, "I am going to the market."
She said to her mother, "I was going to the market."
She told her mother, "You are going to the market."
mcqs.why: In direct speech the speaker uses I and the present continuous am going, with her exact words placed inside quotation marks as in the solved answer.

mcqs.q: Change into direct speech: The teacher said the earth moves around the sun.
options: The teacher said, "The earth moved around the sun."
The teacher said, "The earth moves around the sun."
The teacher said, "The earth will move around the sun."
The teacher said, "The earth is moving around the sun yesterday."
mcqs.why: A universal truth remains in the present tense in both direct and indirect speech, so the direct form keeps the earth moves around the sun.

mcqs.q: Which sentence has quotation marks placed correctly?
options: She's been known to sing beautifully, commented Ali.
"She's been known to sing beautifully," commented Ali.
She's been "known to sing beautifully," commented Ali.
"She's been known to sing beautifully, commented Ali."
mcqs.why: The whole spoken sentence is direct speech and belongs inside quotation marks, with the comma inside the closing mark before commented Ali.

mcqs.q: How should 'When Irum was twenty nine years old' be rewritten, and what rule applies?
options: Twenty-nine, rule: compound number
Twenty - nine, rule: dividing syllables
Twenty nine needs no hyphen at all
Twenty-nine, rule: parentheses for extra information
mcqs.why: Twenty-nine is a compound number, and compound numbers are joined with a hyphen, as the revision exercise on hyphens explains.

mcqs.q: Which rewrite correctly uses an ellipsis? Original: 'The children played in the playground on all the equipment including the swings, the slide, the monkey bars, and the merry-go-round.'
options: The children played ... in the playground on all the equipment
The children played in the playground on all the equipment including the swings ...
... The children played in the playground on all the equipment
The children played in the playground ... on all the equipment including
mcqs.why: The ellipsis at the end omits the remaining list of equipment after the swings, which is exactly how the revision exercise shortens the sentence.

mcqs.q: Which sentence places parentheses correctly?
options: Belize formerly (British Honduras) is in Central America.
(Belize) formerly British Honduras is in Central America.
Belize (formerly British Honduras) is in Central America.
Belize formerly British Honduras is (in Central America).
mcqs.why: Formerly British Honduras is extra explanatory information about Belize, so it is enclosed in parentheses immediately after the name Belize.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: Manahil said, "I am very busy now."
options: Manahil said that she was very busy then.
Manahil said that I am very busy now.
Manahil said that she is very busy now.
Manahil urged that she was very busy then.
mcqs.why: Am changes to was and now changes to then in reported speech, giving Manahil said that she was very busy then, as the revision exercise shows.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: Q1. Write a short poem on a theme similar to the one in 'Abou Ben Adhem'.
    Ans: Love Thy Neighbour A poor man knocked at midnight's door, With empty hands and feet so sore; I shared my bread, I shared my light, And warmed his heart that cold, dark night. I sought no gold, I sought no fame, No list of heaven bore my name; Yet love that serves both great and small Is dearest to the Lord of all.
  • Q: Q2. Write the summary of the poem 'Abou Ben Adhem'.
    Ans: One night Abou Ben Adhem awoke from a deep, peaceful sleep and saw an angel in the moonlight of his room, writing in a book of gold. Made bold by peace, he asked what the angel was writing. The angel replied that it was writing the names of those who love the Lord. Abou asked if his name was among them, and the angel said it was not. Still cheerful and humble, Abou requested the angel to write his name as one who loves his fellow men. The angel wrote and vanished. The next night the angel returned with a great wakening light and showed the names of those whom love of God had blessed — and Abou Ben Adhem's name led all the rest.
  • Q: Q3. Write an essay of about 100 words on 'Haqooq-ul-Ebad'.
    Ans: Haqooq-ul-Ebad means the rights of Allah's servants, that is, our duties towards other human beings. Islam teaches that worship alone is not enough; a true believer must also fulfil the rights of people. These rights include helping the poor and the needy, feeding the hungry, caring for orphans and the sick, speaking kindly, respecting parents, teachers and neighbours, and never harming anyone by hand or tongue. The poem 'Abou Ben Adhem' gives the same lesson: the man who loved his fellow men was placed at the top of the list of those blessed by God. So, to win Allah's pleasure, we must love, serve and protect the rights of humanity.
  • Q: Q4. Paraphrase the first and third stanzas of the poem 'Abou Ben Adhem'.
    Ans: Paraphrase of the first stanza (lines 1–5): Abou Ben Adhem — and the poet prays that the number of good people like him may increase — woke up one night from a deep and peaceful sleep. In his room, filled with moonlight, he saw an angel writing in a golden book. The angel's presence made the room look rich and beautiful, like a lily in full bloom. Paraphrase of the third stanza (lines 11–14): Abou asked the angel, 'Is my name in the list?' The angel replied, 'No, it is not.' Hearing this, Abou did not lose heart; he spoke in a lower, humbler voice but remained cheerful, and requested the angel, 'Then please write my name as one of those who love their fellow human beings.'

mcqs.q: In the model poem 'Love Thy Neighbour', what did the speaker do for the poor man?
options: He gave him gold and fame
He shared his bread and his light and warmed his heart
He wrote his name in a book of gold
He asked an angel to help him
mcqs.why: The speaker shared his bread and shared his light and warmed the poor man's heart on the cold, dark night, seeking neither gold nor fame.

mcqs.q: What lesson does the last part of 'Love Thy Neighbour' state?
options: Love that serves both great and small is dearest to the Lord of all
Only those in heaven's list are blessed
A poor man should never knock at midnight
Fame is dearest to the Lord of all
mcqs.why: The poem ends by stating that love which serves both great and small is dearest to the Lord of all, the same theme as Abou Ben Adhem.

mcqs.q: In the summary, what was the angel writing in the book of gold?
options: The names of those who love their fellow men
The names of those who love the Lord
The names of the wealthiest people
The names of all poets and writers
mcqs.why: The angel replied that it was writing the names of those who love the Lord, and Abou then asked to be written as one who loves his fellow men.

mcqs.q: In the summary, what happened on the next night?
options: The angel refused to return to the room
Abou's name had disappeared from every list
The angel returned with a great wakening light and Abou's name led all the rest
The angel brought a second book of gold
mcqs.why: The next night the angel returned with a great wakening light and showed that Abou Ben Adhem's name led all the rest among those blessed by God's love.

mcqs.q: What does Haqooq-ul-Ebad mean, according to the essay?
options: The rights of Allah Himself alone
The rights of Allah's servants, our duties towards other human beings
The rules for writing poetry
The list of names in the book of gold
mcqs.why: Haqooq-ul-Ebad means the rights of Allah's servants, that is, our duties towards other human beings, and worship alone is not enough without fulfilling them.

mcqs.q: Which duty is included in Haqooq-ul-Ebad in the essay?
options: Harming others by hand or tongue
Ignoring orphans and the sick
Helping the poor and needy and caring for orphans and the sick
Speaking unkindly to neighbours
mcqs.why: The essay lists helping the poor and needy, feeding the hungry and caring for orphans and the sick among the rights of people a believer must fulfil.

mcqs.q: How does the essay connect 'Abou Ben Adhem' with Haqooq-ul-Ebad?
options: The poem shows the man who loved his fellow men placed at the top of the list of those blessed by God
The poem teaches that worship alone is always enough
The poem is about the rights of angels only
The poem never mentions love of fellow men
mcqs.why: The essay gives the poem as the same lesson: the man who loved his fellow men was placed at the top of the list of those blessed by God.

mcqs.q: In the paraphrase of the first stanza, why did the room look rich and beautiful?
options: Because it was full of lilies grown in a garden
Because the angel's presence made it look rich and beautiful, like a lily in full bloom
Because Abou had decorated it with gold
Because the moon had set and lamps were lit
mcqs.why: The paraphrase explains the angel's presence in the moonlit room made it look rich and beautiful, like a lily in full bloom, as the angel wrote in a golden book.

mcqs.q: In the paraphrase of the third stanza, how did Abou react when told his name was not in the list?
options: He lost heart and spoke in anger
He did not lose heart; he spoke in a lower, humbler voice but remained cheerful
He asked the angel to leave the room
He demanded that his name be placed on top
mcqs.why: Abou did not lose heart; he spoke more low, in a humbler voice, yet remained cheerful and asked to be written as one who loves his fellow human beings.

mcqs.q: What request does Abou make in the paraphrased third stanza?
options: Write my name as one of those who love gold
Write my name as one of those who love their fellow human beings
Show me the names of the whole tribe
Bring the book again the next night
mcqs.why: Abou requests the angel to write his name as one of those who love their fellow human beings, which is the request that later places his name at the top.

lessons.notes_html:
Listening and Speaking

  • Q: Listening and Speaking — Make groups to share the idea on 'Humanism'.
    Ans: This is an oral classroom activity (group discussion) with no written answer.
